publicQuestions.question:
Can Council please confirm the following:

Is a hydraulic impact assessment required or is a catchment analysis and overland flow check sufficient?

Considering the carpark layout and location is quite developed, are any front end traffic counts or reports required?

Outside of the existing RAP and design in accordance with the RAP what other contaminated land assessments are required?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hydraulic / flooding assessment: Council has provided flood mapping information within the Tender Appendix. The flooding and overland flow assessment is to assess existing flooding and drainage constraints affecting the site and demonstrate that the proposed development will maintain or improve the existing flood and overland flow behaviour of the site and surrounding land. Council does not currently have a hydraulic flood model available. Tenderers are to determine the level of assessment necessary to support the design and demonstrate that the proposed works will not adversely impact flood behaviour, flood storage, overland flow paths, stormwater drainage performance or adjoining properties. Where the Consultant considers additional hydraulic analysis or flood modelling necessary to support these outcomes, this should be included within their methodology and proposal.

Traffic investigations: Tenderers are to engage a suitably qualified traffic consultant and allow for all traffic investigations, surveys and reporting necessary to support the design and approvals process. Council has not provided traffic count data, turning movement counts, parking demand assessments or patronage forecasts as part of the Tender Appendix. The scope and extent of any surveys are to be determined by the traffic consultant, particularly to support the Foreshore Road slip lane design, TfNSW approvals, site access arrangements and assessment of anticipated car park demand and utilisation.

Contaminated land assessments: Tenderers are to review and rely on the existing PSI, DSI and RAP documentation provided. The Environmental Consultant's role is intended to be limited to interpretation of the existing investigations and incorporation of the identified contamination, asbestos and remediation constraints into the design. No revision of the RAP, validation reporting, post-remediation validation or additional contamination assessment is currently required. However, where supplementary contamination investigations are identified as necessary to address specific data gaps and support completion of a constructable design, they are to be included within the Consultant's scope in accordance with the tender requirements.

publicQuestions.question: Good morning, the Schedule of Prices - Lump sum break-up lists the Civil Engineer as the Lead Consultant, however the A1. Scope of Works lists the Civil Engineer as a subconsultant. Can you please confirm who Council prefer as the lead Consultant?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council's preference is for the Civil Engineer to act as the Lead Consultant.

This is fundamentally a civil engineering project, with key project drivers including the car park, Foreshore Road slip lane/deceleration lane works, stormwater drainage, pavement design, utility coordination and associated TfNSW approvals.

The reference in Appendix A1 to various disciplines reflects Council's expectation that Tenderers assemble an appropriately qualified multidisciplinary team. Whilst other lead disciplines may submit a proposal, Tenderers should recognise that both civil engineering and landscape architecture are critical to the successful delivery of the project.

Accordingly, Council expects the Lead Consultant to demonstrate strong capability in managing and coordinating the civil engineering aspects of the project together with the landscape design, approval and stakeholder coordination requirements. The Consultant team should include all necessary specialist subconsultants to deliver the full scope of services.

2. How access to the site is intended to be managed for the additional site investigations, including any required asbestos controls, and whether tenderers are required to include the associated measures within their fees.
publicQuestions.answer:

publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council has made available all survey information currently included within the Tender Appendix. Any available survey information has been provided in the format available to Council. Tenderers should base their submissions on the information provided and satisfy themselves as to its suitability for the proposed Services.

Where additional feature and level survey, cadastral survey, utility investigation, easement verification or other survey information is required to support the design, approvals and preparation of construction documentation, such services are to be included within the Consultant's scope and fee proposal.

2. Council has not selected a preferred remediation strategy at this time. Tenderers are to review the existing PSI, DSI and RAP documentation and incorporate the identified contamination and remediation constraints into the design. Council encourages tenderers to consider practical and cost-effective remediation outcomes that may be integrated with the proposed car park construction where appropriate and consistent with the RAP.

No additional remediation feasibility documentation is available beyond the information included in the Tender Appendix.

3. Council will not disclose the budget allocated for design and documentation services.

4. An indicative construction budget of approximately $2 million has been provided for tendering purposes only. The final project budget will be refined as the design develops and cost planning progresses.

5. Council does not have a prescribed software platform for hydrologic or hydraulic assessment. Tenderers without certification may submit a conforming tender provided they can demonstrate an equivalent documented Work Health and Safety Management System appropriate for the services being delivered. Tenderers should provide details of their WHS policies, procedures, risk management processes, training arrangements and system implementation measures for Council's assessment.

title: Upgrade to Planet Creek Stock Route Facilities
description:
The Planet Creek Stock Route Reserve is an important infrastructure asset that provides a designated area for the movements, agistment and watering of travelling livestock within the region. The reserve supports Council’s Rural Lands unit by maintaining access to essential stock route networks and provides facilities that assist livestock producers, transport operators and authorised users travelling through the area.

The existing facilities at Planet Creek have reached an age where upgrades and renewal works are required to ensure the reserve remains functional and compliant with current operational and animal welfare standards. These upgrades have been approved in consultation with the Stock Route Management Network, with Queensland Government grant funding secured to support the delivery of the works.

The Plant Creek reserve is the most heavily agisted reserve within the Central Highlands Region. This primary reserve is located along the Blackwater-Rolleston Road.

The successful supplier will be responsible for completing the below specified upgrades in accordance with Council’s standards, legislation, WHS requirements and environmental obligations.

Works must be completed to the Stock Route Facility Minimum Standards, materials should be sourced from a reputable supplier, works must be undertaken in a neat and professional manner.

Troughs:

•	Removal of existing trough - 1

•	Installation of new troughs - 4 x 4.5m. Must have sufficient fall to the drain end/s to allow for complete emptying of water. To be aligned in continuous long row

•	Adequate float valves for correct flow rate, with float cover

•	 Trough guards across full lengths

•	Concrete slabs to be poured:

o	Minimum 100mm thick and reinforced

o	Extend at least 900mm either side of trough, and total width at least 2.5m wide

o	Extend 2.4m at slab ends where trough drains

Trough Piping:

•	If single feed line to distribute (preferred) - minimum 100mm diameter piping required

•	If multiple feed lines from tank to troughs – minimum 75mm diameter piping required

•	Polythene or PVC pipeline is to be buried with a minimum clear cover of 200mm, except for vehicle crossing where the cover must be 300mm

•	Pipes and fittings for troughing from current cement tank

Testing of bores:

•	Testing to be performed on current bore to establish if the reserve maintains the Windmill or installs a bore pump. Testing to establish the following:

o	Determine whether the aquafer in the well is fast or slow filling

o	Determine the type of pump that will be submersed into the aquafer

o	Depth of the bore

Solar Panels:

•	Theft resistant hardware/construction

•	Either:

o	Mounted on a locked cage fasted to a concrete footing with hardware that cannot be removed from outside the cage, or

o	Surrounded by a security fence, comprising of the following as a minimum:

?	Fence height at least 1650mm

?	Chain mesh fencing min height 1500mm

?	Bottom of chain mesh fencing max 50mm above ground-level

?	Min 1 barbed wire 100-150mm above the top of chain mesh attached to every post or picket

?	A gate of sufficient width to allow access to service the pump/panels, secured with a lock and non-removable hinges

?	Gate posts and stays to be cemented a min of 900mm in ground, with a min diameter of 250mm

?	Gate posts and corner posts must be supported by an angle brace stay or a top rail extending around the entire enclosure.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

The Planet Creek Stock Route Reserve is an important infrastructure asset that provides a designated area for the movements, agistment and watering of travelling livestock within the region. The reserve supports Council’s Rural Lands unit by maintaining access to essential stock route networks and provides facilities that assist livestock producers, transport operators and authorised users travelling through the area.

The existing facilities at Planet Creek have reached an age where upgrades and renewal works are required to ensure the reserve remains functional and compliant with current operational and animal welfare standards. These upgrades have been approved in consultation with the Stock Route Management Network, with Queensland Government grant funding secured to support the delivery of the works.

The Plant Creek reserve is the most heavily agisted reserve within the Central Highlands Region. This primary reserve is located along the Blackwater-Rolleston Road.

The successful supplier will be responsible for completing the below specified upgrades in accordance with Council’s standards, legislation, WHS requirements and environmental obligations.

Works must be completed to the Stock Route Facility Minimum Standards, materials should be sourced from a reputable supplier, works must be undertaken in a neat and professional manner.

Troughs:

•	Removal of existing trough - 1

•	Installation of new troughs - 4 x 4.5m. Must have sufficient fall to the drain end/s to allow for complete emptying of water. To be aligned in continuous long row

•	Adequate float valves for correct flow rate, with float cover

•	 Trough guards across full lengths

•	Concrete slabs to be poured:

o	Minimum 100mm thick and reinforced

o	Extend at least 900mm either side of trough, and total width at least 2.5m wide

o	Extend 2.4m at slab ends where trough drains

Trough Piping:

•	If single feed line to distribute (preferred) - minimum 100mm diameter piping required

•	If multiple feed lines from tank to troughs – minimum 75mm diameter piping required

•	Polythene or PVC pipeline is to be buried with a minimum clear cover of 200mm, except for vehicle crossing where the cover must be 300mm

•	Pipes and fittings for troughing from current cement tank

Testing of bores:

•	Testing to be performed on current bore to establish if the reserve maintains the Windmill or installs a bore pump. Testing to establish the following:

o	Determine whether the aquafer in the well is fast or slow filling

o	Determine the type of pump that will be submersed into the aquafer

o	Depth of the bore

Solar Panels:

•	Theft resistant hardware/construction

•	Either:

o	Mounted on a locked cage fasted to a concrete footing with hardware that cannot be removed from outside the cage, or

o	Surrounded by a security fence, comprising of the following as a minimum:

?	Fence height at least 1650mm

?	Chain mesh fencing min height 1500mm

?	Bottom of chain mesh fencing max 50mm above ground-level

?	Min 1 barbed wire 100-150mm above the top of chain mesh attached to every post or picket

?	A gate of sufficient width to allow access to service the pump/panels, secured with a lock and non-removable hinges

?	Gate posts and stays to be cemented a min of 900mm in ground, with a min diameter of 250mm

?	Gate posts and corner posts must be supported by an angle brace stay or a top rail extending around the entire enclosure.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Council tender team,

Conditions of Tendering clause 14 provides that a tenderer may hold an AS/NZS ISO 9001-certified Quality Management System or demonstrate that equivalent QMS systems are in place.

However, Schedule A clause 1.2.7 states that all services, including services performed by subconsultants, must be carried out under a management system certified to AS/NZS ISO 9001:2015 or the current equivalent. The Tender Schedule also states that the Quality Management System schedule is to be included where the estimated fee exceeds $250,000, although this Panel has no defined engagement value.

Please confirm:

whether a documented and internally audited, but non-third-party-certified, equivalent Quality Management System will satisfy the requirements for appointment to the Panel; and

whether the Quality Management System schedule and internal audit log must be submitted with this Panel tender regardless of the value of future individual engagements.

Thanks

Harryan Engineering Consulting
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms the following in relation to the Quality Management System requirements:

Equivalent Quality Management System

For the purposes of appointment to the Panel, Council will accept a documented and implemented Quality Management System that is equivalent to AS/NZS ISO 9001:2015, including where the system is internally audited but has not been subject to third-party certification.

Tenderers should be able to demonstrate that the system is appropriate to the nature and scale of the services being provided and is effectively implemented within their organisation.

Where subconsultants are engaged, the tenderer remains responsible for ensuring that the services provided by subconsultants are undertaken in accordance with the applicable quality management requirements.

Quality Management System Schedule

The Quality Management System Schedule is not required to be submitted as part of the Panel tender solely on the basis that the Panel does not have a defined engagement value.

The requirement for the Quality Management System Schedule and supporting documentation, including evidence of internal audits where applicable, will apply to individual engagements where the estimated fee exceeds $250,000, in accordance with the Tender Schedule.

For the avoidance of doubt, appointment to the Panel does not guarantee any particular volume or value of work, and the applicable quality management requirements will be considered at the individual engagement stage based on the nature, complexity and value of the services required.

Council will clarify the relevant provisions in the tender documentation to ensure consistency between the Conditions of Tendering, Schedule A and the Tender Schedule.

publicQuestions.question:

Hazardous Materials

The Hazardous Materials Report, Asbestos Register and all associated tender documentation have been provided for tendering purposes and shall be reviewed by tenderers in full. Tenderers are required to satisfy themselves as to the nature and extent of hazardous materials and make adequate allowance within their tender pricing for the management, removal, transport, disposal, monitoring, clearance and compliance requirements associated with the identified and presumed hazardous materials.

Where materials are identified as "assumed", "presumed" or "potentially containing" hazardous substances within the provided documentation, these items are to be treated as hazardous materials for the purposes of tender pricing and methodology development. No variation will be considered for the removal of materials identified within the tender documentation as assumed, presumed or potentially containing hazardous materials.

Scaffolding / Hoarding

Tenderers should allow for scaffolding and hoarding arrangements generally in accordance with the Traffic Management Plan provided. The TMP allows for temporary occupation and closure of the Coward Street footpath frontage, with pedestrians diverted via a protected pathway within the parking lane. Any occupation of public land, footpath closures, scaffolding, hoarding or traffic control measures required for the Works shall be subject to obtaining all necessary approvals from the relevant authorities and shall be included within the Contractor's tendered price.

Could Council please confirm that Item 3.2 only requires make-good/reinstatement of damage or temporary modifications resulting from the Works, and does not include general resurfacing, realignment, line marking or reconstruction of the existing carpark?

3. Palisade Fencing and Gates – Tender Pricing Basis

Appendix A advises that the fencing and gate layout is indicative only, with the final extent and configuration to be confirmed with Council’s Project Manager prior to installation.

approximate total lineal metres of new palisade fencing;

number and approximate width of vehicle gates;

number and approximate width of pedestrian gates; and

4. Access to Mascot Fire Station for Temporary Propping and Scaffolding

Tenderers are to allow for the existing car park to be returned to its pre-construction condition upon completion of the Works.

4. Council has liaised with Mascot Fire Station and confirms that access will be made available for the installation, inspection, maintenance and removal of the temporary propping and scaffolding systems associated with the Works.

Tenderers should allow for their proposed methodology to minimise impacts to the ongoing operation of the Fire Station and maintain safe access for emergency services at all times.

Working hours are to be in accordance with the approved Conditions of Consent and any other relevant statutory requirements.

The duration of any temporary occupation cannot be confirmed at this stage and will be dependent on the successful contractor's proposed methodology and construction program. Tenderers should seek to minimise the duration and extent of occupation wherever practicable.

The successful contractor will be required to maintain clear, timely and proactive communication with Council and Fire Station representatives regarding access requirements, staging, inspections and any activities that may affect Fire Station operations. Appropriate notice shall be provided in advance of works requiring access to operational areas.

At this stage, Council is not aware of any areas that cannot be temporarily occupied; however, access arrangements and operational constraints will need to be coordinated with Fire Station personnel throughout the works to ensure emergency response capabilities are maintained at all times.

5. Council confirms that there are no specific building elements, materials or heritage items required to be salvaged, retained or handed over to Council as part of these Works.

Tenderers may therefore manage demolition materials in accordance with the requirements of the tender documentation, applicable legislation, and the approved waste management and recycling requirements.

Should any item of potential heritage significance be identified during the Works that was not previously documented, the Contractor shall notify Council for further direction prior to its removal or disposal.

Hi,

Could Council please confirm which stormwater pipe requires a CCTV condition survey? Could you also please confirm whether this comprises both a pre- and post-demolition CCTV survey?

We note that the existing site survey and DBYD plans do not indicate the presence of any stormwater pipes traversing the site.

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has not identified any stormwater pipelines within the project site requiring CCTV condition surveys based on the currently available information. Tenderers are responsible for reviewing the information provided and undertaking any investigations necessary to satisfy themselves of existing site conditions.

If stormwater assets are identified during the contractor's investigations that may be affected by the Works, the contractor shall notify Council for further direction. No specific pre- or post-demolition CCTV survey requirements have been nominated by Council at this stage.

Bayside Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit a quotation for the demolition of the former Botany Administration Building located at 141 Coward Street, Mascot. The project involves the demolition and removal of the existing three-storey building, associated awnings, water tank and ground floor slab, together with site remediation, clearing and regrading works. The scope also includes the design, supply and installation of new perimeter palisade fencing and gates, and the placement of a crushed aggregate capping layer.

The site is generally level and is located between two locally listed heritage items, Coronation Hall and the Mascot Fire Station, requiring careful management of demolition activities and environmental controls. Existing footings and foundations are to remain in situ, and no works are required within the existing hardstand car parking area.

A mandatory site inspection will be held on site Monday 31 August 2026, at 11.00am. Please note that due to mould and other potential hazardous materials that the use of appropriate PPE is recommended during the site inspection.

The meeting point for the site inspection is at the front entrance of the building on Coward St.

The RFT Closing date / time is Tuesday 22 September 2026, at 10.00am.

Prices submitted as part of this tender shall remain valid and open for acceptance by the Principal until December 2026.

title: RFT000141- Gympie Regional Council 2026/ 27 In-situ Stabilising Works
description:
Tenders are invited from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to establish schedule rates and pricing for the delivery of in-situ pavement stabilisation works within the Gympie Regional Council local government area. The works form part of the Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) 2026/27 reseal preparation program and are required to improve pavement condition, structural performance, and long-term asset durability prior to the application of reseal treatments.

The scope of work encompasses pavement stabilisation activities on two key transport routes located on the Wide Bay Highway and Gympie Woolooga Road.

The successful contractor will be required to undertake the stabilisation works in accordance with the project specifications, relevant TMR standards, and all applicable legislative and safety requirements. Works are intended to provide a sound and uniform pavement platform suitable for the subsequent resealing operations scheduled under the 2026/27 program.

title: Pipe Clay Lagoon and Cremorne Beach Coastal Adaptation Plan
description:
The City of Clarence seeks suitably qualified consultants to prepare a Coastal Adaptation Plan (CAP) for the Cremorne coastal area, encompassing Cremorne Beach and the Cremorne foreshore of Pipe Clay Lagoon.

The project will provide a contemporary framework for managing existing and future coastal hazard risks while recognising and protecting the area's environmental, social, cultural, recreational and economic values.

The Coastal Adaptation Plan must be prepared in accordance with Council's adopted Coastal Hazards Policy and contemporary best practice coastal adaptation planning principles. The consultant will be required to utilise existing technical assessments and planning work completed for Pipe Clay Lagoon and undertake a contemporary coastal hazard assessment for Cremorne Beach to establish a consistent evidence base across the study area.

The final output will be a single integrated Coastal Adaptation Plan that addresses the Cremorne coastal area, comprising the Cremorne section of Pipe Clay Lagoon and Cremorne Beach, as an interconnected coastal system.

CLOSE OF QUOTATIONS

3pm, Wednesday 30 September 2026

LATE QUOTATIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Gwydir Shire is in the centre of the ‘Fossickers Way’, a route which offers the traveller a relaxing alternative to the New England or Newell Highways. The Shire encompasses a diverse landscape that is both picturesque and productive and is approximately 560 km north of Sydney, 160 km north of Tamworth along the Fossickers Way and 85 km north-west of Inverell. The shire is 9,122 square kilometres in size and is situated north of Tamworth Regional Council and continues almost to the Queensland border.

The southern boundary of the shire is the Nandewar Range where the Gwydir and Namoi Valleys meet. The Horton Valley and Cobbadah District are home to some Australia’s most highly regarded beef cattle studs. These enterprising farmers use the latest artificial breeding and agronomic technology to produce beef of exceptional quality. Meat Sheep and merinos that grow high quality wool are also grazed in this area.

The Gwydir River enters the Gwydir Shire where it spills from the Copeton Dam and meanders in a westerly direction through the towns of Bingara and Gravesend. The Gwydir valley is well know for irrigated and dry land cropping as well as livestock production. In addition to the traditional crops of wheat, barley, oats and sorghum, there are olive groves, pecan nut plantations and freshwater fish farms in the Gravesend district.

Heading northwest from the timbered surrounds of the town of Warialda and the close-knit community of Coolatai, the countryside opens into an undulating vista of basalt farmland. This part of the Shire which include the villages of Crooble, Croppa Creek and North Star, is known as the ‘Golden Triangle’. Farmers using advanced farming techniques, such as minimum tillage and satellite guidance systems, produce a variety of high yielding crops such as wheat, barley sorghum, maize, chick peas, canola and cotton to name just a few. This area also has several cattle feed lots which supply grain fed beef to the Australian domestic market and export markets throughout the world.

Both Warialda and Bingara have Hospitals, Aged Care Hostels, Medical Centres, Caravan Parks, Swimming Pools, Pre-schools, Libraries, Tourist Information Centres, and a Mobile Pre-school based at North Star. Warialda is the centre for the Council’s Technical Services functions. Bingara is the centre for the Administrative functions. The two centres are being linked through the use of sophisticated communications equipment to ensure that the amalgamations primary objective is achieved which is to save the existing employment numbers within each of the main urban centres of Warialda and Bingara.
Where is the Gwydir Shire?

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there, could you please clarify the questions below:

RFI-01 - Appendix A lists inspection frequencies in addition to cleaning frequencies. Please confirm whether inspections are standalone visits, may be completed during scheduled cleans, and whether their time is included in the 30.75-hour estimate. eg. GSM Admin Bld - if the clean is to be completed twice per day x 4 times per week "0.5hrs per clean however 2 totals hrs allocated per week. means each clean would be only 0.25hrs or the total hours would be 4 per week. these goes for the another twice daily sites.

RFI-02 - Please clarify whether the additional 10 hours per week for supplementary cleans is a guaranteed paid allowance, a not-to-exceed contingent instruction, or an estimate to be priced as an hourly call-out rate. Please also confirm approval and invoicing protocol. Also the BBQ should be priced separetly or would be allocated in the designated hours.

RFI-03 - Please provide or confirm the Council-approved reporting platform, log-sheet template, photo-retention/privacy requirements, and Council CRM process for defects. Or would the contractor use their own internal rerting platform.?

RFI-04 - Please confirm the required sanitary-bin provider/service frequency, whether bins are to be supplied by the contractor, and all waste-disposal requirements/cost inclusions.

RFI-05 - Please clarify Council’s approved chemicals and consumables specifications/brands, dispenser formats and expected stockholding levels, or confirm whether the contractor is to submit a proposed list for approval.

RFI-06 - Please confirm service windows, key/access arrangements, alarms, water/power availability, parking, and any event/holiday uplift requirements for each facility.

RFI-07 - Please define “deep cleaning as required”, identify expected triggers/frequency, and confirm whether it is included in routine price, supplementary hours, or a separately instructed rate. Eg. Graffiti removal would be under deep cleaning or adhoc?

RFI-08 - Please confirm whether Council expects one contractor to cover all facilities or may award multiple contracts, and state the anticipated commencement date/mobilisation period.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi, thankyou for your questions. Please see answers below.

RFI-01: Inspections would be required at least daily at the sites noted. These may be conducted stand-alone or as part of a scheduled clean. Contractor will be required to return to site to clean outside of scheduled cleans if requested due to high usage or incident or verified community complaint. Negotiation over inspections to account for travel time and to ensure efficiencies can take place at contracting stage.

RFI-02: Supplementary cleans have been included as a contingency to be used as required. BBQ cleaning included in site designated hours. Invoices to be submitted with Monthly Performance Report by 5th business day of each calendar month.

RFI-03: Council uses the Civica Authority and Reflect platforms for CRMs and task verification. Access details to these platforms along with log sheet templates, etc will be provided to successful contractor.

RFI-04: Sanitary bin provision and servicing to be determined/subject to negotiation. Can be included in quote if you wish.

RFI-05: Contractor to supply a proposed list of chemicals for approval.

RFI-06: Service windows would generally be 6am-5pm daily. All sites have parking, water and power. Event/holiday/high-demand requirements subject to negotiation with successful contractor.

RFI-07: Deep cleaning may be required periodically. This can be negotiated with contractor. Indicative rates may be provided. Graffiti and maintenance issues are reporting only – see 3.3 in the RFQ.

RFI-08: Anticipated commencement date is 4Q 2026, subject to successful contracting. Multiple contracting may be considered, although preference is for a single contractor.

title: Landfill Gas Capture and Flaring System
description:
Livingstone Shire Council is seeking proposals from suitably qualified and experienced organisations to provide a commercial solution for the financing, design, approval, construction, commissioning, operation and maintenance of a Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Flaring System at the Yeppoon Landfill. The proposed solution must safely capture and control landfill gas, provide reliable flaring infrastructure, meet applicable environmental and regulatory requirements, and accommodate potential future landfill gas-to-energy or cogeneration opportunities.

Council is seeking a commercial partnership model under which the successful Respondent will be responsible for the delivery and ongoing operation of the system, including all labour, plant, equipment, approvals, monitoring, reporting, maintenance and associated services necessary to achieve the required performance outcomes. Respondents may also propose innovative approaches that improve environmental, operational or commercial outcomes for Council.

Location of Services

 The works and services will be undertaken at Yeppoon Landfill, Livingstone Shire, Queensland. Site inspections will be available during the procurement process. While some design, engineering, monitoring and reporting activities may be undertaken remotely, the successful Respondent must be capable of delivering and supporting on-site operations, maintenance and incident response services throughout the contract term.

Expected Timing

Council's anticipated procurement timetable is:

RFP issued: 27 August 2026

Optional site inspection: 16 September 2026

Questions close: 28 September 2026

RFP closes: 5 October 2026

Key Outcomes Sought

- Capture and control landfill gas in accordance with environmental, safety and regulatory requirements.

- Reliably flare landfill gas to achieve methane destruction and odour control.

- Establish infrastructure capable of supporting future landfill gas-to-energy, cogeneration or other beneficial gas utilisation opportunities.

- Deliver measurable and ongoing commercial returns to Council through a revenue-sharing arrangement.

- Maintain safe, compliant and continuous operation of the landfill gas capture and flaring system throughout the contract term

This Request for Proposal seeks responses from organisations with demonstrated experience in landfill gas capture, landfill gas flaring, landfill gas-to-energy projects and related environmental infrastructure services. Council welcomes innovative and commercially sustainable solutions that support environmental compliance, risk management and long-term value for the community.

title: Rosny Tennis Courts - Retaining Wall Repair and Fencing
description:
Council invites Tenders to undertake works as specified in these Tender Documents for the following works at the Rosny Tennis Club, 18 Bastick Street, Rosny

Rosny Tennis Club, Retaining Wall repairs

-	Supply of all materials and consumables for retaining wall repairs

-	Supply of portable toilet and amenities for the duration of all works

-	Retaining wall repairs as per design drawings

-	Reinstating the Bessa brick wall and returfing

-	Removal and appropriate disposal of all waste materials, including spoil

Rosny Tennis Club, Courts 1&2 Fencing upgrade

-	Supply of all materials and consumables for fencing and footings

-	Remove of the existing Courts 1&2 fencing

-	Install footings as per the JMG footing plan

-	Install court drainage and connect to existing system

-	Install new black chain link fencing as per AS1725.2

-	Removal and appropriate disposal of all waste materials

All works shall comply with Safe Work Australia Code of Practice – Excavation work, AS1725.2 Tennis Court Fencing- Commercial, referenced standards and best practice.

Full details are provided in Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 of the specimen copy of the Contract appearing in Part 4 of this Invitation. Tenderers are to contact Council’s nominated contact officer named on the cover page if additional information is required to submit the Tender.

The Rosny Tennis Club courts were constructed over 30 years ago and the retaining wall along the western side of the courts is cracked and bowed in some areas. The retaining wall requires repairs to restore site safety ahead of a future site upgrade. The perimeter fencing around Courts 1 and 2 is also in poor condition and will be replaced. Council is also progressing a separate tender to resurface Courts 1 and 2. The resurfacing will commence after the retaining wall and perimeter fencing works are complete. All site works must be completed prior to 30 Nov 2026.

PRE-TENDER SITE MEETING

For clarification of the Works, a pre-Tender site meeting is scheduled for 11am on Thursday 17 September on-site. This meeting will convene at the Rosny Tennis Club house at 18 Bastick Street, Rosny. Attendance at this meeting is not mandatory; however, this will be the only opportunity to physically explore the site with the Superintendent in attendance.

Those intending to attend this meeting are requested to inform the contact person nominated on the front cover of this Tender Document prior to the meeting.

CLOSE OF TENDER

3pm, Tuesday 06 October 2026

LATE TENDERS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

The works are intended to provide fully thirty-seven (37) serviced residential lots and one englobo future development parcel, associated public open space, road infrastructure, electrical reticulation, stormwater management infrastructure and landscape works required to support future residential development and community use.

publicQuestions.question:
Following our review of the tender documentation, we would appreciate Council’s clarification of the following matters to ensure that our submission, methodology and fee allowance align with Council’s intended scope.

1.Tender dates - Volume 1 identifies the tender opening date as 2 September 2026 and closing date as 23 September 2026, whereas Volume 4 shows earlier opening and closing dates. Could Council please confirm that the dates stated in Volume 1 and VendorPanel are the current applicable dates?

2. Form of engagement / D&C terminology - Our understanding is that the successful consultant will be engaged under AS 4122-2010 to prepare a Tender Design Package for subsequent procurement of a Design & Construct contractor, rather than being engaged as the D&C contractor. Could Council please confirm?

3. Level of design development - The Scope states that the Tender Design Package is not intended to constitute an IFC design and that the typical designs do not need to be site-specific detailed designs. Could Council confirm that the consultant is required to establish sufficient design intent, typical details, performance requirements and quantities for D&C pricing, with final detailed design and construction certification remaining the responsibility of the future D&C contractor?

4. Survey information - The Scope indicates that detailed survey is not required. Please confirm whether Council will provide any available cadastral, LiDAR, GIS, aerial, rail-corridor or existing survey information, and that the consultant may develop the Tender Design Package using the information provided by Council supplemented by site observations.

5. Culvert assessment and design extent - Could Council please confirm that the consultant is expected to inspect and assess the relevant existing culverts within the approximately 5 km project corridor and nominate an appropriate treatment category such as retain, clean, repair, protect, extend or replace, rather than undertake detailed structural and hydraulic design of every culvert at tender-design stage?

6. Hydraulic assessment - The Scope states that detailed drainage modelling is not required. Could Council confirm whether the culvert and drainage assessment may therefore be qualitative / desktop based, supported by site observations and available catchment information, with detailed hydrologic and hydraulic modelling to be undertaken by the future D&C contractor where required?

7. Bridges and boardwalks - The technical details identify “Proposed Bridges – Nil”, while the wider scope refers to bridges, culverts, boardwalks or other required structures. Could Council please confirm that no new bridge or boardwalk design is presently anticipated and that any significant structure identified during the corridor assessment would first be referred to Council before additional design is undertaken?

8. Environmental documentation - The Scope refers to the approved REF, Biodiversity Assessment Report, Contamination Investigation and SAQP. Could Council please confirm that these documents will be provided to the successful consultant, and advise whether they are available to tenderers prior to tender close?

9. Environmental and heritage specialist services - Please confirm whether the design consultant is expected only to incorporate and respond to the recommendations and constraints contained in the existing environmental, biodiversity, contamination and heritage documentation, or whether Council expects new specialist environmental, ecological, contamination or heritage investigations to be commissioned as part of this consultancy.

10. Bombala Station heritage precinct - The supplied asset information identifies a number of heritage-listed rail assets within or near the Bombala Station precinct. Could Council please confirm whether the trail alignment and works are to avoid physical intervention to these heritage assets wherever practicable, and whether any separate heritage approvals or heritage-impact assessment will be arranged by Council or form part of the consultant’s scope?

11. Removal and storage of rail infrastructure - The Scope requires the consultant to assist in identifying a suitable location for retained rails and sleepers. Could Council please clarify:

whether the proposed storage location must remain within the existing rail lease;

whether Council/TfNSW will provide available candidate areas; and

whether the consultant is required to prepare a formal storage-area design, or only identify and recommend a suitable location.

12. Road crossings - Could Council confirm the intended level of design for road crossings? In particular, are typical concept treatments, signage and traffic-control requirements sufficient for the Tender Design Package, or are traffic counts, detailed traffic engineering, swept-path analysis and/or Road Safety Audits required?

13. Approvals responsibility - Annexure Part A currently identifies approvals to be obtained by the consultant as “TBC”. Could Council please identify any planning, heritage, TfNSW, rail-corridor, environmental, road authority or other approvals that the design consultant is expected to obtain, as distinct from approvals that are only to be identified for the future D&C contractor.

14. Construction programme requirement - The Scope requests that the consultant consider construction methodology, linkages and durations to assist with D&C tender evaluation. Could Council confirm that a high-level indicative construction programme identifying key activities, sequencing, dependencies and indicative durations will satisfy this requirement, rather than a fully resource-loaded contractor construction programme?

15. BOQ accuracy and measurement basis - Given that detailed survey and site-specific detailed design are expressly excluded from the Tender Design Package, could Council confirm that the Bill of Quantities is intended to be an indicative tender BOQ, developed from available corridor information, site observations and typical treatment assumptions, with those assumptions clearly documented?

16. Council review milestones - Could Council please advise whether it has nominated review stages, such as Draft / 80% / Final Tender Design Package, and the anticipated Council review period at each stage?

17. Deliverable formats - Please confirm the required native and issued formats for the final deliverables, including drawings, Design Basis Report, BOQ, performance specification, Safety in Design report, risk register and programme.

18. Bank guarantee / retention - Volume 4 requires the tenderer to indicate whether it can provide a bank guarantee or alternatively agree to retention requirements. Could Council please confirm whether a bank guarantee or retention is actually required for this professional consultancy engagement and, if so, the required amount or percentage and release conditions?

19. Professional Indemnity insurance period - The draft AS 4122 Annexure specifies a $10 million Professional Indemnity limit but the period for which the PI insurance must be maintained appears to remain uncompleted. Could Council please confirm the required post-completion PI insurance maintenance period?

20. Subconsultant approval - AS 4122 requires prior Council approval of subconsultants. Could Council confirm whether nominated specialist subconsultants may be identified in the tender and formally approved following award, particularly where their involvement is dependent on the outcome of the initial corridor assessment?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The correct closing date is 23/09/26.

2. Correct, the tenderer will be engaged to prepare a D&C Tender Package, NOT be engaged as the D&C contractor.

3. Correct, the consultant is required to establish sufficient design intent, typical details, performance requirements and quantities for D&C pricing, with final detailed design and construction certification remaining the responsibility of the future D&C contractor.

4. Council will provide the survey to the successful tenderer. Currently Council are working with TfNSW to gain permission to enter the corridor to undertake the survey.

5. Confirmed

6. This is acceptable. TfNSW may require a Hydrology Assessment as part of the aforementioned survey, but this has yet to be confirmed.

Tenderers may opt to provide a price for provision of a hydrology assessment report as a separate item in their submission for consideration should the hydrology assessment be required, however provision of this price will not affect Council’s assessment of your tender submission.

7. No new bridge or boardwalk design is presently anticipated. Any significant structure identified during the corridor assessment is to be referred to Council before additional design is undertaken.

8. Documents were uploaded to the tender portal.

9. The design consultant is expected to incorporate and respond to the recommendations and constraints contained within the reports which will be uploaded to this tender and ensure any requirements of these reports are met by the tender design package.

10. No works are permitted within the Bombala Station Heritage Precinct. The trail will begin opposite the Visitor Information Centre and continue for 5km. The heritage listed assets were provided for information only.

11. The consultant is to assist with determining the volume/number/quantity of rails and sleepers to be stored and to determine the area required for storage of that volume/number/quantity. Currently no candidate areas are identified as this will be informed by the volume/number/quantity and subsequent area requirement calculation.

The storage location must be within the SMRC LGA.

12. There will be two road crossings: on at the Monaro Hwy (just north of Townsend St) and Sandy Crossing Rd (just beyond the end of Mitchell St). Both of which are 60km/h roads. Road crossings and signage must be specified by the designer to comply with TfNSW requirements for roads of that speed. Traffic counts, detailed traffic engineering, and swept path analysis are not required.

13. No authority approvals are required for the purpose of this of tender, however design of the two aforementioned road crossings must be compliant with TfNSW requirements.

14. Yes, that is satisfactory.

15. An accurate BoQ is required for Council to procure the future D&C contractor. For the purpose of quoting for the preparation of the BoQ, tenderers are to base their tender submission on available corridor information, site observations and typical treatment assumptions. If the survey data provided later by Council differs demonstrably from the tender allowance that will be dealt with as a cost and/or time variation.

16. These review milestones are acceptable. Please allow 4 weeks for Council to review each milestone. Council will endeavour to respond quicker, however if at any point Councillor Approval is required then the 4 weeks will be required.

17. All are to be issued in editable (e.g. MS Word, MS Excel, CAD) and pdf.

18.This is not required.

19. Valid until the end of November 2027.

20. Tenderers are to list their subconsultants and their service in your tender submission. Any queries Council has regarding subconsultants will be discussed prior to engagement. Subconsultant selection only impacts on tender evaluation scores in the context of Council’s local contractor policy.

title: Hinterland Nerang - Expression of Interest
description:
The City of Gold Coast (City), through Invest Gold Coast, is seeking Expressions of Interest from suitably qualified and experienced development partners for the redevelopment of the City's Nerang Administration Precinct.

The project involves the disposal and redevelopment of the former Nerang Administration Centre site and the delivery of the new Hinterland Gateway Community Hub as returnable works under a development partnership arrangement. The redevelopment is expected to transform the precinct into a vibrant mixed-use destination incorporating residential development, community infrastructure, public realm improvements, commercial and employment-generating uses, and supporting infrastructure.

The precinct comprises approximately 7.9 hectares of strategically located land within Nerang and represents a significant urban renewal opportunity. The successful respondent will be responsible for developing a viable master plan, undertaking planning approvals, delivering the proposed development, and designing and constructing the Hinterland Gateway Community Hub in accordance with the City's functional requirements.

Expression of Interest (EOI) submissions must be uploaded via VendorPanel by 4:00 pm AEST on 2 October 2026. title: Meter to Cash Solution and Implementation Services
description:
Energy Queensland Limited (EQL) is seeking proposals for Meter to Cash Solution and Implementation Services via SAP Ariba.

Tenderers who wish to submit a response need to be registered as a Supplier on SAP Ariba. For more information, please see below.

EQL is seeking implementation of a Meter to Cash solution that is cloud-native, highly scalable and compliant with Australian industry standards and regulatory requirements, particularly those set by AEMO and other industry bodies.

Part A: Product

The Meter to Cash Solution must be capable of supporting both Ergon Energy and Energex entities within a single instance, with company-specific business processes, configurations, and workflows where necessary, while also enabling shared processes where appropriate.

Tenders must comply with the following mandatory criteria:

- Australian Energy Market Capability

 • Proposed solution is deployed in production within an Australian DNSP operating in the National Electricity Market (NEM).

- Product Capability: Cloud-hosted solution that provides the following core capabilities:

 • 1.0 Meter Data Management (MDM).

 • 2.0 Network Billing Management (NBM+CIS).

 • 3.0 Market Transactions Management (MDM +CIS).

 • 4.0 Connection Point Management (CIS)

- Local Presence and Support Capability

 • Australian-based support model.

 • Local functional, technical and customer success resources.

- Cyber Security

 • Hosted in Australia.

 • ISO27001 Certified.

 • SOC2 Type 2 Annual Assurance (or equivalent).

Part B: Implementation Services

The Solution will be implemented through a series of controlled delivery Stages and production releases.

• Stage 1: High Level Design – Business Process Gap Analysis, High Level Design and Detailed Implementation Plan (as defined in SOW1)

• Stage 2: Detailed Design and Build (as defined in SOW2)

• Stage 3: Systems Integration Testing (as defined in SOW2)

• Stage 4: UAT & Cutover Readiness (as defined in SOW2)

• Stage 5: Go-Live, Hypercare & Warranty (as defined in SOW2)

Tenders must comply with the following mandatory criteria.

- Product Experience: Tenderer must have proven experience implementing Meter-to-Cash solution(s) that meet Part A mandatory criteria.

- Australian Utility Experience: Tenderer must have implementation experience within the Australian Utilities market.

INSTRUCTIONS:

Tenderers who wish to submit a response need to be registered as a Supplier on SAP Ariba and receive a link to the sourcing event.

To register: Tenderers who are not already registered in Energy Queensland’s realm in SAP Ariba will be required to register by sending an email to the Contact Officer, SPGDigital@energyq.com.au

The email subject should contain the event title ‘Meter to Cash Solution and Implementation Services’ and include the following information:

• Business legal entity name (as displayed in the ABN lookup)

• ABN

• Registered business street address

• Contact name

• Contact phone number

• Contact email address

1.	Registered suppliers: Tenderers who are registered in Energy Queensland’s realm in SAP Ariba, need to request access to the Sourcing Event by sending an email to the Contact Officer, SPGDigital@energyq.com.au

The email subject should contain the event title ‘Meter to Cash Solution and Implementation Services’

2.	Tenderers will receive an email to access the EQL SAP Ariba realm via a link contained in the email notification. ** Please note this link will expire within 24 hours.

3.	Tenderers must accept the Prerequisite Bidder Agreement under the ‘Review and Accept Prerequisites’ tab to ensure all system generated notifications are received. This includes, but is not limited to, content updates and changes to Event Timing.

4.	If the Tenderer elects to submit a response, they must do so using SAP Ariba only. Submissions provided via email or VendorPanel will not be considered for evaluation.

5.	Tenderers are encouraged to read all relevant SAP Ariba documentation located at https://www.energyq.com.au/suppliers .

All queries are to be directed to SPGDigital@energyq.com.au

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Could you please clarify the expected occupancy arrangement under this tender?

Specifically, does the tender require the successful provider to occupy and operate from the centre on a full-time basis for a specified period, or would it be possible to hire and use the facility on an availability/ad-hoc basis as training needs arise?

Our current operating model is to arrange training venues based on the requirements of each client. When we receive a request from a company, organisation or other group, we organise the training at a suitable location based on their needs.

Could you please confirm whether this tender would accommodate this type of flexible, session-by-session facility hire arrangement, or whether the council is seeking a provider to take up ongoing/full-time occupancy of the centre?

Thank you for your clarification.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello,

The purpose of this Request for Proposal is to invite submissions for activation, occupancy and partnership opportunities at the Mid North Coast High Performance Centre.

Council is open to receiving and assessing a range of operating, occupancy and partnership models. This may include proposals involving ongoing occupancy arrangements, periodic use arrangements, shared-use models, partnership approaches, or other innovative activation concepts that support the objectives of the facility.

Respondents are encouraged to propose the model that best aligns with their organisation's operating requirements and demonstrates how their proposed use would contribute to the activation, utilisation and community outcomes of the Centre.

Council has not prescribed a mandatory full-time occupancy requirement and will evaluate submissions based on the criteria outlined in the RFP documentation.

We are preparing a response to T2627.04 Register of Prequalified Suppliers (ROPS) Civil Construction and seek clarification on Schedule N.

Schedule N1 states that "it is a requirement of this project that the successful Respondent be accredited under the Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme (Scheme) established by the Building and Construction Industry (Improving Productivity) Act 2016 (Cth), at the time of entering into the Contract for the Building Work and while the Building Work is being carried out."

Our understanding is that accreditation under the Scheme is required only where the Australian Government funds the building work directly or indirectly above the relevant funding thresholds. As this Request is for appointment to a Register of Prequalified Suppliers rather than for a defined project, could Council please confirm:

Whether accreditation under the Scheme is a mandatory precondition to appointment to the Register; or whether Schedule N should be completed on a not-applicable basis and accreditation considered only if and when a particular work order attracts Australian Government funding above the relevant thresholds.

If accreditation is a precondition to appointment, whether Respondents who are not currently accredited are eligible to be appointed to the Register.

We raise this because the answer materially affects whether a number of capable regional contractors are able to submit a conforming response.

We would appreciate a response prior to the close of tenders.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi,

Please see below the response-

Accreditation under the Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme is not a compulsory requirement for this tender. Should you have this accreditation please do not hesitate to include this in your submission but if you do not we are happy for you to leave this section of the response documents blank

Thanks

title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL 20.26 AIRPORT ADVERTISING LICENSE
description:
The Shire of Ashburton (Shire) invites proposals from suitably qualified and experienced advertising organisations for the provision, management, marketing, sale and ongoing maintenance of advertising opportunities at Onslow Airport and within the surrounding airport precinct.

1.1	Summary of Opportunity

The Shire intends to identify a single advertising organisation (with whom to progress negotiations) at the conclusion of this Request for Proposal process.

The successful Respondent will enter into an exclusivity period of 2 months to endeavour to negotiate a potential licence agreement for advertising space at the Onslow Airport for a 5 year term with an option to extend the term for two (2) x 2 year option periods at the sole discretion of the Shire of Ashburton. It is intended that under this licence agreement (if granted) the successful Respondent will be responsible for developing, installing, managing and commercialising advertising assets across approved locations within the airport environment.

Subject to the terms of the licence agreement and also subject to the Local Government Act 1995 (WA) (LGA) (including s3.58 of the LGA), the successful Respondent will be granted advertising rights to market, sell, manage and maintain approved advertising opportunities within specific agreed locations in the Onslow Airport and the surrounding airport precinct, excluding those areas specifically identified within this RFP (see section 4.2).

The Shire is seeking an innovative and commercially focused partner capable of maximising the value of the airport's advertising opportunities while enhancing the passenger experience and maintaining the high presentation standards of the airport precinct. Respondents are encouraged to present creative and contemporary advertising solutions, including both traditional and digital advertising formats, that are appropriate for a regional airport environment.

The successful operator will demonstrate the ability to attract and retain advertisers, generate sustainable revenue streams, and deliver high-quality advertising infrastructure that complements the airport's role as a key gateway to the Ashburton region. The Shire may, following evaluation of submissions, select a preferred Respondent and enter into an exclusivity period during which time the Shire and preferred Respondent will seek to finalise an in-principle licence agreement without undertaking any further request for tender or quotation process.

The Lansdown Eco-Industrial Precinct (LEIP or Precinct) is positioned as a major industrial precinct for environmentally responsible advanced manufacturing, technology and processing activities. The Precinct is located approximately 40 kilometres south of the Townsville central business district in the suburb of Calcium and comprises approximately 2,200 hectares extending east from the Mingela State Forest and Lansdown Creek towards the Flinders Highway. Townsville City Council (Council) acquired the land in 2001 after its previous use by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation as a pasture research site.

Please could you clarify if 'the Contract' refers only to other Emergency Services Contracts, or if we are permitted to provide referees from other government contracts we have provided services under nationally.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon,

In reply to the question:

The ITO Response Form at 3.10 Referees requests details of 2 other government customers to which the Supplier has provided Goods and/or Services under the Contract. Please could you clarify if 'the Contract' refers only to other Emergency Services Contracts, or if we are permitted to provide referees from other government contracts, we have provided services under nationally.

TMR Reply

The reference to "the Contract" in section 3.10 (Referees) is not limited to Emergency Services Contracts. Suppliers may provide referees from other government contracts under which they have delivered similar or relevant goods and/or services. These contracts may be with Queensland Government agencies or other Australian government entities, provided the referees are able to comment on the Supplier's performance in delivering services comparable to those sought under this procurement.

title: Lithgow Mountain Bike Trails Construction Expressions of Interest (EOI Phase)
description:
Central Tablelands Mountain Bike Club (CTMBC) invites suitably experienced and capable specialist mountain bike trail construction contractors to register their interest in the design and construction of the Lithgow Mountain Bike Park trail network at State Mine Gully, Lithgow NSW.

This Expression of Interest (EOI) is Stage 1 of a two-stage procurement. It is a capability and capacity assessment only. No price is sought at this stage. Respondents assessed as capable will be shortlisted and invited to submit a tender under a subsequent selective Request for Tender (RFT).

This EOI has been prepared in accordance with the CTMBC Procurement Procedure and is an open and transparent process consistent with best practice. It is conducted via VendorPanel and administered by PMO 360 Pty Ltd on behalf of CTMBC.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
43 Minley Cres
East Ballina, New South Wales 2478
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Central Tablelands Mountain Bike Club (CTMBC) is based in Lithgow NSW.

One of the first standalone mountain bike clubs in Australia we formed in 1984 and has been a staple part of the Australian mountain bike scene ever since.

CTMBC is in charge of grant funding to build the Lithgow Mountain Bike Transformation Project, funded by the Department of Regional NSW.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Tuesday 08 September 2026 05:00 PM (AUS Eastern Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
In mid-2022 CTMBC was awarded grant funding by the NSW Department of Regional NSW to develop approximately 25 km of purpose-built single-track and establish a mountain bike park adjacent to Lithgow at State Mine Gully. The project is co-funded, with National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) providing a co-contribution directed to adjacent car parks, walking and bike tracks on the National Park estate, and additional Australian Government funding contributing to the broader program in 2025. Grant funds are held in trust by Keystone Lawyers as escrow agent and disbursed to suppliers as approved and as required.

Development consent for the mountain bike park was granted on 10 August 2026 under DA170/25 (Western Regional Planning Panel reference PPSWES-324). The trail alignments have been designed by World Trail Pty Ltd and are an approved plan under the consent.

Activities to obtain the Construction Certificate are underway and are expected to be completed by November 2026. While the Construction Certificate is a prerequisite to construction commencing, the development application was by far the most difficult activity and is now approved. Subject to those remaining conditions, the project is free to proceed.

This EOI relates to Package 1 — the State Mine Gully (excluding National Park) trail network, being approximately 24.5 km of the 37.6 km total network. The remaining approximately 13.1 km sits within the Gardens of Stone State Conservation Area and is a separate NPWS-funded and NPWS-delivered workstream that is not part of this procurement.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
After four years of planning, assessment and collaboration, the Club is celebrating an approval that marks a major milestone for a project that has navigated a complex planning and environmental assessment process involving multiple agencies, extensive technical studies and broad stakeholder engagement.

The consent unlocks approximately 25 kilometres of purpose built bike and walking trails, within the State Mine Gully precinct commencing from the State Mine Heritage Park and reachable in two hours from Sydney by road, and served directly by passenger rail. It is the link the whole vision depended on, connecting the Lithgow town centre directly to the trail network, so that riders arrive in town, stay in town, and spend in town.

The trail network will play a key role in connecting Lithgow to some of Australia’s most spectacular natural landscapes, helping establish the city as a gateway to both the Gardens of Stone and Wollemi National Parks.

The trails are designed for everyone from first time riders to experienced descenders, with network design by leading international mountain bike trail designers World Trail. Designed for riders and visitors of all abilities, the network will provide new opportunities for outdoor recreation, nature based tourism and community wellbeing while showcasing the region’s unique landscapes and heritage. For a town built on coal and steel, it is a genuinely new chapter: a former industrial landscape becoming a destination in its own right

Your concerns are duly notated, however this is a proper process and is being run with high scrutiny.

The project team is also interested in consortiums. Due to biodiversity constraints, the trails cannot be 100% machine built.

Cheers

title: Design & Construction - Two (2) Bedroom Modular Dwellings - Yarrabah ASC
description:
The Scope is described in the document(s) attached to or provided with this Request for Quotation and identified as:

Scope of Works (Design & Construct)

The Contractor shall undertake the complete design of new residential Modular dwellings at 13 Smith Street and Bulguru Park, Yarrabah with the following design required for council approval –

Tenderers are required to provide separate lump-sum pricing for the following options and Locations:

13 Smith Street, Yarrabah

•	Option 1 – Two (2) Modular Homes: Total lump-sum price for the supply and delivery of two (2) modular homes.

•	Option 2 – Three (3) Modular Homes: Total lump-sum price for the supply and delivery of three (3) modular homes.

Pricing for each option is to represent the complete cost applicable to that quantity, including any applicable economies of scale, bulk purchasing discounts, shared mobilisation, transport, preliminaries or other cost efficiencies.

However, Council reserves the right, at its sole discretion and subject to available funding, to proceed with either Option 1 or Option 2.

Bulguru Park, Yarrabah

•	Two (2) Modular Homes: Total lump-sum price for the supply and delivery of two (2) modular homes.

Design Requirements / Preferred Layout Outcomes

Tenderers are to incorporate the following design considerations within the proposed dwelling layouts, noting these items are preferred outcomes and not limited to the below:

•	Modular Dwellings to include Two (2) bedrooms, with Kitchen, bathroom, WC toilet, and Laundry and any other requirements to ensure they are Platinum level minimum as per Remote Housing Standards

•	Individual Driveways to the dwellings

•	Vehicle parking areas to include colour matched fencing, screening or similar treatments to improve privacy, security and streetscape presentation.

•	Kitchen and/or lounge room preferred toward the street facing side of the dwelling to improve outlook, passive surveillance and natural light.

•	Dining area to provide practical connection between kitchen and living areas with efficient internal flow.

•	Laundry to be located towards the rear of the dwelling with direct access to patio / outdoor area for functionality.

•	Adequate internal linen storage to be provided, centrally located and practical for day to day household use.

•	Overall design to prioritise privacy, functional living, efficient use of site area, and a high quality residential presentation suited to the local environment.

•	The design must conform with Remote Housing Standards and be minimum of Platinum Level in all aspects.

•	Design and Construction to incorporate the Yarrabah Aboriginal Shire Council House Fencing Standards 2024 – which is attached as part of this RFT.

The Works include, but are not limited to, all labour, materials, plant, equipment, design, approvals and activities necessary to deliver a fully operational, compliant and complete housing development fit for purpose and ready for handover and occupation.

Payment Terms

Payment terms are done via progress claims every 21 Days or at agreed payment intervals.

Key Requirements

•	The Contractor is responsible for the complete design development, coordination and certification of the Works.

•	The Contractor shall ensure the Works comply with all applicable legislation, codes, standards and authority requirements.

•	The Works shall be delivered as a complete and functional development, notwithstanding any omissions or discrepancies in the reference documentation.

•	A mandatory Indigenous Employment and Business Participation (IEBP) Plan shall be submitted with the Tender. Failure to submit an IEBP may result in the Tender being deemed non-conforming.

•	Design and Construction must be minimum of Platinum Level as per the Design and Construction standards for Remote Housing.

•	Dwelling must be able to be moved from the property at a later date(10 Years plus) if needed.

•	Property to be raised to acceptable FFL requirements as per Yarrabah Aboriginal Shire Council.

Scope of Works

Without limiting the Contractor’s obligations, the Works include but are not limited to:

Design & Approvals

•	Detailed building designs of all dwellings and associated infrastructure

•	Modular Style homes must be Platinum Level Minimum as per the Design & Construction Standards for Remote Housing.

•	Design coordination across all disciplines

•	Preparation of all documentation required for construction, approvals and certification

o	The Contractor must submit SD stage drawings to Council for feedback and approval prior to progressing to CD.

•	Obtaining all approvals, permits and authority clearances

Site Establishment & Civil Works

•	Site establishment, access, temporary services and controls

•	Clearing, grubbing, demolition if required and site preparation (demolition of existing dwellings is excluded from this tender)

•	Bulk earthworks, cut and fill, trimming and compaction incl. testing if applicable

•	Set-out of all works in accordance with approved design and issued FFLs

•	Stormwater drainage, overland flow management and lawful discharge

•	Geotechnical woks will be undertaken by the successful tender.

Residential Construction

•	Construction of Modular dwellings in accordance with nominated house types

•	Modular Home Style. Must be able to be detached and moved if needed.

•	Complete construction of each dwelling including all structural, architectural and building elements necessary to achieve a fully functional and compliant dwelling

•	Supply and installation of all fixtures, fittings and appliances

•	Kitchens, bathrooms and laundries including joinery

Services & Utilities

•	All hydraulic services including water, sewer and drainage

•	Electrical reticulation, metering, switchboards and internal installations

•	Communications and data provisions as typically required

•	Coordination and connection to mains

External & Ancillary Works

•	Driveways, pathways, hardstand areas and access ways

•	Fencing, gates and boundary treatments

•	Reinstatement and making good of all disturbed areas

•	Installation of external fixtures including T-Bar clotheslines, external sink and bins

Testing, Commissioning & Handover

•	Testing and commissioning of all services and systems

•	Rectification of defects and completion of outstanding works

•	Provision of as-constructed documentation, manuals and warranties

•	Final certification and approvals for occupancy

•	Handover of a complete, operational and compliant development

Contractor Obligations

•	The Contractor shall verify all site conditions, dimensions, levels and service locations prior to commencing Works.

•	The Contractor shall be deemed to have allowed for all conditions that may reasonably be anticipated from available information and site inspection.

•	No claim will be accepted for matters arising from failure to adequately investigate site conditions or coordinate the Works.

•	The Contractor is responsible for all coordination, interfaces and integration of the Works, whether expressly stated or reasonably inferred.

Project Specification

•	National Construction Code (NCC)

•	Design & Construction Standards for Remote Housing

Documents Provided

•	Geotechnical Data – 13 Smith Street

•	386262-4 L147 Smith Survey Data

•	13 Smith St_DFL_Topography

•	13 Smith St_Unit 1_DFL_Topography

•	13 Smith St_Unit 3_DFL_Topography

•	YASC_2026_021 – YASC Housing Fence Standards

The Contractor shall comply with the current edition of the National Construction Code (NCC), all applicable Australian Standards (AS/NZS), and all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.

It shall be the Contractor’s responsibility to identify and comply with all standards applicable to the Works, whether they are specifically listed in this document.

title: ITT269 - Redevelopment Kawana Aquatic Centre - Construction Stage 3
description:
Sunshine Coast Council has engaged a specialist design team to prepare the design and construction documentation for Stages 1 to 4 of the Kawana Aquatic Centre Redevelopment. With Stages 1 and 2 now complete, Council is seeking submissions from suitably qualified Principal Contractors to undertake the Kawana Aquatic Centre Redevelopment – Construction Stage 3 works.

Stage 3 of the redevelopment will involve the resurfacing of the existing 25-metre pool, construction of a new storage facility, and upgrades to the centre's mechanical and electrical infrastructure.

The successful Principal Contractor will be required to supply all materials, plant, equipment and labour necessary to undertake and complete all activities associated with the scope of works under this Contract. This includes carrying out all tasks, operations and associated services required to deliver the works in accordance with the specified requirements and to a satisfactory standard.

Given the facility will remain operational during construction, the Contractor must implement a staged delivery approach that minimises disruption to facility users, pedestrian access, parking availability, traffic movements, and visitors to the precinct.

The works will be delivered under a lump sum contract, with an anticipated commencement date of February 2027 and a required completion date no later than November 2027.

A site information session will be held to provide further details and clarification regarding the project requirements, site conditions and Council’s expectations. Council strongly encourages tenderers to attend this session to facilitate inspection of restricted access areas, including the plant rooms, noting that no alternative access arrangements will be made available. The session will be conducted in accordance with the details provided in Schedule 2 below.

Founded in 1865, Queensland Rail has a proud history of connecting Queensland communities and supporting local jobs, industries and economies. We are committed to providing a customer-focused, safe, modern and world-class rail service for Queenslanders.

With total assets of $8.0 billion, and a network that extends more than 6,600 kilometres across the state, we are also focused on providing customers and Queenslanders with an efficient and value for money service.

Our 7,500 strong workforce delivers services across our South East Queensland and Regional networks, including Travel and Tourism services and Regional Freight.

Our South East Queensland team provides 8,392 services each week, supporting our customers to reach their destination safely and on-time. In 2019-2020, 44 million passenger trips were taken on the South East Queensland network (a decrease of approximately 20 per cent compared to 2018-2019, associated with COVID-19).

The Regional networks commuter and rail tourism markets are serviced by the Travel and Tourism products. These comprise eight services connecting Regional communities across Queensland with other Regional centres and the South East Queensland corner. These services support the Queensland tourism industry through the provision of unique rail tourism experiences including special events and charters through the operation of a small fleet of heritage services.

Our Regional networks and Freight team provides rail access for freight operators and other Queensland Rail supply chain customers to enable the critical transport of resources and general freight across the state.

We are proud of the role we play in providing vital passenger and freight services and we are dedicated to ensuring that our systems, procedures and practices reflect the highest standards of corporate governance.
