title: Call for Submissions: System Restart Service – North Metro Sub-network of the SWIS
description:
AEMO is calling for submissions from Market Participants to provide a System Restart Service (SRS) for the North Metro sub-network of the South West Interconnected System (SWIS) in Western Australia.

This is to address contract expiry in the sub-network and to ensure continuity of System Restart Services.

A System Restart Service is a service from a Registered Facility, with an energy producing system, that can start without requiring energy to be supplied from a Network to assist in the re-energisation of the SWIS in the event of a system shut down or major supply disruption.

Tender approach: Open to Market Participants capable of providing SRS in the North Metro sub-network.

Service commencement: 1 April 2027

Contract term: 5 years from the service commencement date, although shorter durations can be considered by AEMO.

Technical requirements: Service capability must meet the requirements set out in the WEM System Restart Standard and the North Metro SRS Specification.

Standard-form contract: Contract terms are provided as part of the tender documentation.

The tender process is conducted in accordance with the Electricity System and Market Rules (ESM Rules 3.7).

- National Electricity Market (NEM), the interconnected power system in Australia’s eastern and south-eastern seaboard.

- Wholesale Electricity Market (WEM) and power system in Western Australia.

We also operate the:

- Victorian Declared Wholesale Gas Market (DWGM) and the Victorian gas transmission system.

- Wholesale gas Short Term Trading Market hubs in Adelaide, Sydney and Brisbane.

- Retail Gas Markets in Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and New South Wales and Australia Capital Territory.

- Wallumbilla and Moomba Gas Supply Hub in Queensland and South Australia.

- Natural Gas Services Bulletin Board.

- Western Australia Gas Bulletin Board.

As Australia’s independent energy markets and power systems operator, AEMO provides critical planning, forecasting and power systems information, security advice, and services to our stakeholders.

title: MidCoast Council Green Waste Processing Tender Waste Services
description:
MidCoast Council is seeking an experienced contractor to provide as-required on-site shredding, grinding, screening and processing of Garden and Green Waste Organics at the following Waste Management Centres:

- Tuncurry, Midge Orchid Road, Darawank

- Tea Gardens, Transfer Close, Tea Gardens

- Gloucester, 385 Thunderbolts Way, Gloucester

- Bulahdelah, Recovery Road, Bulahdelah

- Stroud, Simmsville Road, Stroud

The Contractor will process accumulated green waste into the Product Grades specified in the tender documents and form separate, safe and surveyable stockpiles or windrows. The proposed Contract term is two years, with three optional one-year extensions exercisable solely by Council. Services require attendance at Council facilities and cannot be provided remotely.

We are passionate about the health and wellbeing of Queenslanders, with a vision for sport to be at the heart of an active, healthy and connected Queensland.

Our purpose is to inspire all Queenslanders to lead active lives in healthy communities and to support the success of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

We work every day to make our vision a reality by supporting the state’s sports industry from the elite to the grassroots, through funding, infrastructure and planning, partnerships, events, disaster assistance, capability development, policy and a regional network of engagement officers. We also operate the state’s four sport and recreation venues in Townsville, Sunshine Coast and on the Gold Coast (Runaway Bay and Tallebudgera).

As a Games delivery partner and the coordinating body for Queensland Government, we’re focused on achieving the best possible outcomes for the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games and delivering enduring legacies for communities across the state. We are committed to delivering a Games Queenslanders can be proud of.

We’re also home to the Office of Racing, supporting the governance and administration of the racing industry across the state.

The Department manages sporting facilities located in Queensland, Australia (Venues).

The Venues has a large membership base over several locations and hosts casual members of the community including students with disabilities as well as athletes and visitors every year.

The Venues include some of the following facilities, 20m indoor heated pool, 50m outdoor pool, recovery ice and heated baths, 600sqm open-air gym, (WA) accredited athletics track with turn infield, FIH standard hockey pitch and two (2) international standard beach volleyball courts. In addition, there are also lodges that can accommodate guests in twin and quad-share comfort, fully equipped, multi-purpose conference facilities, Allied Health Services and bistros catering for guests.

The Venues house open-air and closed gyms providing a large range of bikes, rowing machines, fixed weight machines and free weighs to members and visitors.

Local, state, national and international athletes, teams and sporting bodies will access the facilities including the gym Equipment as part of their training regime.

Some of the Venues due to the nature of the open-air gymnasium may seek Equipment suited to this environment to minimise the effects of premature and accelerated ageing.

(a)	Provision of new Equipment under the Agreement including:

a.	Cardio and Strength Equipment – Refer 26DSROPG025 - Attachment A;

(c)	Delivery of planned and non-scheduled maintenance and repairs and replacements of parts as required.

(a)	Removal and disposal of current equipment.

description:

Tenders are invited for the Statutory Planning Public Notice Installation Service.

Council is seeking submissions from suitably qualified and experienced contractors for the provision of public notification signage services associated with statutory planning applications. The services include the production, installation, maintenance, inspection and removal of public notice signs at locations throughout the municipality, in accordance with Council requirements and relevant legislative obligations.

The successful contractor will be required to provide a reliable, responsive and customer-focused service that supports Council’s statutory planning processes. publicQuestions.question: Can you please explain the journey and processes the jockey takes on race day through the jockey administration building from start to finish? Including where they enter and exit, and if the jockey needs to sign-in and sign-out at Reception upon entrance and leaving?
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see the information provided below for information:

With regards to the Stewards’ Room, the media truck currently hooks up in the Stewards’ Room a couple of hours prior to the start of each Raceday. PRC is checking whether there are any requested changes from the media truck to see if there are any suggestions on how this process can be streamlined. Tenderers are requested to take this into consideration.

 Jockey Processes and Movements

1. Jockey Arrival and Movement

Upon arrival at the racecourse, jockeys report to the Clerk of Scales, who is employed by RWWA, to advise that they have arrived and surrender their mobile phone for the day.

They then proceed to the jockey locker/change rooms. There are separate male and female locker rooms, with associated showers.

Once changed, jockeys generally remain in the Jockeys’ Lounge until they are called for their race.

A doorbell/alert system is currently located in each locker room to notify jockeys when they are required to come out for race preparation.

When called, jockeys leave the locker/lounge area and report to the Clerk of Scales, where those riding in the upcoming race are weighed before proceeding to the mounting yard.

The layout should allow this movement to occur efficiently without trainers, barrier staff, presenters or other personnel needing to move through the jockeys’ private areas.

2. Jockeys’ Lounge & Kitchenette

Required kitchenette facilities:

-Sink

-Bench space for a slow cooker and microwave

-Full-size refrigerator

-Under-bench storage for crockery and cutlery

-Room for: Toaster, Toasted sandwich maker, Kettle, Microwave, Slow cooker

Jockeys will need room for lounge chairs & dining table in this area. Usually 30-36 Jockeys each raceday (Some will only have one race). There will also be a notice Board to pin up raceday information sheets here.

3. Jockey Massage Area

There is currently a small massage area adjacent to the jockey locker rooms.

This should be retained in the new design, with appropriate privacy and convenient access from the jockey facilities.

4. Clerk of Scales

The Clerk of Scales room should remain the central operational point for the jockey facilities.

The Clerk of Scales is the first point of contact for jockeys arriving at the racecourse and is responsible for the weighing process.

The area needs to accommodate:

- Clerk of Scales workstation with notice Board to pin up raceday information sheets

- Jockey arrival/check-in

-Phone collection and secure storage

-Jockey weighing process

-Interaction with jockeys immediately before they proceed to the mounting yard

-Access to the Scales Assistant and saddle/saddle cloth storage

5. Saddles and Saddle Cloths

Trainers need to collect saddle cloths before each race.

Saddle cloths are distributed by the Scales Assistant and are currently stored in large pigeonholes adjacent to the Clerk of Scales.

There is normally a divider/barrier between the trainers and the saddle cloth storage, preventing trainers from simply helping themselves to saddle cloths.

The new design should retain this controlled distribution arrangement, allowing:

Scales Assistant ? Saddle Cloth Storage ? Trainer Collection without trainers having unrestricted access to the storage area.

6. Trainer and Barrier Staff Waiting Area

A waiting area is required for trainers and barrier staff who are waiting prior to each race.

This area could be positioned adjacent to the Clerk of Scales but should not interfere with jockey circulation or the weighing process.

The external side of the building should also provide a gated common area leading towards the mounting yard. Jockeys will go through this area to access the mounting yard.

This area will function as a common waiting/holding area for:

Trainers

Barrier staff

Television presenters

Other race-day personnel requiring access to the mounting yard

7. Stewards’ Area

A dedicated Stewards’ area is required immediately adjacent to the Clerk of Scales.

The room should be approximately boardroom-sized, allowing for up to six RWWA Stewards on a Raceday.

The room will be used for:

-Steward meetings

-Race-day operations

-Reviewing race footage

-Conducting steward enquiries

-Discussions with jockeys, trainers and other participants when required

The room should therefore have sufficient space and privacy to conduct formal enquiries without disrupting the general race-day operation.

Stewards’ technology and equipment requirements

The room will require:

-Up to four large television screens

-Numerous electrical power outlets

-Numerous Ethernet/data outlets

-Suitable locations for screens and associated equipment

-Adequate desk/boardroom table space for up to six Stewards

-A refrigerator for food and drinks supplied by the Race Club

The power and Ethernet requirements should be considered at the design stage rather than relying on extension leads or temporary cabling on Racedays.

The key consideration is that the Clerk of Scales should sit centrally between the jockey facilities, saddle/saddle cloth distribution, Stewards’ area and access towards the mounting yard.

publicQuestions.answer:
RFI 1 – Approval of Nominated Subconsultants

Response:

Tenderers are referred to Clause 3.4.1 of the Tenderer’s Offer Form, together with the subconsultant requirements of the RFT and the relevant provisions of the Consultancy Agreement.

The Principal intends to review the Tenderer’s nominated subconsultants as part of the tender evaluation process, having regard to the information provided in the Tender. The Principal nevertheless reserves its rights under the RFT and Consultancy Agreement in relation to the approval of subconsultants. The RFT requires Tenderers to identify proposed subconsultants and provides that the Consultant remains responsible for their performance.

Where the Principal does not accept a nominated subconsultant, the Tenderer/Consultant will be required to promptly nominate a suitably qualified and experienced alternative for the Principal’s approval. No fixed timeframe applies; however, this is to occur without unreasonable delay and so as not to adversely affect the Project programme.

Consistent with Clause 3.4.1 of the Tenderer’s Offer Form, Tenderers should allow for any replacement of a nominated subconsultant required through this approval process without adjustment to the tendered fee.

If, following appointment, the Principal requires a change that materially alters the agreed scope of Services or gives rise to circumstances outside the requirements contemplated by the RFT, any associated cost or programme implications will be considered in accordance with the variation provisions of the Consultancy Agreement. No adjustment to the Contract Price or programme will apply unless approved in writing by the Principal.

Except as clarified above, the requirements of the RFT, Scope of Works, Tenderer’s Offer Form, Consultancy Agreement and issued Addenda remain unchanged.

________

RFI 2 – Development Approval Pathway

Tenderers are referred to Clause 4.3 – Planning and Statutory Approvals, Clause 7 – Programme and Milestones, Clause 9 – Principal’s Responsibilities and Clause 10 – Exclusions and Additional Services of the Scope of Works, together with Addendum No. 1.

The Principal is not prescribing at tender stage whether the Project will proceed by way of a new Development Application, an amendment to Development Approval P140/2022, or continued reliance on the existing approval where legally available.

As set out in Clause 4.3 of the Scope of Works, the successful Consultant is required to review the existing Development Approval and current project information, determine the applicable statutory approval pathway and advise the Principal whether a new Development Application, amendment to an existing approval or other statutory approvals are required.

Addendum No. 1 also confirms that the Development Approval documentation previously provided remains available for reference and consideration in relation to the previous approval and statutory approval pathway. The concept drawings subsequently issued with Addendum No. 1 represent the current concept information for the purposes of the RFT.

For tender pricing purposes, Tenderers are to allow within their lump sum for the professional services necessary to determine and progress the applicable planning approval pathway, including preparation and coordination of a new Development Application or amendment to the existing Development Approval if required.

Any Development Application or amendment is to address the Project works requiring planning approval and have regard to both Separable Portion 1 and Separable Portion 2. The documentation is to preserve the Principal’s ability to proceed with Separable Portion 1 only or both separable portions in accordance with the RFT.

The Project programme contemplates the planning and statutory approval process occurring prior to construction. Tenderers are required to develop their proposed programme having regard to the applicable approval pathway and anticipated authority assessment periods, with the objective of supporting construction commencement following completion of the major race meetings at the end of March 2027. Tenderers should identify any approval-related programme risks or constraints in their submission. The Scope expressly requires the Consultant to prepare the consultancy programme, identify critical path activities and integrate statutory approvals with the required Project programme.

Tenderers are to include within their lump sum the consultant services, documentation and supporting specialist inputs reasonably identifiable from the RFT documentation as necessary to progress the applicable Development Application or amendment. If, following appointment and confirmation of the statutory pathway, additional investigations or specialist services are required that were not reasonably identifiable at the time of appointment, these will be dealt with in accordance with the Additional Services provisions of the Scope of Works.

Statutory application fees, authority fees and other third-party statutory fees will be paid by the Principal in accordance with Clause 9 of the Scope of Works.

Except as clarified above, the requirements of the RFT, Scope of Works, Tenderer’s Offer Form, Consultancy Agreement and issued Addenda remain unchanged.

title: Marybourough Hospital - The Demaine External Refurbishment - WBHHS-MBH26008
description:
The Demaine is a building that is over 100 years old and is located on the Queensland Heritage Register. It has been identified by the Building, Engineering and Maintenance Department (BEMS) that the structural integrity of the building in various locations is compromised.

The Demaine also has several compliance issues, which includes the Level 1 Balustrade along with asbestos material in the waterproof membrane located on the level 1 veranda floor. These items need to be addressed to ensure ongoing safety for our patients, staff and the broader community.

The proposal is to complete all external refurbishment works to meet current compliance and avoid expensive maintenance issues in the future. The proposed works will align with the extensive engineering reports, and Heritage approved Architectural design completed in 2024.

Works will include, but are not limited to:

•	Veranda and Balustrade Upgrades

•	Asbestos Removal

•	New Waterproof Protection (Level 1 - Veranda Deck)

•	External Lighting Upgrades

•	Replacement of Fire Stairs

•	New Covered Walkway (Block F to Block V)

•	DDA Front Ramp

•	Various Building Works

•	External Painting

The Works will take approximately 10 to 12 months to complete (from award date) and will need to be staged to suit the scope of works and the operations of Oral Health, Supportive Therapy, Hospital in the Home and Staff Accommodation.

title: 5603-6500-0001 Escott Weir Repair
description:
Burke Shire Council invites tenders from suitably qualified tenderers for the construction of DRFA restoration works on the Escott weir.

The scope of works required under the contract includes repairs to the existing water supply weir. Repairs are undertaken with a combination of sheet piling, concrete fill and rock protection.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
19 Main St
Buderim, Queensland 4556
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Shire of Burke is in far North West Queensland on the Gulf of Carpentaria, adjoining the Northern Territory border.

Burketown is located on the Savannah Way, one of the world's great transcontinental road journeys for adventure travellers.

Burketown is 2,115km to the north west of Brisbane, the capital of Queensland, and 2,100km from Darwin. The Shire lies on the southern coast of the Gulf of Carpentaria and and shares a border with the Northern Territory.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Thursday 10 September 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
buyerQuestions: Please complete Response Schedules within the Tender documents.

publicQuestions.question:
The questions for this Escott Weir Repair job:

1. Can we have the Geo Tech report for the foundation and soil condition of the work area please? As we need to install the spec sheet pile 4mm thick & 5.5 meters deep under the working ground (6 meters depth of the sheet piles), it's very important to have that Geo Tech report for the soil condition.

2. Can we use the nearest empty space near the weir to be a site establishment for the site facilities (office, lunchroom, etc.) put the equipment within the site fence please?

3. About the traffic management plan, can we ask the permit from the council, or should we ask the traffic management company to apply for that?

Thanks very much.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Please refer to GT25-014-25 issued by ARO, uploaded today.

2. Yes, site facilitites can be located near the weir within road reserve

3. The contractor will arrange for a TMD to draft a traffic management plan and TGS for the works. The successful contractor will issue this to council for approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there,

Can we use the Brand Terra the steel sheet pile STC S355 BTPILESEC SCH 5 or the VINYL pile STC TKV620 to replace the sheet pile PSH3-700 from Piling Solutions please? From the Terra company the item can replace this Piling Solutions, As the Piling solution still haven't sent the price out, the Vinyl sheet pile will be 9.5mm thick, more echo-friendly, never get rusted, long life-span, and cheaper. So, can you please let us know if it's ok to quote with different brand and material replacement for the price. Thanks very much.

Carter
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

As long as the section modulus is greater than the specified pile, the nominated alternatives are acceptable.

We would consider this substitution to be an alternate tender. Please ensure you submit both a conforming tender as well as the non-conforming tender. Please advise if any issues in this regard.

publicQuestions.question: Good morning. Can Council please provide the geotechnical report for this project.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to GT25-014-25 Issue 1.pdf (119.0 Kb), added to the Vendorpanel request yesterday.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI - Geotech Report

Hi Council,

Could we please request any available Geotech reports or site investigations to determine ground conditions for sheet piling works. If these sheets were to hit anything underground in the driving process, they will bend very easily rendering the job unsuccessful.

RFI - Wet Season

Hi Council,

Could you please advise of any funding constraints that require the project to be complete prior to wet season? Given Leadtime on sheet piles is around 3weeks this becomes increasingly risky in an already heavy flow stream to perform works.

RFI - Existing Concrete Slab

Hi Council,

the project drawings do not clearly demonstrate a saw cut line or demolition details, section A and B both show mass concrete fill behind downstream sheets. Is there replacement of existing slab required?

RFI - Cultural Heritage

Hi Council,

Has cultural heritage inspection of the work area been undertaken or will be undertaken prior to contract award to ensure no delays occur?

RFI - Sheet Pile material & Method

Hi Council,

Is construction sequencing flexible? currently there is large amount of dump rock and rock erosion control bags present within downstream work area. The current designed sheet piles would be unable to be driven through any rocky materials and therefore would require downstream toe to be excavated prior to commencing sheet piles. If these sheets were to hit anything underground in the driving process, they will bend very easily rendering the job unsuccessful.

RFI - Local Traffic

Hi Council,

Given the required construction methodology will generate significant increased flows through section 2 of the weir. Has community consultation been sought to advise of significant increase in safety risks when crossing this weir during construction? Proposal to close to local traffic should be considered given the increase in safety risks.
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI - Geotech Report

Answer: Please refer to GT25-014-25 Issue 1.pdf (119.0 Kb), uploaded to Vendorpanel on 01/09/2026.

RFI - Wet Season

Answer: Current intent is to complete the Works this year.

RFI - Existing Concrete Slab

Answer: Replacement on the existing slab is not required. The Tenderer is to identify in their response how they will repair any temporary demolition required to facilitate the Works.

RFI - Cultural Heritage

Answer: All works are located along within the road reserve. The local cultural heritage body has been notified of the Works.

RFI - Sheet Pile material & Method

Answer: Contractor may advise on alternative sequencing, if preferred, provided the scope doesn't change. Changes to sequencing alone shall be considered as a confirming tender. 

RFI - Local Traffic

Answer: Access must be maintained at all times. Current water level has fallen allowing access to be currently maintained.

title: PSA00330 - Audio Visual Partner
description:
Townsville City Council is seeking to establish a Preferred Supplier Arrangement with a suitably qualified and experienced audio visual (AV) partner.

The purpose of this arrangement is to establish a strategic audio-visual technology partner capable of providing design, supply, installation, commissioning, integration, maintenance, lifecycle management, training and support services for Council's existing and future audiovisual environments. Council reserves the right to procure goods and services outside this arrangement where operational, technical or commercial circumstances warrant.

103 Walker St
Townsville City, Queensland 4810
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: The City of Townsville is an Australian local government area (LGA) located in North Queensland, Australia. It encompasses the city of Townsville, together with the surrounding rural areas, to the south are the communities of Alligator Creek, Woodstock and Reid River, and to the north are Northern Beaches and Paluma, and also included is Magnetic Island. Townsville is considered to be the capital of North Queensland.

publicQuestions.question:
Are we required to decommission the old systems?

Public BYOD Rooms - Logitech Rally Bar, Rally Bar Mini, or Rally system (BYOD Mode) with Tap control, and Philips display. This may suggest these are not MTR rooms but BYOM rooms, thus not requiring a Tap. The users laptop plugs into the Rally bar using the Extend or HDMI/USB and drives the meeting using the Rally Bar for camera, mic and speakers. Is this correct?

Bespoke AV rooms/sites - Involving control and signalling equipment from AMX, SVSi, Extron, Extron NAV, Biamp, Q-SYS, BSS, Kramer, Audinate, Bose, Lumens

These rooms require floor plans or photos with room dimensions and a functional brief to accurately quote. After receiving the floor plans/photos, I am happy to hold a stakeholder meeting over Teams to discuss the process and functional requirements. We conduct this work nationally and if the Council can provide the requested information we won't need to attend any site visits. Alternatively as another option we may be able to quote a Consultation to fly in a specialist to go through each room and design them appropriately.

We can provide and install under carpet floor track. We will however need to understand specifics around power and data requirements at the display and at the table so we can quote accurately.
publicQuestions.answer:
Are we required to decommission the old systems?

Yes. Where an engagement involves the replacement of an existing AV system, the supplier may be required to decommission the superseded equipment. Specific decommissioning, disposal, and related requirements will be defined and agreed on a project-by-project basis through the applicable Statement of Work (SoW).

Public BYOD Rooms:

o These facilities are purely BYOD Rooms. As of Sept 2026, only 2 of these rooms exist however Council has plans for approx. 5-8 more to be installed. Current rooms (and some future rooms) are/will be based on Rally Bar/Rally Bar Mini BYOD mode: as per Logitech diagrams:

https://www.logitech.com/content/dam/prosupport/vc-general/vc-product-wiring-diagrams.pdf#page=18.

Retaining the Logitech Tap in place allows for Camera control, volume control and muting etc. It is an optional extra we use and require.

o Other rooms will involve Logitech rally parts, minus the MTR NUC. None of these are built as of Sept 2026, but are intended to be installed.

To be built as per Logitech Diagram: https://www.logitech.com/content/dam/prosupport/vc-general/vc-product-wiring-diagrams.pdf#page=41

For these units we use the Logitech BT remote for Camera and volume control.

Bespoke Rooms/systems:

o 7 bespoke systems utilising a combination of AMX, SVSi, Extron, Extron NAV, Biamp, Q-SYS, BSS, Kramer.

o These rooms are summarised as below:

1. Local Disaster Coordination Centre - AMX Control, SVSi routing, BOSE DSP, various displays. AMX Code available. Schematic not available.

2. Council Chambers - AMX Control, SVSi routing, NDI cameras & routing, Coriomaster windowing processor, Biamp Tesira DSP, Lumens Streaming. AMX Code available, Schematic available (attached).

3. Riverway Library – AMX Control, SVSi routing, Biamp Tesira DSP, AMX Code available. Schematic available (attached).

4. Riverway Stadium – Extron and BSS Control, Extron DTP routing, Kramer matrix switcher routing, BSS DSP. Extron code available, BSS code NOT available, Schematic for Extron Side available (attached) No schematic available for BSS side.

5. Northern Beaches Community Centre. – Extron Control, Extron NAV routing, Q-SYS DSP. Extron Code available, Schematic available (attached).

6. Project Connect Workshop – Extron Control, Kramer routing, Cisco Room Bar MTR. Extron Code available, Schematic available (attached).

7. Daly Rd Gugu Badham Room 1st Floor – AMX Control, SVSi routing, BOSE DSP. AMX Code not available, Basic schematic available (attached). Room intended to be demolished/rebuilt within 18 months.

Schematics for the above noted meeting rooms have been attached to this tender

Floortrack Installation:

o We use Cisco Room Bars in MTR mode. Floor track products are used to provide a safe data path between the meeting room table and the wall where the display/meeting bar are mounted.

o This data path facilitates

 - mains power from the wall,

 - Logitech extend for wired content/BYOD,

 - Cat6 run for Cisco AES67 table mics,

 - Cat6 run for Cisco navigator control panel,

 - Cat6 run for 2nd Cisco Mic or future use.

publicQuestions.question:
In 1 - Scope of Work, PSA00330 – Audio Visual Partner, PG 9 refers to 13 Bespoke rooms requiring Annual Maintenance.

In PSA00330-Audio_Visual_Partner_II_Schedule_2-Response_Schedule_v1.0, Business Requirement 2.7 it asks for Biannual checks for all AV systems.

Can you confirm which direction you would like this priced at? Annual on Bespoke or Biannual for all 96 Rooms.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your clarification question.

We request that the maintenance schedule is priced so that the bespoke rooms are serviced biannually and the 96 standard meeting rooms annually.

Given their higher complexity, greater number of components and increased criticality, the bespoke rooms present a higher risk of failure and would benefit from more frequent maintenance. The standard meeting rooms are generally reliable, receive firmware updates automatically and faults are typically straightforward to resolve.

title: Request for Quotation: Waste Management Services for New Year’s Eve 2026-27
description:
Carry out waste management and cleaning services within Woollahra Council parks and adjoining areas on New Year’s Eve 2026 and New Year’s Day 2027 ensuring that the Parks are kept to a high standard over the New Year Period.

Carry out waste management and cleaning services within the parks (refer below) on New Year’s Eve 2026 and New Year’s Day 2027.

Council requires most of these services to be carried out on New Year’s Eve in order to reduce the workload on the following day.

All cleaning work will need to cease no later than 2.00am New Year’s Day and not commence again prior to 6.00am on New Year’s Day.

Parks will be open to the public for general use on New Year’s Day and must be clean of all litter, bottle tops, broken glass etc. as early as practicable to ensure they are safe for public use.

title: RFT260087 Construction of Blackwater Recycled Water Pipeline Stage 2 Valve Station
description:
Background Information

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the construction of the Blackwater Recycle Water Pipeline Stage 2 Valve Station at Hunter Street, Blackwater.

The works form part of Council’s recycled water infrastructure and involve the fabrication, supply and installation of new valve station pipework and associated equipment and protective structural cover, together with connections to existing pipeline infrastructure. The works include integration with the existing DN300 HDPE Stage 3 pipeline and DN200 HDPE rising main, installation of Principal-supplied and Contractor-supplied equipment, and associated civil, excavation, backfilling, testing, commissioning and reinstatement works.

The existing DN100 effluent pipeline is required to remain operational during construction until the new work is complete, and the final connections can be undertaken.

The successful Contractor will be required to carefully plan and coordinate the works with Council to maintain continuity of service, minimize operational disruption, and deliver a complete, tested and commissioned installation in accordance with the detailed design drawings and Contract requirements.

Key Deliverables include:

•	Site establishment, management plans, site preparation and disestablishment.

•	Supply and fabrication of stainless-steel pipework and fittings in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

•	Excavation, trenching, backfilling and associated civil works required for the valve station and pipeline connections.

•	Construction of the reinforced concrete valve station slab, plinths and associated civil works in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

•	Supply, fabrication, delivery and erection of the structural steel valve station cover over the above-ground pipework, including roof sheeting and associated structural components, in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

•	Construction and installation of the new valve station pipework and associated equipment.

•	Connection of the new works to the existing DN300 HDPE Stage 3 pipeline and existing DN200 HDPE rising main.

•	Installation and integration of Principal-supplied and existing valves, flowmeters and water meters, including relocation and reuse of nominated existing equipment.

•	Supply all other materials required to complete the works.

•	Planning and sequencing of the works to maintain operation of the existing DN100 effluent pipeline until the final connection and changeover.

•	Supply and installation of the complete Air Bleed Valve (ABV) assembly on the existing DN200 HDPE rising main at CH 516.477, including associated pipework, valves, pit, civil works and ancillary components.

•	Electrical and instrumentation installation for the flowmeters and electrically actuated valves, including field cabling, conduits, terminations and testing to the existing electrical/control board at the Purple Tank irrigation pumps, with PLC and SCADA programming remaining the responsibility of the Principal.

•	Testing, commissioning and demonstration of satisfactory operation of the completed works.

•	Preparation and submission of the completed commissioning checklist and Asset Breakdown Register for all installed pipework, fittings and associated equipment, regardless of source of supply.

•	Site reinstatement, provision of handover documentation and final handover to the Principal.

Particulars of Goods and Services

Central Highlands Regional Council requires the supply, manufacture, installation, testing, commissioning and handover of the Blackwater Recycle Water Pipeline Stage 2 Valve Station works at Hunter Street, Blackwater.

The Works are divided into two (2) Separable Portions as described below.

Tenderers may submit a Tender for Separable Portion 1 only, Separable Portion 2 only, or both Separable Portions. Tenderers are not required to tender for both Separable Portions. The Principal reserves the right to award the Separable Portions separately to different Contractors or together to one Contractor.

Separable Portion 1 – Supply and Manufacture of Stainless-Steel Pipework and Fittings

Separable Portion 1 comprises the supply and manufacture of the stainless-steel pipework, fittings and associated fabricated components shown on the detailed design drawings.

The Contractor for Separable Portion 1 must include all preliminaries and general obligations applicable to Separable Portion 1, including project management, contract administration, coordination, quality management, workplace health and safety obligations associated with fabrication and delivery activities, and all insurances required under the Contract.

The Contractor must:

•	supply all stainless-steel pipework, fittings, flanges and fabricated components identified on the detailed design drawings as Contractor-supplied items;

•	manufacture the stainless-steel pipework, fittings and associated components in accordance with the detailed design drawings;

•	ensure all fabricated components are dimensionally compatible with the valves, meters, pipework and other equipment forming part of the completed valve station assembly;

•	provide all fabricated stainless-steel components required to enable complete assembly of the valve station, except for items specifically identified as Principal-supplied or existing items;

•	coordinate fabrication dimensions with the detailed design drawings and the nominated Principal-supplied and existing equipment; and

•	provide fabrication as-built drawings and all bolts and gaskets required for the complete fabrication package (where required).

•	Stainless-steel pressure pipework and fittings supplied and fabricated under Separable Portion 1 must comply with the material grades, schedules, dimensions and other requirements shown on the detailed design drawings and the applicable requirements of AS 4041. Welding procedures and welding personnel qualifications must comply with AS 3992 and AS 1796, as applicable.

•	Prior to delivery of the fabricated pipework, the Contractor for Separable Portion 1 must submit a complete fabrication quality record / Manufacturing Data Record (MDR). The MDR must include, as applicable, material certificates, welding procedure specifications and qualification records, welder qualification records, weld maps or weld registers, inspection and non-destructive testing records, dimensional inspection records, records of any fabrication or shop testing required by the Tender Documents or applicable standards, fabrication as-built drawings, and release or inspection records. Hydrostatic pressure testing of the complete installed pipework system must remain the responsibility of the Separable Portion 2 Contractor in accordance with Sections 4.4 and 4.6.

The Contractor must make due allowance for all materials, fabrication, welding, fittings, flanges and associated components required to provide a complete Separable Portion 1 fabrication package in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

Separable Portion 2 – Installation, Testing, Commissioning and Handover

Separable Portion 2 comprises the installation and assembly of the valve station and associated pipework, civil and pipeline works, connections to the existing recycled water infrastructure, testing, commissioning and handover of the completed Works.

See Part 2 Specification for further details.

title: Sale of Part 1-13 Cross Street, Double Bay
description:
Council is seeking Tenders for the sale of part 1-13 Cross Street, Double Bay.

The site for sale as part of this tender is a 1,465sqm parcel to be subdivided from 1-13 Cross Street, Double Bay.

1.	Sale of the site with a requirement of 15% of all residential floor space to be provided as affordable housing in perpetuity

2.	Sale of the site with a requirement of 250sqm of floor space for community use

3.	Sale of the site with a requirement of 15% of all residential floor space to be provided as affordable housing in perpetuity and 250sqm of floor space for community use

The sale of the site will provide funds for Council to develop a new car park on the remainder of its land.

It is expected that settlement will occur by June 2029 following demolition of the existing car park and subdivision of 1-13 Cross Street. Further information is provided in the RFT and Draft Contract of Sale.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Could you please confirm the following queries:

1.	The glass proposed for the sloped glazed roof appears non-compliant with the Glazing Code. Has this been assessed for compliance?

2.	Please advise whether the existing roof framing has been checked to support the increased load from the new glazing, or if structural certification will be provided by others.

3.	Could you please confirm whether the existing timber window frames and glazing beads require modification to accommodate the new 9.52?mm bottom row of glazing proposed for the curtain wall, windows, and doors?

4.	Drawing A1500 notes “Salvage basalt pitcher at edge of flagstone paver paving.” Could you clarify this reference? The existing conditions indicate only a concrete spoon drain around the perimeter of the flagstone paving.

5.	Please confirm whether the contractor is required to supply and install new basalt edge stones to the perimeter of the new granitic sand path, or whether Council will provide stock. Additionally, please confirm whether the stone sizing is to match the existing paths adjacent.

6.	Please clarify whether the scope requires full replacement of the existing timber window sill, or only selective renewal of damaged sections.

7.	Please confirm whether the contractor is required to obtain a Division 6 Audit/Report and include associated fees within the Tender submission.

8.	Please confirm whether the contractor is to remove the existing bench seats surrounding the building and reinstate them upon completion, noting that no footing details have been provided for reinstallation.

9.	Please confirm the required treatment of the existing plaques associated with the bench seats, and the finish expected on adjacent rendered surfaces.

10.	Are all existing electrical and security assets not shown on the plan to be retained or removed? Please confirm whether the existing lights and speakers are to remain in place during the restoration works.

11.	Please confirm whether the existing GPOs on each column are to be retained in their current condition. They appear to have been previously painted over.

12.	Please advise whether the existing external surface-mounted power feeds to the four external flood lights are to remain unchanged.

13.	If the existing switchboard is to be installed on two legs as noted, could you please confirm whether all existing power and data circuits are intended to remain within the surface mounted duct located in the corner?

Regards

Request for Information (RFI) – Mobile Carrier Reception Improvement Managed Services

The University of Queensland (UQ) invites interested suppliers to respond to this Request for Information (RFI) and provide information on solutions and market capabilities to improve mobile carrier coverage across selected UQ locations.

UQ is seeking information on carrier-neutral, multi-carrier solutions and related managed services, including support, maintenance and future expansion capabilities. The information obtained through this RFI will assist UQ in understanding available solutions and informing the development of any future procurement requirements.

This RFI is an open market engagement process for information-gathering purposes only. It does not constitute an invitation to tender, request for quotation, or other procurement process, and does not create any commitment or obligation on UQ to proceed with a procurement or award a contract.

Please refer to the attached RFI document for further details, including the scope of information requested and response requirements.

	• RFI Close Date: 25/09/2026 2:00 PM AEST

	• Please note: Dates displayed at the top of the screen may appear in MM/DD/YYYY format.

Interested suppliers can register into the portal firstly, view the tender documents, and then submit an offer using the UQ tendering portal which is called UQProcure.

UQProcure is UQ's procurement solution operating on the Jaggaer One platform. You can view an instructional video on the Buyer Attachments page that will guide you through the platform and how to submit a response to this RFI. Your response will save as you progress through the pages however we would encourage you to save your progress regularly as you complete the form. If you have any questions about using UQProcure, please contact the UQProcure support team or the Contact/s listed above.

description:
The Department of Primary Industries, Queensland Boating and Fisheries Patrol (QBFP) seeks to commission a new 6.5 to 7 metre aluminium fisheries patrol vessel and offroad capable trailer to operate effectively in Queensland’s Gulf of Carpentaria waters. This vessel will be used for long range patrols operating in both shallow coastal foreshores and offshore waters between Kowanyama and the NT border including the Wellesley Island group.

The new vessel is expected to deliver a service life of 10 years, offering robust, efficient, and reliable operations with enhanced seakeeping capabilities, ease of operation, and maintenance.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Queensland Boating and Fisheries Patrol (QBFP), operates a diverse fleet of commercially registered watercraft. This fleet ranges from 3.4m aluminium punts to our largest offshore vessel that is 24m and operates out to 200nm offshore.

The QBFP monitor compliance with State and Commonwealth legislation through field enforcement, investigation, surveillance, and inspection activities. They also undertake investigations of fisheries, fisheries habitat, and small craft safety non-compliance as well as education services that enable the community to develop knowledge and understanding of fisheries resource management and small craft safety. With over 160,000 recreational and 13,000 commercial vessels in use, compliance with laws is necessary to ensure both the safe use of waterways and the sustainability of our fisheries resources.

As part of the QBFP vessel replacement program the 6.5m vessel ‘Mentana’ located in Karumba has been identified as being due for replacement. This vessel is operated in Gulf of Carpentaria waters from the Norman River in Karumba north to Kowanyama and west to the Queensland - Northern Territory border. The vessel is used to ensure service delivery to the public and compliance activities.

title: Expansion of Bamaga Sewer Ponds
description:
The Northern Peninsular Area Regional Council is seeking proposals from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to carry out works to expand the capacity of the Sewer Treatment Ponds in Bamaga.

Concept designs are attached. NPARC will accept variation to these designs.

The work involves the increase in size of the 2 primary lagoons and the addition of a 3rd secondary lagoon.

Other works include: New interconnecting pipework and valves; new bypass pipelines, relocation of a rising main, relocation of electrical wires, fencing and landscaping works.

In addition, the contractor will provide an improved screening and grit removal system at the inlet to the STP. The design and type of these systems has not been specified and therefore the Contractor can propose the most cost effective system, with a focus on total life-cycle costs.

There is some desludging work required in the existing ponds. That work can be delivered as a variation, using unit rates.

title: Palm Island Aboriginal Council - 2025 Natural Disaster Reconstruction Civil Works
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council wishes to invite suitably qualified and experienced civil contractors to submit tenders for this package of natural disaster reconstruction works. The works consist of sealed and unsealed road repairs, earthworks and civil drainage works. It is anticipated that the works will commence in 2026 and be completed no later than the end of June 2027. Contractors will need to consider the North Queensland wet season and whether the scope of works can be completed in 2026 or whether a second mobilisation will be required in following the upcoming wet season 2027.

Prospective Tenderers should note that access to Palm Island is by barge, ferry and air services, and should familiarise themselves with the available services prior to submitting their tender. Tenderers should also familiarise themselves with local accommodation providers and confirm the availability of sufficient accommodation to house their crews for the duration of the works.

Tenderers who do not have recent construction experience on Palm Island are recommended to arrange a site visit during the tender period and to reflect their observations in their methodology.

Tenderers are to assume that all works other than "bulk fill – local" are inclusive of materials supplied by the Contractor, and are advised to familiarise themselves with barge arrangements and any upcoming constraints on barge service availability. All quarry materials, including gravel and imported bulk fill, are to be supplied by the Contractor to the laydown area at Wallaby Point (18°43'01"S 146°35'57"E). For items identified in the tender documents as "bulk fill – local," Tenderers may assume that locally available material can be collected free of charge from the same location. Contractors are to make their own arrangements for carting material from the laydown area to site.

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our coastal fringe extends from Wallaga Lake in the north to Cape Howe and the Victorian border in the south. Collectively this 225-kilometre section forms the beautiful Sapphire Coast, the heart of Australia’s Coastal Wilderness.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. publicQuestions.question:
Dear Council Tender Team,

We are currently preparing our tender submission for TEN16777 – Rehabilitation of Sewer Mains, Cleaning, CCTV Inspections, Condition Assessment, Lining & Associated Works.

Having reviewed the tender documentation and the clarifications already published on VendorPanel, we request clarification on the following items to ensure our Schedule of Rates is prepared in accordance with Council’s intended delivery and payment arrangements.

1. Indicative quantities and sewer segment lengths

Council has advised that the works will be issued as a single-block work package each financial year and that the current financial year budget is approximately $500,000.

Can Council please provide, if available, indicative quantities for the anticipated 2026/27 works, including approximate sewer main lengths by diameter, number of sewer segments, anticipated number of house service connections/junctions, and approximate quantities of cleaning/CCTV works?

If these quantities are not yet available, can Council provide historical annual quantities or a representative previous work package to assist tenderers in establishing appropriate Schedule of Rates pricing?

2. Minimum work package quantities / mobilisation

Schedule 3 requires unit rates that incorporate mobilisation/demobilisation, equipment setup and associated activities.

Within the annual work package, will Council establish minimum work package quantities, minimum chargeable liner lengths, mobilisation/demobilisation items or minimum call-out values?

If not, can Council please advise whether tendered per-metre rates are expected to cover mobilisation and setup costs irrespective of the length or quantity of individual sewer segments instructed?

3. Traffic management

The tender documentation requires traffic control to be incorporated into various cleaning, assessment and lining activities while also providing separate Traffic Management items within the Schedule of Rates.

Can Council please clarify the intended application of the separate Traffic Management Schedule items and provide an indication, if available, of the anticipated proportion of works likely to require additional traffic management, particularly works on higher-volume roads, controlled arterial roads, lane closures or other complex traffic environments?

4. Abnormal cleaning and obstruction removal

Where sewer cleaning encounters conditions materially beyond normal pressure cleaning and root cutting, such as significant deposits, concrete, major obstructions or other conditions requiring specialist or extended removal methods, will these additional works be separately authorised and paid under an applicable Schedule of Rates item or treated as a variation?

5. Major bypass pumping

Where sewer flows cannot be adequately controlled using normal bunging or flow-control methods and substantial temporary bypass pumping is required to undertake cleaning, CCTV or lining works, can Council please confirm whether major bypass pumping is deemed included within the applicable scheduled rates or will be separately authorised and payable based on the site-specific requirements?

6. Schedule of Rates – basis of payment

The tender documentation describes TEN16777 as a Schedule of Rates contract, and the Technical Specification provides for payment based on the unit rate for quantities ordered and accepted.

Can Council please confirm that the Contract is intended to operate on a remeasurable Schedule of Rates basis, with payment based on the actual quantities of work ordered and completed at the applicable tendered unit rates, notwithstanding the fixed lump sum wording contained within the amended Clause 3 of the General Conditions of Contract?

Thank you for your assistance. We look forward to Council’s clarification.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council does not have confirmed quantities for the 2026/27 works package at this stage. As a guide only, a typical annual package may include Cleaning, CCTV and Relining of the following assets:

•	80-100 sewer segments of 150mm diameter (approximately 2,500m to 3000m)

•	4-8 sewer segments of 225mm diameter (approximately 200m to 400m)

•	3-6 sewer segments of 300mm diameter (approximately 150m to 300m)

These quantities are indicative only and may vary based on condition assessments, priorities and available budget. Council does not guarantee any minimum quantity, value or distribution of work under the contract.

2. Council intends to issue the annual rehabilitation works as a single work package. Tenderers should include mobilisation, demobilisation, setup and associated costs within their tendered rates. No minimum quantities, minimum liner lengths or minimum call-out values are guaranteed.

3. Traffic management requirements will vary depending on the location and nature of the works. Where external traffic control services are required, the separate Traffic Management items within the Schedule of Rates will apply.

4. Where abnormal cleaning or specialist obstruction removal is required, the work will be subject to Council approval and paid under an applicable Schedule of Rates item or treated as a variation.

5. Major bypass pumping will be assessed on a site-specific basis and, where approved by Council, will be separately authorised and paid under the relevant Schedule of Rates item or as a variation.

6. The contract is intended to operate as a Schedule of Rates contract, with payment based on the actual quantities of work completed and accepted at the tendered unit rates.

title: Supply and Delivery of Waste Handling Wheel Loader
description:
Hinchinbrook Shire Council (Council) invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced suppliers for the supply and delivery of a waste handling wheel loader for use within Council’s Waste and Resource Recovery operations.

The procurement forms part of Council’s fleet replacement program and is intended to replace Council’s existing 2019 JCB 427HT Wheel Loader (Asset No. PA00466). The replacement machine will undertake demanding waste handling activities including the loading, pushing, stockpiling and movement of waste and recyclable materials, together with the formation and maintenance of batters, pads and other operational areas within Council’s waste facilities.

Due to the harsh operating environment, Council requires a robust, fit-for-purpose machine specifically designed or suitably equipped for continuous waste and landfill operations. The proposed machine is to have an operating weight generally within the 16–20 tonne range and incorporate appropriate waste-handling features including solid heavy-duty tyres, enhanced underbody and component guarding, heavy-duty cooling and filtration systems, a pressurised operator cabin with appropriate air filtration, and suitable attachments for Council’s operational requirements.

Particular importance will be placed on the machine’s ability to operate reliably within dusty and debris-intensive waste environments, including the protection of hydraulic, electrical, driveline and other vulnerable components from damage.

Tenderers are required to provide a complete machine that satisfies the technical requirements detailed within the Tender Documents and clearly identify any departures, optional equipment or alternative solutions proposed. Council will also consider whole-of-life operational requirements, including warranty, servicing, maintenance, parts availability and access to suitable technical support.

Council is seeking a reliable and practical solution that provides a safe and comfortable operating environment, strong waste-handling capability, durability and ongoing serviceability throughout the expected operational life of the machine.

Tenderers are required to provide a complete machine that satisfies the technical requirements detailed within the Tender Documents and clearly identify any departures, optional equipment or alternative solutions proposed. Council will also consider whole-of-life operational requirements, including warranty, servicing, maintenance, parts availability and access to suitable technical support.

Council is seeking a reliable and practical solution that provides a safe and comfortable operating environment, strong waste-handling capability, durability and ongoing serviceability throughout the expected operational life of the machine.

publicQuestions.question:
-	It would be appreciated if Council could please advise of your target timeframe for the project.

-	It would be appreciated if Council could please provide an indication of budget or budget range for the project as we suggest this will allow submissions to be more tailored and aligned with Council’s expectation?

-	In relation to the Scope of works item:

“A fit for purpose risk assessment will be required to inform the provisions of the Planning Scheme relating to natural hazard risk (flood, bushfire, landslide and coastal hazards). The Integrating State Interests in a Planning Scheme guidance material includes information on the steps involved in undertaking a fit for purpose risk assessment”,

we seek Council's confirmation that whilst the planning risk assessment is part of the Scope of Works, the risk assessments based on the technical studies for flood, bushfire, landslide and coastal hazards, have been completed by the relevant technical expert and will be provided to the successful consultant as background material?'
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for the questions. Council provides the following clarification:

1. Project timeframe

Council requires the draft Planning Scheme Amendment to be completed and submitted for State Interest Review by June 2027. Tenderers should provide a project program demonstrating how this milestone will be achieved, including sufficient time for technical studies, drafting, Council review and Councilor workshops.

2. Project budget

Council has not prescribed a fixed budget or budget range. Tenderers are requested to provide a competitive fee proposal based on the Scope of Works, clearly identifying key project stages, assumptions, exclusions and any additional or optional services.

3. Natural hazard risk assessment

Council confirms that the requirements differ across the four natural hazards:

Flood – the technical study has been completed and will be provided to the successful consultant.

Coastal hazards – the technical study has been completed and will be provided to the successful consultant.

Bushfire – a technical study and associated risk assessment are required to be completed as part of this commission.

Landslide – a technical study and associated risk assessment are required to be completed as part of this commission.

The successful consultant will be responsible for undertaking the overall fit-for-purpose planning risk assessment and integrating the outcomes of all four hazard assessments into the Planning Scheme in accordance with the relevant State interests and guidance material.

Previous housing engagement: Council has undertaken previous community and stakeholder engagement through strategic planning, housing and community planning activities. Relevant available reports and consultation outcomes will be provided to the successful consultant. Project-specific housing engagement will still be required.

Existing stakeholder relationships: Council has established relationships with relevant community, industry, service providers, major employers and State Government agencies. Council will assist with stakeholder identification and introductions where appropriate. The Study Team will be responsible for maintaining the project stakeholder register and managing engagement.

First Nations engagement protocols: Council has existing relationships with Traditional Owners and First Nations organisations. Council will assist the Study Team in identifying appropriate representatives and engagement protocols to ensure consultation is culturally appropriate.

First Nations engagement responsibilities: This will be a shared responsibility. Council will facilitate introductions and provide guidance on existing relationships and protocols. The Study Team will be responsible for preparing, facilitating, documenting and reporting on the engagement and incorporating outcomes into the project.

Consultation responsibilities: Council will assist with stakeholder identification, introductions, Council communication channels, elected-member engagement and State agency coordination. The Study Team will be responsible for engagement planning, materials, logistics, facilitation, surveys, recording outcomes, analysis and consultation reporting.

Stakeholder contact information: Council will provide or facilitate appropriate stakeholder contacts where permitted, subject to privacy requirements. The Study Team will manage the project-specific contact database.

Venues and logistics: Council can assist with access to suitable Council facilities where available. The Study Team should allow for coordination and delivery of consultation activities within its proposal.

Engagement materials: The Study Team will prepare consultation and engagement materials, subject to Council review and approval before release.

Workshops and community sessions: The Study Team should allow for professional facilitation of workshops, meetings and community sessions. Council officers will participate where appropriate.

Online engagement: The Study Team will be responsible for preparation and administration of online engagement and surveys. Council can assist with promotion through its existing communication channels.

Elected representatives: Council will coordinate access to elected representatives. The Study Team should allow for preparation and facilitation of relevant Councillor workshops and briefings.

State Government agencies: Council will assist with formal agency coordination. The Study Team will be responsible for technical input, participation, follow-up and incorporation of State agency feedback.

Consultation outcomes: The Study Team will be responsible for recording and analysing consultation outcomes and demonstrating how findings have informed the Housing Needs Assessment, Housing Strategy and Planning Scheme amendment.

Preliminary consultation: Tenderers should assume that project-specific preliminary consultation remains within the scope of the successful Study Team. Council will provide relevant previous consultation material where available as background information.

Council participation: Council officers will participate in key workshops, Councillor briefings and major engagement activities where appropriate. Tenderers should nevertheless allow for the Study Team to independently facilitate engagement activities.

Fee proposal: Tenderers should include sufficient allowance for the consultation and engagement required to deliver the project. The final engagement program and methodology will be agreed with Council during project inception.

title: North Johnstone River Bridge Replacement
description:
This tender is seeking to engage a Principal Contractor to undertake the construction of the North Johnstone River Bridge Replacement project, which involves the construction of a new single track railway bridge over the North Johnstone River, approximately 4 km north of Innisfail on the North Coast Line (NCL) in Far North Queensland.

The existing bridge, located at approximately chainage 1597.870 km, has been in service for approximately 100 years and currently supports both passenger and freight rail operations. Due to age related deterioration, increasing maintenance demands and ongoing structural performance concerns, Queensland Rail has initiated the replacement of the existing structure to ensure the continued safe and reliable operation of the rail network.

The project has been developed as an offline bridge replacement to minimise disruption to rail operations during construction and to improve constructability and safety outcomes. The proposed works include significant enabling and temporary works to facilitate construction and demolition adjacent to a live operational railway and within a constrained river environment, construction of a new rail alignment offset approximately 17 m downstream of the existing bridge, construction of a new six-span prestressed concrete rail bridge, associated earthworks, drainage, rail infrastructure, rail maintenance access roads (RMAR), utility relocations, temporary works, demolition of the existing bridge structure, and reinstatement works.

Our 7,500 strong workforce delivers services across our South East Queensland and Regional networks, including Travel and Tourism services and Regional Freight.

The Regional networks commuter and rail tourism markets are serviced by the Travel and Tourism products. These comprise eight services connecting Regional communities across Queensland with other Regional centres and the South East Queensland corner. These services support the Queensland tourism industry through the provision of unique rail tourism experiences including special events and charters through the operation of a small fleet of heritage services.

Our Regional networks and Freight team provides rail access for freight operators and other Queensland Rail supply chain customers to enable the critical transport of resources and general freight across the state.

We are proud of the role we play in providing vital passenger and freight services and we are dedicated to ensuring that our systems, procedures and practices reflect the highest standards of corporate governance.

title: Long-Term Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country
description:
Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country (Long-Term) - WS5659204351

The Coordinator of Energy has determined, under clause 3.11A.4 of the Electricity System Market (ESM) Rules, to trigger a Non-Co-optimised Essential System Services (NCESS) procurement process by Western Power for Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country.

The proposed services aim to address reliability and system strength concerns during planned or unplanned outage events affecting one or more 132 kV transmission lines supplying the North Country.

Call for NCESS Submissions

Western Power invites NCESS Submissions from prospective NCESS providers to deliver Reliability Services and/or System Strength Services located in the North Country. The North Country is defined as the area supplied by the Rangeway, Geraldton and Chapman substations.

This tender relates to the Long-Term contract term option (10-25 year terms). Proponents may offer a solution that fully or partially meets the requirements for either service (or both).

Activation requirements, performance measures, preferred connection locations and other technical requirements are set out in the Final NCESS Service Specification.

Queries may be submitted by email to emerging.technology.portfolio@westernpower.com.au or via the Q&A function in the VendorPanel portal.

Please submit NCESS Submissions via VendorPanel no later than 5:00pm (AWST) on 1 February 2027.

Interested NCESS providers should register with VendorPanel to be informed of whether any supporting documentation such as clarifications to questions may be published.

title: TRC000584 Southern Cross Oval Light Upgrade
description:
Southern Cross Reserve Oval is a Council-managed, multi-use sporting facility comprising a single irrigated oval with a turf wicket block and supporting amenities. The oval is classified as a Class 1 sports field within Toowoomba Regional Council’s sports field hierarchy due to the quality of the playing surface, the level of supporting amenities and the availability of oval lighting.

The facility supports a high level of seasonal community sport. During summer, it is used for Toowoomba A Grade Cricket competition, including limited-over, night fixtures and T20 night games. During winter, the oval supports Downs Rugby competition and AFL Darling Downs competition. Key user groups operating from Southern Cross Reserve Oval include Toowoomba Cricket Incorporated, Bears Rugby Union and South Toowoomba Bombers AFL.

The current oval lighting configuration includes three 30 metre TP EK30M GM poles, and three 25 metre TP EK25M GM poles, fitted with a combination of Philips MVP507 luminaires and Philips MVF403 ArenaVision luminaires.

Council has approved a capital budget allocation for the replacement of luminaires at Southern Cross Reserve Oval as part of the Sports Lighting Replacement Program. The upgrade is scheduled for delivery during the 2026–2027 financial year and is intended to improve lighting performance, reliability, energy efficiency and ongoing serviceability while supporting continued community sport use of the facility.

Toowoomba Regional Council (TRC) invites submissions from suitably qualified and experienced Principal Contractors for the design, supply, installation, management and coordination of the replacement of sports oval luminaries at Southern Cross Reserve.

title: MidCoast Council Concrete Processing Tender Waste Services
description:
MidCoast Council is seeking an experienced contractor to crush, grind, screen and process stockpiled concrete, bricks and tiles under a five-year, non-exclusive, as-required contract.

Processing will be undertaken at Council’s Waste Management Centres at Taree, Gloucester and Stroud. The Contractor will produce the following finished products:

20 mm minus road base;

40 mm minus road base; and

80 mm minus cobbles.

The Contractor must provide all personnel, supervision, mobile processing plant, loaders, screening and magnetic-separation equipment, water-based dust suppression, traffic controls, site establishment, product testing, stockpiling, cleaning, reporting and demobilisation required to complete each processing occurrence.

For standard Service Requests, the Contractor must commence site establishment within 21 calendar days. For urgent Service Requests, commencement is required within seven calendar days, with up to four urgent requests permitted each Contract Year.

The services require physical attendance at the nominated facilities and cannot be provided remotely. Council does not guarantee any minimum quantity, number of processing occurrences, product-grade mix or expenditure.
