10: Ovens-Murray
11: Western District
12: Wimmera

publicQuestions.question: The Brief #15 notes attachments to be found on vendorpanel, however the documents aren't available. Please advise if these will be provided as part of the RFQ process
publicQuestions.answer: Apologies, these will be uploaded as soon as possible.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there,

Are you able to provide a budget range to help guide our submissions?

The site is complex and a budget range will help support an understanding of the expectations around further specialist technical input from environmental and other services on top of masterplanning services.

Many thanks,
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello consultancies

I have had two requests for an indicative budget and whilst we thought we would leave it open ended it seems that a range is required to assist with scoping the project, acknowledging it is a complex one. Our budget range is $150,000 to $190,000 ex GST.

regards

Kathy

publicQuestions.question: Hi Eddie, addendum 3 mentions conflicting dates for the second site inspection (26/08 in the text & 28/08 in the table) Can you please confirm? Many thanks
publicQuestions.answer: The second site visit is scheduled for next Wednesday 26 August at 1pm.

publicQuestions.question: Hello can you confirm the alternative time for the Site inspection - is it the Wednesday 26th? I note on the addendum notice it indicates the 26th and 28th at 1pm in the table.
publicQuestions.answer: Sorry for any confusion. Second site inspection will be Wednesday 26 August 1-3pm.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI Question 1: Flood risk and integrated water management

The site is subject to the Land Subject to Inundation Overlay and adjoins Bendigo Creek. Will respondents be expected to address flood risk as part of the scope?

RFI Question 2: Access and movement

Could the City clarify the expected scope of access, movement and car parking component within the Master Plan? Will specialist transport expertise be required, or is this expected to be addressed at a high level within the urban design response?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question 1: Yes, the constraints of the LSIO should be taken into account.

Question 2: Indicative pedestrian/cycling access through the site linking into public spaces and broader networks should form part of the master plan. Vehicle access (most likely through the existing gate entry/ies) including for emergency vehicles is required. It is anticipated that parking will need to be provided to some extent but given there is a large public car park to the east and some on street parking, hopefully on-site parking can be discreet and minimised. We do not think the scrutiny of the project by traffic expertise is warranted at master plan stage and would expect that those issues are dealt with later.

publicQuestions.question:
From a review of the brief, it is our assessment that the scope of works is misaligned with the budget of $150-190k.

Can you please confirm if the price is fixed or the scope? Would you be open to a non-conforming bid with a greater fee or a more confined scope?
publicQuestions.answer: Thanks for this question and an important one to clarify. The budget is indicative only. The scope is fixed and a submission needs to be received that conforms with the scope at whatever price/costing you consider is necessary to meet the scope. A greater fee outside of the indicative budget will certainly be considered. You may also choose to put in a non-conforming submission that doesn't meet the full scope but meets the indicative budget. The non-conforming submission is additional to a conforming submission and won't be considered if it is a stand along submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

Regarding Q1 in my previous RFI. On Page 16 of the RFQ under Key Stakeholders:

Council’s Project Manager is the primary contact and is responsible for the day-to-day requirements of the project, including, but not limited to:

• Confirm the project brief, scope of the project and methodology

• Following procurement, engage organisations to complete technical investigations

• Assist with onsite community consultations

• Engagement of Councillors and Council.

Cheers,

James
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi James

That would be if we felt there was something that might need further investigation such as some contamination advice if a proposal was to breach the capping of the ground surface or perhaps some engineering advice on the structural integrity of one of the buildings. I think at master plan stage this scenario is not likely but just in case something arose.

In regard to your other questions, they have disappeared off Vendor Panel after I responded to Q1 privately. Could you repost the rest of the questions as I will respond publicly to those?

many thanks

Kathy

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

1. The RFQ notes that Council will engage organisations to undertake technical investigations. Can Council confirm which investigations are anticipated and whether the consultant is expected to coordinate and incorporate these findings rather than undertake the investigations?

2.Can Council confirm the anticipated number and format of consultation activities for Stages 1 and 2? Can the listed stakeholders be engaged through a combination of grouped sessions, individual meetings and online engagement?

3. Section 13 identifies an estimated project duration of 10–12 months and lists Milestones 1–4 against Weeks 1, 9, 20 and 35 under a column headed ‘Start date’. Could Council please confirm whether these weeks represent the commencement of each subsequent stage, or the required completion dates for the stated milestone outputs?

4. Can Council confirm the expected Heritage Victoria review process for the Options Analysis and Heritage Interpretation Plan, including the anticipated number of review rounds and whether Council will facilitate the referral?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. If there were additional investigations necessary to enable a fulsome design response then Council would engage relevant expertise to deliver this. It is anticipated that for master planning we have sufficient information but perhaps we may need to investigate some structural integrity of something or seek some further clarity around contamination such as breaking through the capping. Council will coordinate this work if it is required and it would be at the discretion of Council and funded by Council.

2. Consultation Stage 1 - one group session would suffice and if they are unable to make that then online engagement. Council can assist with this. Consultation Stage 2 - up to the consultancy as to how they can effectively reach the public such as drop-in sessions which Council can assist with any format. We also have several media avenues to reach out such as Facebook page and website, local paper. Group session with key stakeholder groups as per Stage 1.

3. This is the anticipated start dates but acknowledge that there will be some crossover with dates. They are not hard and fast but indictive so that we all have some understanding of the possible length of the project. This can be further discussed at an inception meeting and negotiated, with the understanding that there is flexibility given the unknowns of the project.

4. Council will facilitate the referral to HV. I am seeking some clarity from them as to the scope of this work given the permit conditions are theirs and I will post that advice as soon as I get it. If you have a heritage consultant already on board, they should have an idea of this. I would refer to your heritage consultant as to how may rounds this would normally entail with HV. I understand they are very particular and accounting for the heritage significance of the site.

publicQuestions.question: For Evaluation Criteria Response 1.2, can you please confirm if you would like this information for all key personell listed on the project or just the leadership team? Can you also confirm if this extends to the subconsultants.
publicQuestions.answer: We would like to know what experience the team can bring to the project whether that is key personnel and/or leadership team and this extends to sub-consultants. If the leadership team has good experience on similar projects but the key personnel on the project don't then we would want to know how involved and what oversight the leadership team will have. This is a high-profile project for the City and will have a lot of scrutiny by the Councillors and community and we would like that there is an experienced and strong leadership team involved and leading that public/Council interface when required.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

Can you please confirm if there is an existing feature & level survey for the subject site?

Also, can you confirm if Council has undertaken any economics assessments related to retail demand in the area?

Thanks!
publicQuestions.answer:
There is an existing feature survey that was undertaken as part of the Environmental Audit as part of the remediation works. I am endeavouring to get access from the Auditor to the document so it can be shared on Vendor Panel hopefully tomorrow. I will keep you posted. This will be sufficient as an interim document, however, I will get an updated feature survey with revised levels done as soon as possible.

There are no economic assessments related to retail demand in the immediate area, however, I can tell you that there are vacant shops in the city centre. The Gasworks site does however, have a different context and possibly more nuanced potential than that of a site within the city.

publicQuestions.question: For Evaluation Criteria Response 1.1, can you confirm if you would accept 3 project examples that are Non-City of Greater Bendigo
publicQuestions.answer: Yes of course. That wording is a bit confusing. Three non-Bendigo projects are absolutely acceptable. We accept that not all consultancies will have done work in Bendigo and it is not necessary to have done so. It's about capability and not whether past projects are local.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello,

Please confirm whether Council will arrange and fund DJAARA participation and cultural advisory services, or whether the consultant is expected to engage DJAARA directly.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will initiate contact with DJAARA for their involvement. Costs associated with DJAARA will be the responsibility of Council. There is no formal protocol for engaging with DJAARA. It has been and continues to be a very collaborative relationship on design projects.

publicQuestions.question:
1. The Assumptions (Item 11) state that consultants' attendance at engagement activities is "to be confirmed" and that "an hourly rate to be provided to participate in engagement." Can you please confirm whether attendance at consultation and workshops is to be included in the fixed milestone fees, or reimbursed separately at the hourly rates provided in the Schedule of Rates.

2. The brief treats economic viability as a "foundational requirement," referring to revenue streams, tenant and activation mix, and a sustainable operating model. Can you please confirm whether the project requires a full business case or financial model, or a strategic economic and activation framework to guide the Options Analysis and Master Plan.

3. The Options Analysis and Master Plan ask for "approximate costs" and "indicative capital implications." Can you please confirm whether a quantity surveyor cost plan is anticipated within the fee, and if so, to what level of detail.

5. Early engagement with DJAARA is a required part of the scope. Can you please confirm whether Council has an existing engagement agreement or protocol, and whether any DJAARA participation fees are to be borne by Council.

6. In the Schedule of Rates and Basis of Payment, "Consultation Stage 1 completed" appears under both Milestone 1 and Milestone 2. Can you please confirm which milestone this deliverable sits under for payment.

7. A Heritage Impact Assessment is listed as a Stage 3 deliverable. Please confirm whether it must be prepared to permit-grade standard (to Heritage Victoria requirements), or as a high-level assessment to inform the concept options.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. I think you should include a fee for consultant attendance at the engagement activities. Also provide an hourly rate in case there will be additional attendance required.

2. The City is not after a business case at this stage. A framework to guide potential options is sufficient which could be tested at the next stage through a business case.

3. A quantity surveyor is not required. Indicative costs based on previous experience is sufficient at this stage.

5. Costs with DJAARA involvement will be the responsibility of Council. There is no agreement of protocol in place. Council will facilitate the initial engagement with DJAARA.

6. Apologies, that Consultation Stage 1 sits within Milestone 1 and will be scheduled for payment accordingly.

7. The Heritage Impact Assessment should be high level and consider the impacts on heritage within the concept options.

publicQuestions.question:
We have a question regarding 2.1 Demonstrated organisations capacity to provide resources.

The response schedule requests a list of current projects but also mentions project in the last 5 yearse and provides space for three projects only. Can Council please confirm whether tenderers are required to list all current projects or three representative current projects?
publicQuestions.answer: Three projects completed in the past 5 years that you would like to put forward as good examples of master planning projects that share some similarities.

publicQuestions.question: Addendum no. 3 specifies two different dates for the site visit - the 26th and the 28th of August. Can you please confirm which date is correct?
publicQuestions.answer: The second site visit is today 26 August at 1pm. This was clarified last week.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning. We would appreciate clarification on the following questions to support the preparation of our tender submission: 1. Does Council have any preconceived views on what they would like to see developed on the site? 2. Is Council considering private investment as part of the site's future, or is the expectation that development will be government-funded? 3. Would Council consider selling or leasing parts of the site to facilitate redevelopment?

Thank you in advance.
publicQuestions.answer: Council has no preconceived views on what mix of uses would occupy the site. What the model for development is has not been decided and Council is open to all options as they arise throughout the options analysis and master plan stage.

publicQuestions.question:
Section 13. Project Timeframe:

This section provides indicative duration for the project.

Question: In order to consider project resourcing, please clarify Council's preferred start date.

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer: I would anticipate a start date around mid-October and Consultation Stage 1 with key stakeholder groups to commence soon after that.

publicQuestions.question: Could Council please confirm whether tenderers may reproduce and format the Part 4 Response Schedules in their own document style to be inline with our corporate branding. (e.g. formatted in Adobe InDesign), to accommodate our responses. We would ensure that all questions, numbering, sequence and required information are retained exactly as issued, and all applicable page limits are observed.
publicQuestions.answer: Yes you may choose to do this. Just ensure that everything aligns with the questioning, numbering and required information as in the template to allow for the full evaluation.

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification on Question 2.1 (Capacity)

We note a similar question has been raised on this item, but are seeking further clarification on the following:

1.	Question 2.1 states "capacity to provide resources to deliver similar projects over the last 5 years," while the accompanying instruction asks tenderers to "provide a list of current projects, their value and expected completion dates." Could Council please confirm whether this question is seeking evidence of past project experience (similar to Question 1.1) or the tenderer's current workload/capacity to take on this contract?

2.	Where a tender is being submitted by a multi-disciplinary team (e.g. a lead consultant supported by sub-consultants or partner practices), could Council please confirm whether Question 2.1 should be answered by the lead consultant only, or whether each practice/sub-consultant in the team is required to provide their own capacity details?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The aim of this questioning is to ascertain whether the tenderer has delivered similar projects (although accepting that this project has some unique aspects) and there is the capacity to deliver projects of a similar nature in the past ie. there is a capacity of expertise/resources to deliver something similar. Not asking about your current workload capacity.

2. This should be answered by the lead consultant. If sub-consultants have experience/capability then this could be added in the attachments to support that.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

can Council confirm if CV's are counted in the 10-15 page limit?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer: CVs can be provided outside of the 10-15 page limit.

publicQuestions.question: Is there a contract or consultancy agreement that we can review prior to submission? Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: There is a link in the Attachment 2 RFQ at page 2 which will provide the base conditions.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

I was wondering if it's possible for Council to share the previous master planning works undertaken by Tonkin Zulaikha Greer?

With thanks.
publicQuestions.answer: The link to the Tonkin Zulaikha Greer work has been refreshed in a new addendum.

publicQuestions.question:
Question 1.5 asks for our Past performance for the last 3 years. Can you please clarify what kind of response you are expecting for this question? E.g are you asking about our project performance?

How does this question differ from 2.1?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
There have been a few questions around Part 4, Section 1 Capability and Section 2 Capacity. Procurement have provided some clarity on this as follows:

1. Capability is requesting examples of past work that shows your capability to complete this work. These examples are selective and should represent work you have completed of a similar nature and may be used as reference checks for short listed organisations. (these don't need to be current projects and should be of a similar nature to the works requested in the RFQ)

2. Capacity is requesting details of your current workload with completion dates and how much each project would represent as a percentage of your workload capacity. This is to demonstrate that you have the capacity to take on this project within the agreed timeframe.

If you need any further clarity, please send through a query.

thanks

Kathy

publicQuestions.question: Can you confirm if there is an architect or urban designer on selection/assessment panel.
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes there is an architect/urban designer on the selection panel and also myself as a landscape architect/strategic planner.

regards

Kathy

publicQuestions.question:
Hello. Noting there has already been a number of questions relating to the Part 4 Response Schedule, can you please provide further clarifications on the following:

Criterion 1.2 Could you confirm whether this criterion asks tenderers to nominate a single key person and provide three examples of their relevant experience, or whether it should cover multiple key personnel across the proposed team?

Criterion 1.5 The criterion notes that "past performance for the last 3 years may be included when evaluating this criterion." Could you clarify what type of response Council expects here, and how it is intended to differ from the project examples provided under Criterion 1.1?

Criterion 2.1 Could you confirm whether this criterion asks for all current projects of the tendering entity, or a representative selection? Could you also confirm what "capacity" refers to — for example, the proportion of the practice's overall resource each project currently consumes?

Criterion 2.2 Could you confirm what "capacity" refers to in relation to individual personnel? For example, the proportion of that person's available time allocated to this commission, or their availability more generally. Could you also confirm whether sub-consultant personnel should be included in this table alongside the tendering entity's own staff.

Schedule of Rates The schedule lists rates for Principal, Senior staff and Junior staff. Could you confirm whether tenderers can add rows reflecting their actual staffing structure. Could you also confirm whether sub-consultant rates should be included in this schedule.

Many thanks.
publicQuestions.answer:
Criterion 1.2 - For any key personnel nominated in criterion 2.2, list all of those that were involved in any of the projects listed in 1.2.

Criterion 1.5 - No response required here. Council reserves the right to use previous projects not listed by the Tenderer as examples of previous capability.

Criterion 2.1 - Preference is to list all current workloads to allow the City to understand the Tenderers capacity to undertake this project in a timely manner. We would prefer all projects to be listed or alternatively if this exceeds 10, a representative selection of key projects the key personnel will be working on. Under capacity for this item please note the practice's overall resources as a percentage of commitment to each contract.

Criterion 2.2 - Capacity here should represent the individual's commitment to this project as a percentage of their overall workload (eg 1 out of 4 projects on the go 25%). You can list subcontractors however don't assign a percentage to them as you possibly can't keep them to that value.

Schedule of Rates - Yes, you can add as many new lines as you see fit. This should include all sub consultancies as well.

publicQuestions.question: Are the cover pages, contents page and cover letter included in the 15 page count? Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: The 15 page limit does not include the cover pages, contents page or cover letter although it is preferred that the cover letter is no more than two pages.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

can you please elaborate on the following response? Would you like us to nominate an additional 3 projects and outline who from our proposed key personnel have worked on those projects or would you like us to submit 3 projects per key personnel?

Criterion 1.2 - For any key personnel nominated in criterion 2.2, list all of those that were involved in any of the projects listed in 1.2.
publicQuestions.answer:
2.2 This should list the key personnel that will be working on the Gasworks project and their capacity to be involved in the project. These personnel may not have worked on the projects listed in 2.1 as this is organisational wide. We want to know who will be the key personnel for this project. For example if a Principal Architect or Director is to have 10% involvement in the project and the graduate architect is to have 90% involvement. This is to give us an idea of the level of oversight by senior personnel, input of experienced and less experienced so we can get an understanding of the level of expertise across the life of the project.

1.2 List three projects of the organisation and the key personnel that worked on these projects. They may not align with the projects you have put forward for the organisation's capability or capacity at 1.2 or 2.1. It may be that some key personnel were involved in these projects or none of them had involvement with any of the projects listed. It gives us an idea of the experience of the key personnel you are putting forward to do the Gasworks project.

publicQuestions.question: We were unable to attend the briefing meeting, is there are chance we can review meeting minutes? Or if there will be another sitting?
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear all,

Thank you for those that attended the briefing held on 1 September 2026 at 2pm.

Council will not be issuing minutes or an addendum for the briefing however below are the questions raised in the session and the responses provided:

Q1: Clarification on the requirement for: Subconsultant - Recreation Planning.

A1: Whilst Recreation Planning was identified as a separate line item under the list of required subconsultants in the RFT, a separate consultant may not be required should the Respondent demonstrate that this discipline is sufficiently addressed through in-house expertise or experience within the team.

It is also noted that Council's Sport Services team will assist with providing information to support a collaborative approach for recreation planning at the site, already having provided some guidance through Appendix 6 in the RFT and identifying key opportunities in alignment with the draft Sport Strategy and Implementation Plan which has recently been put on public exhibition here.

Q2: Definition of Recreation Planning

A2: Recreation Planning in this context relates to the open space planning for the provision of sporting infrastructure at the sites. Recreation Planners are familiar with the planning and design of sporting facilities and the specific requirements of this type of land use.

Q3: Clarification on the consultation scope

A3: Consultants will assist with the preparation of an external-facing consultation package prior to consultation stage (for club/stakeholder meetings and public exhibition) and upon completion of this stage will be provided de-identified consultation data and a consultation summary for consideration and integration into final design concepts.

The lead consultant will not be required to attend external stakeholder meetings, pop-up consultation days or the like. Council's Project Managers and Sport Services team will be the external facing contacts for clubs, sporting groups and the general public. Council will lead the consultation process.

Additional information provided in the briefing:

•	The Master Plans are intended to establish a strategic, long-term vision for each precinct, rather than detailed design or design development. The Ridge Sporting Complex and Parc Menai will be treated as one Master Plan, while the Sylvania Waters/Taren Point Recreation Precinct will be treated as a separate project, with each managed by its own Project Manager within Council. While the projects will be developed independently, it is Council’s intention to identify alignment, synergies and efficiencies in sport and recreation delivery across the Shire, where appropriate across the two Master Plans.

•	Council reiterated that the preference is for 1 lead design consultant to deliver both packages but will consider the award of separate lead design consultants where quality submissions are provided. Consultants may respond to one or both packages.

•	As previously posted on VendorPanel, Cyber Security Insurance is waived for this RFT however the Cyber Security Questionnaire/checklist must be completed.

Please note: Closing date is 24th September at 2pm, Enquiry cut-off date is 22nd September. Please have a fully completed submission by the cut-off date as incomplete submissions will not be considered despite what was implied in the meeting.

publicQuestions.question:
CAD Deliverables Clarification

The tender documentation identifies both the Draft Master Plan and Final Master Plan as requiring submission in CAD format. Could Council please clarify its expectations regarding the CAD deliverable and the intended use of the files?

Our standard approach for strategic master planning is to prepare plans using industry-standard graphic design and publishing software, including Adobe Illustrator and Adobe InDesign. This workflow produces high-quality presentation plans suitable for stakeholder engagement, Council reporting, funding submissions and grant applications, while still allowing accurate spatial planning and design outcomes.

We note that plans prepared directly in CAD software can result in a more technical drawing style and may require additional drafting and graphic production processes to achieve the presentation quality typically expected of master planning documents.

Importantly, Illustrator-based plans can be exported to DWG format, with model space linework and layer information retained and accessible within AutoCAD. As such, it may be possible to satisfy Council's CAD requirements without preparing the master plan entirely within a CAD platform.

Could Council please clarify:

- Whether the requirement for CAD is intended to provide Council with an editable digital file of the final master plan;

- Whether CAD files derived from Illustrator exports would be acceptable;

- Whether Council has a preferred CAD platform or file format (e.g. DWG, DXF); and

- Whether there is a specific operational or asset management purpose for requiring CAD deliverables.

Understanding Council's intended use of the CAD files will assist tenderers in proposing the most appropriate and cost-effective approach to delivering the master plan. Thank you in advance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council requires the Draft Master Plan and Final Master Plan to be submitted in editable CAD format (DWG) in accordance with the RFQ requirements.

In response to your specific questions:

1. Whether the requirement for CAD is intended to provide Council with an editable digital file of the final master plan

Yes. Council requires editable CAD files of both the Draft and Final Master Plan to support future planning, concept development, staging reviews, grant funding applications and subsequent design activities.

2. Whether CAD files derived from Illustrator exports would be acceptable

Tenderers may utilise their preferred software and workflows during development of the master plan. However, the submitted deliverable must be an editable DWG file that accurately represents the adopted master plan and is suitable for future use and modification by Council and future consultants.

3. Whether Council has a preferred CAD platform or file format

Council requires submission of the Draft and Final Master Plan in DWG format.

4. Whether there is a specific operational or asset management purpose for requiring CAD deliverables

The purpose of the CAD deliverables is to ensure Council retains an editable spatial representation of the adopted master plan that can be utilised for future planning, concept refinement, staging assessments, funding applications and subsequent project development.

Council acknowledges that presentation-quality master plans are often produced using a range of software platforms. However, regardless of the software used during plan development, the Draft and Final Master Plan must be provided as editable DWG files in accordance with the RFQ requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 1 – Status of Concept Plan Review and Future Facility Provision

Council has provided the Barmaryee Multisport Precinct Concept Plan Review 2024 which identifies preferred future infrastructure including rugby union, AFL, cricket, running track and beach volleyball facilities.

Can Council confirm whether the findings, priorities, facility allocations and future development opportunities identified within the Concept Plan Review represent Council's endorsed strategic position and preferred development direction for the precinct, such that the consultant's role is primarily to validate, refine and spatially accommodate these facilities?

Alternatively, is Council seeking the successful consultant to independently reassess facility requirements, undertake option analysis and prioritisation, and potentially recommend materially different outcomes based on technical investigations, stakeholder consultation, servicing constraints and affordability considerations?

RFI 2 – Sporting Needs Analysis

The Concept Plan Review 2024 references an existing Sporting Needs Analysis used to inform engagement outcomes and future planning for the precinct.

Can Council provide this document to tenderers?

Further, can Council confirm whether the successful consultant is expected to include a specialist sport and recreation consultant to undertake additional participation forecasting, demand modelling or needs assessment activities beyond review of existing Council studies and stakeholder engagement outcomes?

RFI 3 – Stakeholder Engagement Expectations

The Concept Plan Review 2024 identifies previous community surveys, stakeholder engagement activities and direct discussions with sporting clubs and user groups.

Can Council clarify whether the consultant is expected to:

a) validate and refine existing stakeholder requirements; or

b) undertake a new consultation process and re-establish stakeholder requirements from first principles?

Please also clarify the minimum stakeholder engagement activities expected as part of this commission to ensure consistency across tender submissions.

RFI 4 – Cost Planning Scope

The Scope requires preparation of planning-level cost estimates and staging strategies.

Can Council confirm whether cost estimates are required only for the preferred Master Plan outcome, or whether alternative layouts, facility configurations and staging options are also expected to be developed, costed and comparatively assessed?

RFI 5 – Traffic Assessment Scope

Can Council clarify whether the traffic assessment is intended to comprise:

a) a strategic review of site access, circulation and parking requirements to support the Master Plan; or

b) a detailed traffic engineering assessment including traffic generation analysis, intersection performance and future event capacity modelling?

RFI 6 – Flooding and Environmental Assessment Scope

We acknowledge Council's previous responses regarding flood and environmental investigations.

Given the supporting information is not available during the tender period and the extent of any further investigations cannot presently be determined, can Council confirm that:

a) tenderers may assume review of existing information and provision of strategic master planning advice only;

b) any additional flood modelling, hydraulic investigations, ecological field surveys, EPBC Act assessments or specialist studies identified as necessary following review of existing information may be treated as provisional sums or variations?

RFI 7 – Site Servicing Capacity

Has Council undertaken any previous investigations into utility servicing capacity for future expansion of the precinct, including potable water, irrigation water, sewer, electrical and communications infrastructure?

If so, can relevant studies and available servicing information be provided to tenderers?

Further, can Council clarify whether the successful consultant is expected to:

a) undertake a high-level servicing review only; or

b) engage utility authorities and identify network constraints, augmentation requirements and upgrade implications necessary to support the ultimate Master Plan development scenario?
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI 1 – Status of Concept Plan Review and Future Facility Provision

Council confirms that the Barmaryee Multisport Precinct Concept Plan Review 2024 forms the primary basis for preparation of the Master Plan and represents the most recent planning undertaken for the precinct.

The Concept Plan Review 2024 has not been formally endorsed by Council. The consultant is expected to review, validate, refine and optimise the recommendations contained within the Concept Plan Review in accordance with the Scope of Works.

Council is not seeking a new strategic planning exercise or a reassessment of facility requirements from first principles.

RFI2 – Sporting needs analysis

Council will make available relevant background information and previous studies held by Council that are considered applicable to the project. If available, the Sporting Needs Analysis referenced within the Concept Plan Review 2024 will be provided.

Council is not specifically seeking a standalone sporting needs analysis, participation forecasting exercise or demand modelling study. Tenderers should allow within their fee for review of available information, stakeholder engagement and investigations reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI3 – Stakeholder engagement expectations

Council expects the consultant to review previous engagement outcomes and undertake stakeholder engagement activities necessary to validate and refine stakeholder requirements for the Master Plan. Existing consultation outcomes should be considered as key inputs into the process.

The consultant shall engage with the stakeholders identified in the Scope of Works and any additional stakeholders nominated by Council. Tenderers should allow within their fee for all stakeholder engagement activities reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI 4 – Cost Planning Scope

Planning-level cost estimates are required for the preferred Master Plan outcome and associated staging framework. Cost estimates shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of the Scope of Works and be suitable for strategic planning purposes

RFI 5 – Traffic Assessment Scope

The consultant shall undertake a traffic assessment in accordance with the Scope of Works to inform development of the Master Plan, including consideration of site access, circulation, parking and future precinct requirements. Tenderers should allow within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI 6 – Flooding and Environmental Assessment Scope

Existing flood and environmental information held by Council, including the Flood Assessment Report, will be provided where available.

The consultant shall review the information provided and undertake the assessments required by the Scope of Works, allowing within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to inform development of the Master Plan

RFI 7 – Site Servicing Capacity

Relevant servicing information held by Council will be provided where available.

The consultant shall undertake the servicing assessment required by the Scope of Works and allow within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to inform development of the Master Plan

changes.to:
Livingstone Shire Council (Council) invites suitably qualified and experienced consultancy firms to submit a Tender for the preparation of the Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct Master Plan.

The objective of this engagement is to develop a comprehensive, evidence-based and implementable Master Plan that will guide the future planning, development and staged expansion of the Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct as a regionally significant sporting and recreation hub.

The Master Plan will establish a long-term vision for the precinct, incorporating the planning and integration of sporting infrastructure, supporting facilities, transport networks, access, parking, open space, landscaping and associated infrastructure to meet current and future community needs.

The Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct is a strategically important Council-owned facility that currently accommodates a range of sporting and community activities, including Junior Rugby League, Touch Football, Netball, OzTag, Keppel Coast District events and school sporting carnivals.

The precinct has been identified as the preferred location for the future expansion of rectangular sports, including Rugby Union, Outriggers, Volleyball and other compatible sporting and recreation activities. Continued population growth, increasing participation rates and demand for regional sporting infrastructure have created the need for a coordinated and sustainable master planning approach to maximise the precinct's capacity, functionality and long-term value to the community.

The successful Tenderer will be responsible for providing all professional services necessary to deliver the Master Plan in accordance with the Contract, Technical Specification and associated Tender Documents, including project management, stakeholder engagement, site investigations, technical assessments, concept development, implementation planning and final reporting.

The Contract will be administered under AS 4122 – General Conditions of Contract for Consultants, with services delivered in accordance with the staged deliverables specified in the Tender Documents.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Diamantina consists of two main towns Birdsville and Bedourie, with a third town of Betoota.

Bedourie is located 1,600km west of Brisbane, while Birdsville is 200km south of Bedourie and 1,200km from Adelaide.

Our towns have four aircraft services per week on the Brisbane- Mount Isa Circuit. REX (Regional Express) provides this service.

Despite it's size, Birdsville is a well-known destination for many Australian and International visitors. The town hosts one horse race meeting a year, when over 6,000 people swell the town population. It is the start of the famous Birdsville Track, which originally was used as a stock route for moving cattle from Queensland to Southern markets.

Bedourie is the Shire's administration centre. The last ten years has seen its population more than double to 140 people. The town boasts many new amenities including an aquatic centre, hot artesian spa and a community hall. Visitor numbers have increased to over 120,000 per year.

The Shire's wealth lies within its cattle industry, tourism and natural environment. Located within Queensland's Channel Country, bordering South Australia and the Northern Territory, this area is renown for producing prime quality beef. The natural irrigation from the Diamantina and Georgina River Systems is also assisting with developing an organic cattle industry.

We are fortunate that National Parks comprise 25% of our shire's area. The Simpson Desert, Diamantina National Park, (just been named in the top ten National Parks in Australia) and Astrebla National Park all offer unique scenery and wildlife for visitors to experience.

Visit the Diamantina Shire for a unique outback experience.

title: WT25-25/26 Pechey PAC Dosing and WTP Upgrades
description:
Toowoomba Regional Council (TRC) is seeking quotations for the supply and installation of a new Powdered Activated Carbon (PAC) dosing system. This PAC system is to be installed at the Pechey Water Treatment Plant located on Grapetree Road. The scope of works involved are detailed in this document and consists of a mixture of mechanical, electrical, and control systems integration.

The existing PAC dosing system and layout has resulted in issues such as improper powder feed, blockages, inaccurate dosing, and corrosion of the hopper frame. Due to these issues and the age of the unit, Council is looking at replacing this PAC dosing system.

To cater for the new PAC dosing system, several Control System upgrades are required to be undertaken. This includes a PLC Platform upgrade and the installation of a new RIO network. Several other plant modifications are also required including waste pit level instrument control, automated UV duty selection and ATV600 upgrade.

Pechey Water Treatment Plant is located north of Toowoomba in the Pechey State Forest along Grapetree Rd, QLD 4355.

A non-mandatory site inspection is scheduled for Thursday 27th August 2026 at 10am AEST. Offerors are encouraged to attend this site inspection. Refer to the Annexure to Conditions of Offering within the Conditions of Offer document for further information including Council contact details and registering for the site inspection.

publicQuestions.question:
Pensar seeks clarification on the queries below, which relate to conflicting specification requirements and information required to accurately scope and price the works:

1. There is conflicting information regarding the Fibre Optic Cable. The provided General Electrical Installation spec (ELE-SPEC-001) references.

- Section 7.14.2 Fibre Optic Cabling: All in-plant control systems networks and patch leads (Remote I/O LAN, PLC LAN, SCADA LAN), fibre optic cabling shall be 50/125 µm (OM2) multi-mode glass fibre type cable.

- In Appendix A: Preferred Managed Ethernet Switches are Moxa EDS-5xxA-T Series.

The provided Principal’s Project Requirements (Contract Annexure Part E) references:

- First page, bullet point: Install vermin resistant (armoured) Single Mode Optical Fibre cabling between the Switchroom and the PAC dosing system. This shall include FOBOT installation at both ends.

 The provided Principal’s Project Requirements (Contract Annexure Part E) references:

- Section 3.4 PAC RIO Integration: The RIO shall be connected to the main WTP PLC using simple Daisy Chain Loop via parallel cores of the multicore fibre cable

- Section 3.4 PAC RIO Integration: Councils preferred switch with fibre capabilities is Planet Technologies ISW-621TF with MFB-TF20 SFP modules (Our engineers tell me this hardware seems to be more appropriate for connecting long distances to sites that don’t require a managed switch for redundant loops. And would likely require attenuators to be installed due to the short distance (50m) run.

Can TRC confirm whether the fibre is to be multi-mode or single-mode, and which brand (and series) of Ethernet Switches are required?

2. Shutdown windows

- Section 8 of the RFO allows the plant to be taken offline for "short periods of time (4hrs)" within the 20-day window, but states no maximum duration. Can TRC confirm the maximum continuous shutdown duration that will be approved?

- Can TRC confirm the frequency of approved shutdowns (e.g. one 8-hour shut per day, twice a week, or five days a week) and the required plant recovery period between shutdowns?

- Can TRC confirm whether a multi-day continuous outage would be considered for the PLC platform cutover, subject to an approved cut-over plan?

Existing plant documentation

- Can TRC provide the current Functional Description (Parts A and B) and any design report for the existing plant, to show how the plant currently operates and its condition?

- Can TRC provide the current PLC I/O list, to allow control systems pricing to reflect the actual scope?

- Can TRC provide the as-constructed electrical drawings for the site, including layout drawings?

- Can TRC provide the existing switchboard drawings and photographs behind the 415V escutcheons and doors, relevant to the VSD replacement in the existing switchboard?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question: Can TRC confirm whether the fibre is to be multi-mode or single-mode, and which brand (and series) of Ethernet Switches are required?

Council Response: With Planet Technologies ISW-621TF hardware, neither multi or single mode fibre modules require attenuators over a 50m run. Council uses this configuration without issue at other sites. MFB-TF20 single mode modules are to be used.

Question: Can TRC confirm the maximum continuous shutdown duration that will be approved?

Council Response: The maximum shutdown that will be guaranteed to be approved is 4 hours. However, depending on operational constraints, weather and other contributing factors this could be extended by agreement at the time of the works. For further reference, works completed between October – March summer period will typically have less flexibility for the maximum outage duration. Works in Winter months (~March onwards) have more flexibility. The long term rainfall will also affect the maximum outage time.

Question: Can TRC confirm the frequency of approved shutdowns (e.g. one 8-hour shut per day, twice a week, or five days a week) and the required plant recovery period between shutdowns?

Council Response: Council can guarantee 1 x 4hr shutdown, twice per week on non-consecutive days. This will be governed by recovery periods during works, which are impacted as per the above, but typically 2 days recovery is sufficient.

Question: Can TRC confirm whether a multi-day continuous outage would be considered for the PLC platform cutover, subject to an approved cut-over plan?

Council Response: No multi-day continuous outages would be considered.

Question: Can TRC provide the current Functional Description (Parts A and B) and any design report for the existing plant, to show how the plant currently operates and its condition?

Council Response: Council can provide the Functional Description directly to your approved integrator if you provide details. Council will not provide this information to parties not bound under its system integration panel. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the name of your integrator.

Question: Can TRC provide the current PLC I/O list, to allow control systems pricing to reflect the actual scope?

Response: Council can provide the I/O list directly to your approved integrator if you provide details. Council will not provide this information to parties not bound under its system integration panel. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the name of your integrator.

Question: Can TRC provide the as-constructed electrical drawings for the site, including layout drawings?

Response: Council can provide a view only link to the As-Constructed Drawings for the site, however Council cannot guarantee all modifications that occurred on site have been reflected in the changes. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the email address you wish to have the files shared to.

Question: Can TRC provide the existing switchboard drawings and photographs behind the 415V escutcheons and doors, relevant to the VSD replacement in the existing switchboard?

Response: Council can provide a view only link to the As-Constructed Drawings for the site, however Council cannot guarantee all modifications that occurred on site have been reflected in the changes. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the email address you wish to have the files shared to. Council does not have any photo’s however would note that there is an opportunity for another non-mandatory site inspection at Pechey WTP from 10am-12pm on Thursday 17th September. Please email Ben.Oon@tr.qld.gov.au if you wish to attend this visit.

title: RFT CT2027006 Livestock Marketing Centre: Sheep Loading Ramp Renewal D&C
description:
Wagga Wagga City Council (Council) are improving the loading ramps of the Livestock Marketing Centre (LMC) sheep delivery yards. The ramps, located in the northeast corner of the site, were constructed with the original facility and have reached the end of their useful life. This increases the risk of slips, injuries and creates potential workplace safety and animal welfare concerns.

The project aims to replace the original ramps with modern equipment to ensure safe operating conditions for animals, staff, and operators. Pavement renewal at the base of the ramps will also be undertaken.

The desired outcome of this RFT is to enter into a Lump Sum Contract with an appropriately experienced Contractor for the Design & Construction of new ramps and pavement renewal in accordance with the tender documentation.

The Scope of Works under this RFT is to design new loading ramps, remove the existing ramps, remediating the pavement, and installing new loading ramps.

The works to be performed by the Contractor include the provision of all labour, supervision, materials, equipment, designs, overheads, administration, taxes, wages, accommodation, transport, allowances, consumables, testing services and any other incidental costs, to construct the works in accordance with this Contract.

ON-SITE BRIEFING:

A pre-tender briefing will be held on Tuesday 1st September 2026 at 11AM. The meeting is to be held on-site at the Livestock Marketing Centre, Webb Street, Bomen. Registration to attend the briefing can be made via email procurement@wagga.nsw.gov.au.

Whilst this briefing is not compulsory, consultants are encouraged to attend to obtain a firsthand understanding of the works required.

title: Palm Island Barge Ramp Upgrades – Pre-Construction Engineering and Detailed Design
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking a suitably qualified multidisciplinary engineering consultant to undertake the pre-construction engineering, investigations and detailed design required for the upgrade of the existing Palm Island Barge Ramp.

The Services are intended to progress the project from the currently identified infrastructure deficiencies through investigations, options assessment, design development and detailed design to a complete, coordinated and RPEQ-certified construction-ready documentation package suitable for future construction procurement and funding.

The Services must consider repair, extension, widening and/or reconfiguration of the existing ramp, as appropriate, including opportunities to improve tidal accessibility, accommodate larger and wider barges, increase operational capacity and facilitate concurrent barge operations where technically and operationally practicable.

The Services include all investigations, surveys, engineering assessments, stakeholder and approvals coordination, cost estimation, technical specifications and other pre-construction activities reasonably necessary to achieve this outcome.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island, also known as Great Palm Island, or by the Aboriginal name Bwgcolman, is the largest of twelve tropical Islands in the Palm Island Group. The settlement is named variously Palm Island, the Mission, Palm Island Settlement or Palm Community.

The group of Islands is less than 20 kilometres from the nearest point on the mainland (Lucinda) and is 65 kilometres north of Townsville over sea. The Islands are serviced by a 20 minute plane ride or one and a half hour ferry ride from Townsville and a one hour barge trip from Lucinda.

Palm Island consists of small bays, sandy beaches, fringing reefs, beautiful freshwater streams and steep forested mountains rising to the highest peak of 548 metres at Bentley Ridge. Other islands in the chain, such as Orpheus and North Palm have globally renowned resorts and marine research stations. Situated in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, the surrounding reefs are as good as any on the outer reef, presenting wonderful fishing and diving opportunities and are used extensively by locals for hunting and gathering and other cultural purposes.

Palm Island is the largest discreet Indigenous community in Australia with approximately 4,000 people residing on Palm Island. There is high mobility between Palm Island and the mainland, and the population can increase to over 5,000 people during festivals and events. There are seven suburbs on the Island, running from Butler Bay in the south to Wallaby Point in the north, with the main, central settlement area, The Mission having the mall, shops, service centres, police station, motel, hospital and health service and Council chambers. Critical services infrastructure, including the Council’s works depots, waste and recycling facility, (Ergon) power station, water and sewer treatment plants, and two water supply reservoirs are at The Farm area, Solomon and Wallaby Point.

publicQuestions.question:
1. There does not seem to have quantities in the BOQ. Drawings have broad quantities (54 piles for instance). Could you please provide all quantities to price accordingly (m2 of repairs per type)

2. The contract mentions liquidated damages in case program is not met. However, it does not seem to have any targeted completion date. Please provide an indication as to when the works are intended to start and intended to be completed.

3. There is a note in the specification making reference to galvashied anodes, however, it is not clear whether or not these are required. Please confirm.
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see below responses to your Request for Information.

1 - A Bill of Quantities has not been published as part of the Tender invitation. Refer to Part C Clause 1.6-1.9. Refer also to Part D, Appendix C, Clause 4.

2 - It is not expected that a timeframe to completion can be accurately determined at the start of the project. Target Completion Date will be determined jointly by the Principal and successful Contractor as the works are underway; as detailed condition survey efforts inform the extent of work to be completed; and as the general rate of progress is established and observed on site by the project team.

3 - Part D, Appendix C, Clause 1.1 makes reference to AS 2239. However, the Specification currently does not require that sacrificial anodes are installed as part of concrete patch repairs. If Tenderers consider this a valuable component of repair methodology, they are invited to provide an optional Rate to Design, Supply and Install anodes (say a Rate per 10 or 20 anodes), for consideration by the Principal. The provision of this optional Rate is not mandatory.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 1 - Pile Section dimensions, Wharves 5 and 6

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; Appendix E reference drawings 403-003, 403-007, 403-017

The Technical Specification and the Pile Repair Detail at Figure 6 specify a retained core of not less than 250mm x 250mm and reference existing 40mm reinforcing bars, but do not state the overall pile section dimensions.

Of the reference drawings at Appendix E, drawing 303-001 relates to Wharf No. 1 and notes columns of 17" x 19½". Drawing 403-003 is annotated as not proceeded with. Drawing 403-017, which covers the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area, carries the note "WHARF GEOMETRY NOT VERIFIED".

Would the Principal please confirm the pile section dimensions, including corner chamfer, applicable to the piles nominated for repair on Wharves 5 and 6; or confirm that no verified dimensional information is held by the Principal.

Further notes that clause 1.6 states a precise scope of work has not been defined and that the exact extent of repairs will be determined during the Works. Confirmation of the pile section is nonetheless required at tender, as it governs the design and fabrication of reinstatement formwork.

RFI 2 - Release of existing condition survey and investigation reports

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 1.4, 1.5, 7.14; FY26 Works Layout Plan (KBR annotation)

Clause 1.4 of the Scope of Works states that the Priority 1A and 1B defects were identified during a detailed inspection undertaken by KBR in February 2023, that further deterioration has likely occurred since, and that some areas have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey. Clause 7.14 of the Technical Specification quotes concrete cover data attributed to a 1993 report by Beal.

Elouera observed at the Site Inspection that elements beneath the wharf carry survey markings, and that previously executed repairs are visible, consistent with the 2023 rectification works identified on drawing 300-085.

Would the Principal please make available to all Tenderers the KBR February 2023 detailed inspection report, the 1993 Beal report, and any supporting data relied upon in preparing the FY26 Works Layout Plan, including measured element dimensions, chloride profiles, cover meter surveys, delamination survey results and photographic records.

Would the Principal also please advise which elements have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey, and confirm whether those elements are excluded from the present scope.

RFI 3 - Annexure to the General Conditions of Contract

Reference: Conditions of Contract cl. 18, 20, 26; definitions of LD Cap and Operational Delay Allowance

The General Conditions repeatedly refer to particulars stated in the Annexure, including the Date for Practical Completion, the rate of liquidated damages, the LD Cap, the Operational Delay Allowance, the Defects Liability Period, Security and retention, and required insurance limits.

The Annexure does not appear within Parts A to E of the RFT package. Would the Principal please issue the completed Annexure to all Tenderers.

RFI 4 - Quantities for slab soffit and beam repairs

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 4.4(c), cl. 6.1; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Items 3.00 and 4.00

Clause 6.1 states that precise locations and defined areas for slab soffit and beam repairs have not been defined on the drawings. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams by element count.

Part G requires banded rates per square metre, and clause 4.4(c) provides for payment against the final measured area of each individual patch.

Would the Principal please advise the indicative total repair area, in square metres, anticipated for slab soffit repairs and for beam repairs respectively; and the anticipated distribution of individual patch repairs across the area bands set out at clause 4.4(f). If no such estimate is held, would the Principal please confirm this.

RFI 5 - Split of pile repairs between Type A and Type B

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Item 2.00

Clause 5.5 requires two types of pile repair to be priced. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 54 piles for repair but does not indicate which are anticipated to be Type A and which Type B.

The two repair types differ materially in extent, Type A being one full face over a 2000mm height and Type B extending from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab.

Would the Principal please advise the anticipated number of Type A and Type B pile repairs, or confirm that this allocation is to be determined at the joint inspection under clause 5.2.

RFI 6 - Tenderer access for measurement prior to close of Tender

Reference: Part A — Site Inspection / RFT Briefing; Conditions of Tender cl. 6.2, 6.3

Access at the mandatory Site Inspection on 19 August 2026 was limited to visual observation from the wharf deck. The elements to be repaired are located beneath the wharf deck and were not accessible for inspection or measurement.

Clause 6.2 deems the Tenderer to have inspected the Site and satisfied itself of conditions. In order to discharge that obligation in a meaningful way, would the Principal please confirm in writing whether Tenderers may arrange a further inspection prior to close of Tender with access beneath the wharf deck, including by small vessel, and advise the conditions, notice period, induction and security requirements applicable to such access.

If such access cannot be made available, would the Principal please confirm this in writing.

RFI 7 - Basis of the Principal's estimate of repair extent

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 4.4(d) and Figure 3; cl. 7.9; Conditions of Contract cl. 26

Clause 4.4(d) sets expected repair depths of 150mm for piles, 120mm for slab soffits and 140mm for beams, each with a tolerance of plus or minus 20mm, and provides for rate adjustment where measured depths fall outside that tolerance. Clause 7.9 provides that excessive removal beyond the specified extent is at the Contractor's cost.

Would the Principal please advise the basis on which the expected repair depths at Figure 3 were derived, and confirm whether the Principal anticipates that the actual extent and depth of deterioration may differ materially from those expected values.

Would the Principal further confirm that where measured extents exceed those anticipated to a degree that affects the Contractor's ability to reach Practical Completion by the Date for Practical Completion, the Contractor's entitlement to an extension of time under clause 18 is preserved.

RFI 8 - Part G Prices and Rates Schedule

Reference: Part A — RFT Package Details; Technical Specification cl. 4.4

Part A lists Part G Prices and Rates Schedule in Excel format as a returnable document. Would the Principal please confirm that the current issue of Part G, together with Part F Schedules, has been made available to all Tenderers via Vendor Panel, and advise the issue date and revision of each.

RFI 9 - Approved Budget and its relationship to the scope of works

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 1.6, 1.7, 1.8; Conditions of Contract — Date for Practical Completion

Clause 1.7 provides that tendered Fixed Costs and Rates, combined with on-site measurement, will be used to track and forecast project costs up to an approved budget to be advised by the Principal at contract formation. Clause 1.8 provides that the approved budget must not be exceeded by the Contractor unless approved in writing.

The approved budget is therefore not disclosed to Tenderers at the time of pricing, yet governs the volume of work that may be executed under the Contract.

Would the Principal please advise:

(a) the approved budget, or an indicative range, to enable Tenderers to assess the likely volume of work and resource it accordingly;

(b) the mechanism by which the Works will proceed if the approved budget is reached before all nominated elements have been repaired — specifically whether the Contractor is to cease work, whether Practical Completion is achieved at that point, and how Preliminaries are treated for the balance of the Contract period; and

(c) whether the quantities shown on the FY26 Works Layout Plan, being 54 piles, 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams, are within the approved budget at the Principal's own estimate of rates.

RFI 10 - Pile head haunching and termination of Type B repairs

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5(d); Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; observed conditions at Site Inspection

Clause 5.5(d) provides that Type B pile repairs shall extend from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab. Figure 6 depicts the pile as a prismatic section of constant dimension.

Elouera observed at the Site Inspection that the piles flare into a substantial curved haunch at the pile head, over a significant proportion of the exposed pile height, before meeting the beam soffit. This geometry is not reflected in Figure 6 and appears to vary between piles.

Would the Principal please advise:

(a) whether Type B repairs are required to extend through the haunched pile head to the underside of the slab, or are to terminate below the commencement of the haunch;

(b) if the haunch is included, whether reinstatement of the haunch profile is deemed included in the Type B pile repair rate or is to be measured separately; and

(c) whether any dimensional information for the haunch geometry is held by the Principal.

RFI 11 - Removal of marine growth

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 9.10 Surface Preparation; cl. 14.4 Silane Application; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule

Elouera observed dense marine growth, including oyster and barnacle encrustation, extending a substantial height up the piles from the bed. Removal of this growth is a necessary precursor to hydro-demolition, to reinstatement, and to silane application on any surface within the affected zone.

The Technical Specification addresses surface preparation at clause 9.10 but does not identify removal of marine growth, and no corresponding item is evident in the payment mechanism at clause 4.4.

Would the Principal please confirm whether removal and disposal of marine growth is deemed included within the tendered pile repair rates, or is to be measured and paid separately; and confirm any environmental controls required for its capture and disposal under the Environmental Management Plan.

RFI 12 - Heritage General Exemption Certificate

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 2.1, 2.2

Clause 2.2 provides that work shall not commence until the Principal has confirmed that the General Exemption Certificate — Queensland Heritage Places will apply to this project.

Would the Principal please confirm whether that certificate has been obtained or confirmed as applicable as at the date of tender; and if not, advise the anticipated timing and confirm that any delay to commencement arising from it will be treated as an act or omission of the Principal for the purposes of extension of time under clause 18.

RFI 13 - Hydro-demolition working hours and tidal working windows

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.3(a), 8.3(b); cl. 8.5(b)

Clause 8.3(a) permits working hours between 6.00am and 6.30pm, Monday to Sunday. Clause 8.3(b) provides that there shall be no excessively noisy activities such as hydro-demolition before 8.00am or after 5.00pm, giving an effective nine-hour window for concrete removal.

The elements to be repaired are tidal. Type B pile repairs commence at 1.700m Chart Datum, which the Specification identifies as Mean Sea Level, and are accessible only during low-water windows. Those windows advance by approximately 50 minutes each day and will regularly fall wholly or partly outside the 8.00am to 5.00pm period.

Would the Principal please confirm:

(a) whether the Superintendent will consider approval under clause 8.3(a) for hydro-demolition to be undertaken outside 8.00am to 5.00pm where a low-water working window falls outside those hours, and the basis on which such approval would be assessed; and

(b) whether any noise limits, monitoring requirements or conditions apply, having regard to nearby residential receivers.

RFI 14 - Maritime Security Identification Cards

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.2(g); General Conditions of Contract cl. 7.3

Clause 8.2(g) of the Scope of Works states that it is expected Maritime Security Identification Cards will not be required, as the works are being undertaken around vessel operations.

Clause 7.3(a) of the General Conditions provides that if the work is required to be performed in maritime security zones, at least two employees of the Contractor must hold an MSIC, with all associated costs borne by the Contractor.

Would the Principal please confirm which position applies to these works, and whether any part of the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area is designated a maritime security zone.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon

Please see responses to your questions.

RFI 1 - Pile Section dimensions, Wharves 5 and 6

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; Appendix E reference drawings 403-003, 403-007, 403-017

The Technical Specification and the Pile Repair Detail at Figure 6 specify a retained core of not less than 250mm x 250mm and reference existing 40mm reinforcing bars, but do not state the overall pile section dimensions.

Of the reference drawings at Appendix E, drawing 303-001 relates to Wharf No. 1 and notes columns of 17" x 19½". Drawing 403-003 is annotated as not proceeded with. Drawing 403-017, which covers the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area, carries the note "WHARF GEOMETRY NOT VERIFIED".

Would the Principal please confirm the pile section dimensions, including corner chamfer, applicable to the piles nominated for repair on Wharves 5 and 6; or confirm that no verified dimensional information is held by the Principal.

Further notes that clause 1.6 states a precise scope of work has not been defined and that the exact extent of repairs will be determined during the Works. Confirmation of the pile section is nonetheless required at tender, as it governs the design and fabrication of reinstatement formwork.

Response:

No verified dimensions are held by the Principal - historic drawings provide indicative, expected dimensions which will likely vary across the asset.

RFI 2 - Release of existing condition survey and investigation reports

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 1.4, 1.5, 7.14; FY26 Works Layout Plan (KBR annotation)

Clause 1.4 of the Scope of Works states that the Priority 1A and 1B defects were identified during a detailed inspection undertaken by KBR in February 2023, that further deterioration has likely occurred since, and that some areas have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey. Clause 7.14 of the Technical Specification quotes concrete cover data attributed to a 1993 report by Beal.

Elouera observed at the Site Inspection that elements beneath the wharf carry survey markings, and that previously executed repairs are visible, consistent with the 2023 rectification works identified on drawing 300-085.

Would the Principal please make available to all Tenderers the KBR February 2023 detailed inspection report, the 1993 Beal report, and any supporting data relied upon in preparing the FY26 Works Layout Plan, including measured element dimensions, chloride profiles, cover meter surveys, delamination survey results and photographic records.

Would the Principal also please advise which elements have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey, and confirm whether those elements are excluded from the present scope.

Response:

Historic survey results or results of previous work will not be provided during tender.

RFI 3 - Annexure to the General Conditions of Contract

The General Conditions repeatedly refer to particulars stated in the Annexure, including the Date for Practical Completion, the rate of liquidated damages, the LD Cap, the Operational Delay Allowance, the Defects Liability Period, Security and retention, and required insurance limits.

The Annexure does not appear within Parts A to E of the RFT package. Would the Principal please issue the completed Annexure to all Tenderers.

Response:

Refer to Annexure A on Pg 111 of Parts A to E of the RFT Package.

RFI 4 - Quantities for slab soffit and beam repairs

Clause 6.1 states that precise locations and defined areas for slab soffit and beam repairs have not been defined on the drawings. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams by element count.

Would the Principal please advise the indicative total repair area, in square metres, anticipated for slab soffit repairs and for beam repairs respectively; and the anticipated distribution of individual patch repairs across the area bands set out at clause 4.4(f). If no such estimate is held, would the Principal please confirm this.

Response:

No such estimate is held.

RFI 5 - Split of pile repairs between Type A and Type B

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Item 2.00

Clause 5.5 requires two types of pile repair to be priced. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 54 piles for repair but does not indicate which are anticipated to be Type A and which Type B.

The two repair types differ materially in extent, Type A being one full face over a 2000mm height and Type B extending from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab.

Would the Principal please advise the anticipated number of Type A and Type B pile repairs, or confirm that this allocation is to be determined at the joint inspection under clause 5.2.

Response:

Allocation of Type A and Type B repairs of Piles is to be determined at the joint inspection.

RFI 6 - Tenderer access for measurement prior to close of Tender

Reference: Part A — Site Inspection / RFT Briefing; Conditions of Tender cl. 6.2, 6.3

Access at the mandatory Site Inspection on 19 August 2026 was limited to visual observation from the wharf deck. The elements to be repaired are located beneath the wharf deck and were not accessible for inspection or measurement.

Clause 6.2 deems the Tenderer to have inspected the Site and satisfied itself of conditions. There is no intent for detailed inspection or measure-up by tenderers, before award of contract. Visual inspection from publicly accessible/navigable areas of the Inlet is allowed. Access beneath the wharves will not be available during tender.

RFI 7 - Basis of the Principal's estimate of repair extent

Clause 4.4(d) sets expected repair depths of 150mm for piles, 120mm for slab soffits and 140mm for beams, each with a tolerance of plus or minus 20mm, and provides for rate adjustment where measured depths fall outside that tolerance. Clause 7.9 provides that excessive removal beyond the specified extent is at the Contractor's cost.

Would the Principal please advise the basis on which the expected repair depths at Figure 3 were derived, and confirm whether the Principal anticipates that the actual extent and depth of deterioration may differ materially from those expected values.

Would the Principal further confirm that where measured extents exceed those anticipated to a degree that affects the Contractor's ability to reach Practical Completion by the Date for Practical Completion, the Contractor's entitlement to an extension of time under clause 18 is preserved.

Response:

Expected repair depths were derived from records of similar repairs previously undertaken at Heritage Wharves 1-6. Some differences should be expected, and the contract allows for cost adjustments to repair depth and reinforcement content to be made.

Refer to Tender Addendum 1 for additional comment provided, regarding programme.

RFI 8 - Part G Prices and Rates Schedule

Reference: Part A — RFT Package Details; Technical Specification cl. 4.4

Part A lists Part G Prices and Rates Schedule in Excel format as a returnable document. Would the Principal please confirm that the current issue of Part G, together with Part F Schedules, has been made available to all Tenderers via Vendor Panel, and advise the issue date and revision of each.

The Tender Invitation package uploaded to Vendor Panel includes the following files, on Tuesday 4 August:

RFT CNS 26-22-01 Parts A-E.pdf

RFT CNS 26-22-01 part F.docx

RFI 9 - Approved Budget and its relationship to the scope of works

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 1.6, 1.7, 1.8; Conditions of Contract — Date for Practical Completion

Clause 1.7 provides that tendered Fixed Costs and Rates, combined with on-site measurement, will be used to track and forecast project costs up to an approved budget to be advised by the Principal at contract formation. Clause 1.8 provides that the approved budget must not be exceeded by the Contractor unless approved in writing.

The approved budget is therefore not disclosed to Tenderers at the time of pricing, yet governs the volume of work that may be executed under the Contract.

Would the Principal please advise:
