(b) the mechanism by which the Works will proceed if the approved budget is reached before all nominated elements have been repaired — specifically whether the Contractor is to cease work, whether Practical Completion is achieved at that point, and how Preliminaries are treated for the balance of the Contract period; and

(c) whether the quantities shown on the FY26 Works Layout Plan, being 54 piles, 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams, are within the approved budget at the Principal's own estimate of rates.

Response:

An approved budge will be advised at award of contract, not before. The approved budget for this Financial Year is deemed sufficient to undertake a major, significant campaign of work to the Asset.

Preliminaries are anticipated to be drawn down as appropriate during the commencement of works (mobilisation and establishment), and during the conclusion of works (demobilisation and conclusion of works). Production Rates shall apply as the works are underway.

The Principal may extend the approved budget at its sole discretion - with significant advance notice to be provided to the Contractor. The expectation is that the Principal and Contractor will work collaboratively to understand and track the rate of progress and budget spend, to inform and manage the quantity of work and related time to completion, including any potential change in scope and time as a result of the Principal's approval of additional funding.

RFI 10 - Pile head haunching and termination of Type B repairs

(a) whether Type B repairs are required to extend through the haunched pile head to the underside of the slab, or are to terminate below the commencement of the haunch;

(b) if the haunch is included, whether reinstatement of the haunch profile is deemed included in the Type B pile repair rate or is to be measured separately; and

(c) whether any dimensional information for the haunch geometry is held by the Principal.

Response:

Accurate dimensional information on haunches is not available, beyond historic documentation. Pile Repairs are to focus on Piles. Haunch repairs, if needed, will be quantified and paid for in a manner similar to, and using rates associated with beam repairs.

RFI 11 - Removal of marine growth

Elouera observed dense marine growth, including oyster and barnacle encrustation, extending a substantial height up the piles from the bed. Removal of this growth is a necessary precursor to hydro-demolition, to reinstatement, and to silane application on any surface within the affected zone.

The project is not anticipated to incorporate any disturbance of marine plants. Removal and appropriate disposal of oyster and barnacle encrustation is to be included within the tendered pile repair rates.

Reference also Part D Appendix B and Part E Conditions of Contract, Clause 7.6 (c) for the Principal's fundamental requirement regarding capture and responsible disposal of demolished material. For further clarity: all solid demolished material is to be captured and disposed of responsibly. Hydrodemolition water is to be filtered, but is not required to be fully captured. Tenderers are requested to outline in Returnable Schedule 10 how they will achieve this requirement.

RFI 12 - Heritage General Exemption Certificate

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 2.1, 2.2

Clause 2.2 provides that work shall not commence until the Principal has confirmed that the General Exemption Certificate — Queensland Heritage Places will apply to this project.

Would the Principal please confirm whether that certificate has been obtained or confirmed as applicable as at the date of tender; and if not, advise the anticipated timing and confirm that any delay to commencement arising from it will be treated as an act or omission of the Principal for the purposes of extension of time under clause 18.

The Principal now has approval for the works to be undertaken under the General Exemption Certificate — Queensland Heritage Places.

RFI 13 - Hydro-demolition working hours and tidal working windows

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.3(a), 8.3(b); cl. 8.5(b)

Clause 8.3(a) permits working hours between 6.00am and 6.30pm, Monday to Sunday. Clause 8.3(b) provides that there shall be no excessively noisy activities such as hydro-demolition before 8.00am or after 5.00pm, giving an effective nine-hour window for concrete removal.

A pragmatic approach will be taken - adjustments of time for noisy work will be considered and likely approved, so long as Stakeholders are not adversely affected.

It is expected MSIC will not be required to deliver the works. The preferred outcome is for the Contractor to schedule works, and potentially have multiple established/available works areas, such that none are required to be performed in maritime security zones.

Thank you

The Mackay Regional Council area is one of the fastest growing regions in Queensland. Covering the areas of the former Sarina and Mirani shires and Mackay city, it extends 7261 square kilometres.

With a population of around 110,000 as at June 2008 and a projected annual growth rate of 2.1 per cent, the region’s estimated population in 2031 is about 173,000 people.

Its coastal location is complemented by its spectacular natural environment. This includes 31 beautiful beaches, a picturesque blue river and a pristine rainforest hinterland.

Only an hour’s flight from Brisbane, the Mackay region boasts an enviable lifestyle and a buoyant economy with the benefits of a fastgrowing coastal city. It is the gateway to the rich coal deposits in the Bowen basin.

It is the largest sugar-producing region in Australia and nearly a third of Queensland’s export goods originate from the Mackay region.

There are about 25 different nationalities represented in the region, including people from Malta, South Africa, the Netherlands and Germany. The region also boasts the largest Australian South Sea Islander population.

title: Mental Health Wellbeing Investment Package ITO
description:
The Package is being delivered through a partnership-based approach, working across Queensland Government, with up to six government partner agencies, to implement strategic funding partnerships. The Commission has established a group with representatives from each partner agency, to support coordination, collective impact measurement, shared learning and governance oversight across the package.

The partnerships fund a range of initiatives including, a mix of place-based activities, community and local council grant programs, cross-sector collaboration, and activities that strengthen workforce capability, service integration, and policy and practice across systems. Activities are delivered across metropolitan, regional, and remote Queensland. Timing of initiatives will be staggered across financial years FY2025/2026 to mid FY2028/2029.

The Commission requires an external Supplier to undertake an independent evaluation of the previous Grants and the Package, including development of an evaluation framework, to assess mental health and wellbeing outcomes and broader system impacts. The Supplier will be expected to design practical data collection and reporting approaches that partners can reasonably implement within existing operational environments.

The evaluation will also examine the collaborative approach between the Commission and government partners to inform future policy and reform directions. The Supplier will be expected to take a collaborative and developmental evaluation approach, working alongside the Commission and government partners over the life of the Package to support learning, adaptation, and continuous improvement, rather than undertaking a single end-point evaluation.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Queensland Mental Health Commission (the Commission) is a statutory body established under the Queensland Mental Health Commission Act 2013 to drive systemic reform across Queensland’s mental health, alcohol and other drugs, and suicide prevention systems. A core function of the Commission is to develop and facilitate implementation of a whole-of-government strategic plan to improve mental health and wellbeing outcomes for Queenslanders. The current plans, Shifting minds: The Queensland Mental Health, Alcohol and Other Drugs, and Suicide Prevention Strategic Plan 2023-2028 (Shifting minds) and its associated sub-plans; The Queensland Trauma Strategy 2024-2029, Achieving balance: The Queensland Alcohol and Other Drugs Plan 2022-2027 and Every life: The Queensland Suicide Prevention Plan 2019-2029 Phase Two, provides the overarching framework for this work.

In addition, in response to Recommendation 19 of the 2022 Queensland Parliament Mental Health Select Committee Inquiry into opportunities to improve mental health outcomes for Queenslanders, Thriving Lives, Connected Communities – Queensland’s Commitment to Mental Health and Wellbeing (Thriving Lives, Connected Communities) was developed to provide a focused direction for improving community mental health and wellbeing.

Recommendation 19 – Develop Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy

The committee recommends the Queensland Government considers the development of a population based Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy that works across human services portfolios and is aimed at improving community mental health and wellbeing.

Time-limited, non-recurrent funding has been provided to the Commission to progress priorities identified in Thriving Lives, Connected Communities.

In 2025, the Commission delivered the Mental Health and Wellbeing Grants program, (the Grants) distributing $2.8 million across 22 projects to strengthen community mental health and wellbeing through mental health promotion, prevention and early intervention initiatives.

Building on the Grants, the Commission established the Mental Health and Wellbeing Investment Package (the Package), a targeted, time-limited investment of $9 million that adopts a strategic and coordinated approach. The Package supports initiatives that strengthen population-based mental health and wellbeing through mental health promotion and prevention, while leveraging existing systems, infrastructure and partnerships to maximise impact, reduce duplication and support sustainability beyond the funding period.

The Package is being delivered through a partnership-based approach, working across Queensland Government, with up to six government partner agencies, to implement strategic funding partnerships. The Commission has established a group with representatives from each partner agency, to support coordination, collective impact measurement, shared learning and governance oversight across the package.

The partnerships fund a range of initiatives including, a mix of place-based activities, community and local council grant programs, cross-sector collaboration, and activities that strengthen workforce capability, service integration, and policy and practice across systems. Activities are delivered across metropolitan, regional, and remote Queensland. Timing of initiatives will be staggered across financial years FY2025/2026 to mid FY2028/2029.

The Commission requires an external Supplier to undertake an independent evaluation of the previous Grants and the Package, including development of an evaluation framework, to assess mental health and wellbeing outcomes and broader system impacts. The Supplier will be expected to design practical data collection and reporting approaches that partners can reasonably implement within existing operational environments.

The evaluation will also examine the collaborative approach between the Commission and government partners to inform future policy and reform directions. The Supplier will be expected to take a collaborative and developmental evaluation approach, working alongside the Commission and government partners over the life of the Package to support learning, adaptation, and continuous improvement, rather than undertaking a single end-point evaluation.

The evaluation is intended to inform future cross-government investment approaches, strengthen the evidence base for mental health promotion and prevention, and provide practical insights to inform ongoing mental health and wellbeing system reform and policy development in Queensland.

description:
Market Notification – Intention to release Invitation to Offer (ITO) – Mackay and Rockhampton Emergency Helicopter Services (VP510612).

NOTE - This notice is for information only. No action is required.

Queensland Health wishes to advise interested suppliers of an intention to release an ITO to the market for a single supplier to provide emergency helicopter services from Mackay and Rockhampton. The objectives of the intended procurement include achieving value for Queensland and taxpayers’ money and ensuring fair and open competition via an open tender procurement approach. The ITO will be a genuine opportunity to bid for the services and interest from all suitability qualified and experienced suppliers is welcomed and encouraged.

The services sought encompass aeromedical patient transport including pre-hospital retrieval, inter-facility transfer, search and rescue, law enforcement and/or support to other government agencies as required.

The anticipated timing for release of the ITO is likely to be during Quarter 4 of the 2026 calendar year. A supplier briefing may be held to provide suppliers with information regarding the ITO requirements and to allow suppliers to raise questions.

The ITO will be coordinated by Retrieval Services Queensland (RSQ), the body within the Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) responsible for the clinical and logistic coordination and contract management of all statewide aeromedical tasking. The ITO and any updates will be published on VendorPanel under reference VP510612.

Further updates may be provided via VendorPanel.

title: RFQ260197 - Emerald Saleyards Dip Yards Redesign Construct
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council (Council) operates the Emerald Saleyards and has a clearing dip which services thousands of cattle each year. Council's current objective is to upgrade existing areas and utilise spaces that will overall improve operational use and provide a safer and more reliable working environment.

Council have provided draft/concept drawings for the addition of gates to the Emerald Saleyards dip area, currently it has 90-degree passages with pull down portable panels. Construction to the area will optimize cattle flow and accessibility, improving livestock welfare, driving higher processing volumes and increased sales.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
65 Egerton St
Emerald, Queensland 4720
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) invites suitably qualified consultants to submit tenders for RFT260086 – Long-Term Residual Waste Solution – Standardised Site Assessment.

The engagement is for a strategic waste planning consultancy to undertake a comprehensive, evidence-based assessment of Council's long-term (30–50 year) residual waste disposal solution. The successful consultant will reconcile the remaining life of the existing Lochlees Resource Recovery and Landfill Facility, model long-term residual waste demand, develop a standardised assessment methodology, evaluate potential long-term disposal options against the Queensland Landfill Siting, Design, Operation and Rehabilitation Guideline (ESR/2015/1627), and prepare a defensible options report to inform future Council decision-making.

This is a desktop strategic planning and technical assessment. It does not include detailed engineering design, statutory approvals, land acquisition, or intrusive field investigations, which are outside the scope of this procurement.

The consultancy is expected to commence shortly following contract award and be completed over an approximately six-month period. Services may be undertaken remotely; however, attendance at key meetings and site inspections in Emerald, Queensland, will be required during the engagement.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) operates the Lochlees Resource Recovery and Landfill Facility at Emerald as its principal regional residual waste disposal facility. With the remaining capacity of the existing landfill being finite, Council is undertaking strategic planning to identify the most appropriate long-term (30–50 year) residual waste solution for the region. This procurement forms part of that strategic planning process and does not represent a decision to develop or acquire any particular site.

Tenderers should demonstrate experience in strategic landfill planning, waste infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and multi-criteria options analysis within the Queensland regulatory environment. Experience applying the Queensland Landfill Siting, Design, Operation and Rehabilitation Guideline (ESR/2015/1627), landfill capacity modelling, life-cycle costing, GIS-based spatial assessment, and facilitation of strategic decision-making for local government or similar organisations will be highly regarded.

Council will provide relevant background information, including previous investigations, landfill survey information, airspace and stockpile data, waste generation information, existing planning studies and other reference material identified within the tender documentation. Tenderers are expected to validate and appropriately use this information while exercising independent professional judgement.

The successful consultant will be required to:

- Work collaboratively with Council's project team throughout the engagement.

- Attend key project meetings and undertake site inspections at Emerald where required.

- Provide all reports, models and supporting documentation in fully editable electronic formats.

- Develop a transparent, evidence-based and independently defensible assessment methodology.

- Cooperate with an independently appointed peer reviewer engaged separately by Council for review of the assessment methodology.

The engagement is a professional services consultancy only. Intrusive field investigations, statutory approvals, detailed engineering design, land acquisition activities and other downstream implementation works are expressly excluded from this procurement and, if required, will be commissioned under separate engagements.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a consultant that can deliver a transparent, evidence-based and independently defensible assessment of long-term residual waste disposal options that will support future strategic decision-making.

The successful consultant should:

- Deliver a robust, standardised assessment methodology capable of objectively comparing all reasonable long-term residual waste options on a consistent basis.

- Produce clear, high-quality technical reports and supporting models that are fully editable and suitable for future refinement and downstream planning.

- Demonstrate a sound understanding of Queensland landfill planning, environmental constraints, waste infrastructure planning and strategic options assessment.

- Apply recognised industry best practice and relevant Queensland regulatory guidance throughout the engagement.

- Provide practical, well-reasoned recommendations supported by documented assumptions, analysis and evidence.

- Maintain proactive communication, meet agreed project milestones, and work collaboratively with Council's project team throughout the engagement.

- Respond constructively to Council feedback and the independently commissioned methodology peer review within the agreed programme.

- Deliver all services within the agreed fixed lump-sum fee and project timeframe.

Council is seeking a consultant capable of becoming a trusted strategic advisor for this engagement by combining strong technical capability with practical understanding of local government decision-making, risk management and long-term infrastructure planning. The successful outcome will provide Council with a defensible evidence base to support future decisions regarding its long-term residual waste disposal strategy, while recognising that this engagement does not commit Council to any particular site, development or capital project.

title: Pick of the Crop 2027-28 expansion to Far North Queensland
description:
HWQld is Queensland’s dedicated prevention agency established to prevent chronic disease and improve health equity, with a focus on healthy eating, physical activity and obesity.

HWQld has committed to implementing a whole-school healthy eating program in all state primary schools across Queensland to increase children’s vegetable and fruit consumption. Pick of the Crop (POTC) is a whole school, multi-strategic, evidence-based healthy eating initiative developed by HWQld; it is flexible and designed by schools to focus on their unique community needs and school environment.

HWQld seeks to engage one or more Implementation partner/s in a two-year agreement to support delivery of POTC across Far North Queensland's Department of Education (DoE) regions.

Implementation Partner/s will be responsible for recruiting and managing a regional coordinator and supporting school engagement, implementation and stakeholder collaboration.

Key activities are expected to include:

 •	Recruitment, onboarding and support of a Regional Coordinator.

 •	School engagement, recruitment and relationship management activities to achieve school participation targets.

 •	Support at least 15 new schools per DoE region each year to develop and implement School Action Plans and approval processes.

 •	Support schools to apply for grants administered by HWQld and associated reporting requirements.

 •	Facilitate access to POTC resources, professional learning opportunities and implementation support.

 •	Coordinate stakeholder engagement and regional partnerships that strengthen POTC delivery.

 •	Ongoing support to participating schools to embed and sustain locally run activities.

 •	Collect required data and contribute to monitoring, evaluation and reporting activities.

 •	Prepare implementation insights and lessons learned to inform ongoing POTC development and continuous improvement.

 •	Networking with other POTC coordinators across the state, working in partnership and collaboration.

The Regional Coordinator is the primary point of contact for participating schools and stakeholders and will support the successful implementation, growth and sustainability of POTC across the region and state.

Key aims of POTC are:

 o	All Qld primary school students develop the knowledge, attitudes and skills to make healthy food choices through quality learning experiences, which are reinforced by supportive environments at school and at home.

 o	All Qld primary school educators have the capability and resources to deliver quality nutrition education learning experiences consistent with, and integrated across, the school curriculum.

 o	Build capacity and capability of communities to support schools increase student’s intake of vegetables and fruit.

Key Objectives for schools align with the World Health Organisation’s Health Promoting Schools framework. These are:

 1. Teaching and Learning: integrate food and nutrition education into the curriculum. Students will learn and gain knowledge, skills and experiences that will promote greater consumption of vegetables and fruit.

 2. Healthy School Environments: provide opportunities for students to access vegetables and fruit by incorporating them into the school tuckshop, breakfast clubs, brain breaks, tasting activities and establishing school gardens.

 3. Grower and Community Connections: strengthen connections with growers and producers (from Paddock to Plate), and implement engagement strategies with the community, families, parents and beyond.

Implementation of POTC regionally involves funding provided to local organisations (called Implementation Partners) under a negotiated Service Agreement with defined performance measures and contract deliverables.

For more detailed information please see the attached Request for Quote Information Document and supporting material.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
POTC is a tried and test model, demonstrated to be feasible for schools and teachers to implement and resulting in changes to students’ attitudes and beliefs towards vegetables and fruit consistent with project objectives.

Program need

Most Queensland (Qld) children do not meet the Australian Dietary Guideline recommendations:

 •	Only 3.2% of Queensland children aged 5 to 11 years are eating the recommended amount of 5 vegetables every day.

 •	80.7% of children eat the recommended 2 serves of fruit every day.

 •	39% of total energy intake of 4 to 8-year old males and 36% of females comes from unhealthy food and drinks.

 •	In 2022, research commissioned by HWQld found that children born in Queensland in 2023 could lose up to 4 years of life expectancy if obesity rates are not reversed, increasing up to 5 years for First Nations children.

Schools are ideal settings to reach large numbers of children, their families and communities and can shape their values and foster lifelong habits.

The overall goal of POTC is to achieve a sustained increase in vegetable and fruit consumption among primary school aged children in Queensland.

HWQld Strategic Alignment

POTC started with 35 state (primary) schools in three regional areas (Bowen, Bundaberg and Logan) as a pilot in 2021 to support HWQld’s commitment to increasing vegetable and fruit consumption for Queensland’s children, and since then has grown to reach 300 state schools with more than 70,000 student enrolments across Queensland. The vision for POTC is for all Queensland primary schools to have an opportunity to implement POTC by 2032.

description:
Installation of Pergola Roofing over Existing Cement Slabs for 6 Units.

There will be a Mandatory Site Inspection:

Date: Wednesday, 9 September 2026

Time: 10.00am

Place: Meet at 13 Malvern Street, Capella Qld

**Please register your attendance by 7 September 5pm**

The Contractor is to provide all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision and associated works necessary for the supply and installation of pergola roofing over the

existing concrete slabs at six (6) units.

The works are to be completed in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards, manufacturer’s requirements and applicable Building Regulations.

Site Verification

• Verify the existing slab dimensions, levels, condition and suitability for the proposed pergola structure.

• Confirm all dimensions, locations and site conditions prior to fabrication and installation.

• Dimensions shown in the documentation are indicative only. The Contractor is responsible for confirming all actual dimensions on site.

• Identify and confirm the location of any existing services that may affect the works.

• Undertake a Site Inspection of all six (6) units prior to commencing works.

Pergola Structure

• Supply and install the complete pergola framing structure, including posts, beams, rafters, brackets, fixings and associated components.

• Provide suitable structural connections between the pergola structure and the existing slab/building, as required by the design.

• Ensure all structural members are appropriately sized and designed for the site conditions and applicable wind loads.

• Provide corrosion-resistant fixings and connections suitable for the location.

• Ensure the structure is adequately braced and securely fixed.

• Provide appropriate clearances from existing buildings, doors, windows and other structures.

Roof

• Supply and install roofing over the pergola structure.

• Roofing material is to be suitable for the location and comply with the approved design.

• Provide all required flashings, trims, closures, gutters and associated roofing accessories.

• Ensure roofing is securely fixed and weatherproof.

• Provide appropriate roof falls to ensure effective stormwater drainage.

• Ensure roof drainage does not discharge onto adjoining properties, access paths or areas where it may create a hazard.

Storm Water

• Provide gutters and downpipes where required.

• Connect downpipes to the existing stormwater system where suitable and approved.

• Where connection to the existing system is not practicable, provide an appropriate alternative discharge arrangement.

• Ensure all stormwater works comply with relevant requirements and do not adversely affect the existing property.

Existing Concrete Slabs

• Inspect the existing concrete slabs prior to installation.

• Confirm the slab is suitable to support the proposed structure and associated loads.

• Avoid damage to the existing slab during drilling, anchoring and installation.

• Make good any minor damage caused by the Contractor during the works.

• Any structural deficiencies identified in the existing slab are to be reported to the Principal prior to proceeding.

Finishes and Protection

• Provide appropriate protective coatings to all exposed steel/aluminium components as required.

• Touch up any damaged coatings resulting from transportation or installation.

• Ensure all exposed edges, fixings and connections are finished safely.

• Match existing finishes where reasonably practicable and as agreed with the Principal.

Building Interfaces

• Ensure the new pergola roofing integrates appropriately with the existing building.

• Provide flashing and weatherproofing at all interfaces with the existing building.

• Maintain access to existing doors, windows, services and maintenance areas.

• Ensure the works do not interfere with existing building drainage, electrical services or other infrastructure.

Safety and Compliance

• Comply with all applicable WHS requirements and site safety procedures.

• Provide appropriate fall protection and safe access for working at heights.

• Maintain safe access to each Unit throughout the works.

• Protect existing buildings, landscaping, finishes and property during construction.

• Remove all construction waste and surplus materials from site.

Completion

• Inspect the completed pergola roofing works for structural stability, alignment, drainage and workmanship.

• Rectify any defects identified during inspection.

• Clean the work area and leave the site in a neat and safe condition.

• Provide relevant warranties, product information and certification upon completion.

• Provide as-built information where required.

Contractor’s Responsibility

The Contractor is responsible for confirming all dimensions, site conditions, quantities and interfaces prior to ordering materials or commencing fabrication. All dimensions shown or provided are indicative only and must be verified on site by the Contractor.

The Contractor is to allow for all incidental works necessary to provide a complete, functional and weatherproof pergola roofing installation for all six (6) Units.

Mandatory Site Visit

• A mandatory site inspection is required prior to submission of a quotation.

• The Contractor is to attend the site and inspect all Six (6) Units and the existing concrete slabs.

• The Contractor is responsible for verifying all existing site conditions, dimensions, levels, access requirements, services and interfaces relevant to the proposed works.

• All dimensions provided in the RFQ documentation are indicative only and must be verified on site by the Contractor.

• The Contractor is to satisfy themselves as to the full extent and nature of the works prior to submitting their response.

• No additional costs arising from a failure to attend the mandatory site inspection or verify site conditions will be considered, unless otherwise approved by the Principal.

• Respondents are to confirm attendance at the mandatory site inspection as part of their submission.

Estimated Start Contract Date 21/09/2026

End Contract Date 4/12/2026

publicQuestions.question:
Tender Queries

1/ Bridge Safety Barrier and Surfacing Works

The drawings indicate that asphalt surfacing is limited to the area between the new guardrails, while Drawing 162496 (A) requires the bitumen seal to extend at least 0.5 m beyond the face of the safety barrier; please confirm the required extent of each treatment with respect to the queries below.

•	There appears to be various locations where the bitumen seal will be installed on existing site earth / clay / topsoil material (i.e. non-pavement material). Can you confirm this is correct?

•	In terms of methodology and with reference to the specification requirements, the bitumen seal works will need to be undertaken prior to the guardrail installation to achieve compliance. Can Council confirm the extent of the bitumen seal, and whether compliance with the specification is required is these locations?

2/ With reference to project drawing 162496 (A), Table 2 Bridge Deck Wearing Surface and section B – Existing Road Bridge Crossing Section, we acknowledge the following:

•	The top of safety barrier height to be 1.00m above existing road surface.

•	The drawings indicate the new deck wearing surfacing will comprise of AC7H at minimum 25mm thickness and AC14H at minimum 50mm thickness. Hence, total minimum of 75mm.

With reference to the Bill of Quantity work item 41801.10, the description does not align with the drawings or annexures. Can you please review and provide comment?

We have inspected the site and believe the thickness of the existing surfacing is minimal (maybe limited to approximately 30mm). Hence, we have the following concerns:

•	Can you please confirm whether the barrier height is to be installed relative to the existing road surface level, or whether is should be relative to the design surface level of the new works?

•	The increased thickness of the deck wearing surfacing may create issues with the existing bridge drainage points. Are there any special treatments required in these areas?

•	Can you confirm that the existing bridge surface will withstand the additional deck wearing surfacing loading plus the loading associated with the construction activities with due consideration to vibration?

3/ Work Items 41701.01 Preparation of Existing Surfacing – Milling (both work items)

With reference to the work item associated with additional milling to 100mm depth, can Council confirm that the widths of the areas nominated, and whether these widths are based on profiler equipment minimum widths?

In relation to the drawing 162495 (A), can council confirm that the existing red brick paving nominated to be removed is asphalt surfacing with stamped stencil only, and can be removed via milling activities under this work item?

4/ Work Item 50001.01 Demolition of existing safety barrier

We acknowledge epoxy is to be used to fill existing holes in the bridge structure. Can Council advise of preferred products to undertake this work?

With reference to project drawing 162495 Note 2, we acknowledge that the existing posts are to be removed and care is to be taken around existing services. We have inspected the site and given the prevalence of basalt boulders (notably in the bridge abutment backfill), we are concerned that the existing guardrail posts may be a combination of driven posts and concrete encased posts. These will be problematic to remove when adjacent to services or the bridge abutment. Can council provide details of the installation of the existing guardrail posts or a possible methodology to address this issue?

5/ Existing Ground Conditions

Our site inspection identified prevalent basalt boulders that may prevent guardrail posts from being driven and may affect installation of the Crocguard concrete footings. Please confirm the applicable contract payment mechanism if additional work is required because of these ground conditions. For example, guardrail posts to be installed via coring and concrete encasement. Please also provide the preferred construction methodology, noting that coring equipment is likely to damage the bitumen surfacing if this is completed in advance of the guardrail works.

title: Service Review Framework
description:
The City of Boroondara is seeking a suitably experienced provider to work with Council to develop a Service Review Framework (Part 1), with the option to subsequently extend the Framework to incorporate a Service Planning Approach (Part 2).

Part 1 – Service Review Framework

1.	Part 1.A – Development of the Framework

The provider will develop a practical, fit-for-purpose Service Review Framework that establishes a consistent approach to planning and undertaking service reviews across Council, including the methodology, tools and supporting resources required to undertake future service reviews.

The Framework should complement Council’s Benefits Framework by supporting the identification, assessment and tracking of benefits from review recommendations, and enable insights and opportunities identified through reviews to inform ongoing service improvement.

The Framework, associated resources and intellectual property will be owned by Council and will provide the basis for establishing a panel of suitably qualified providers to undertake future service reviews on Council’s behalf.

2.	Part 1.B – Pilot of the Framework

As part of Part 1, the successful provider will be required to pilot the Service Review Framework with one small Council service. The pilot will provide an opportunity to test the Framework, methodology and tools in practice and refine them based on the experience of undertaking a review.

The pilot should demonstrate how the Framework can be practically applied and help ensure the final Framework is fit-for-purpose, scalable and capable of being applied consistently across Council.

Part 2 – Service Planning Approach

As an optional next phase, Council may choose to engage the successful provider to extend the Service Review Framework to incorporate a Service Planning Approach.

Part 2 is not guaranteed and would only proceed at Council’s discretion. It is dependent on the development of Council’s Service Catalogue, which is currently underway, and would therefore be undertaken after Part 1 has been completed.

Reverse Brief

Council is seeking a reverse brief from respondents that demonstrates their understanding of the opportunity across both Part 1 and the potential Part 2, recommends an appropriate approach and sequencing, and identifies any refinements, considerations or dependencies that Council should take into account. This should include how the proposed Framework would complement Council’s Benefits Framework and support ongoing service improvement.

Respondents should outline their proposed approach to developing and piloting the Service Review Framework and, where relevant, their proposed approach to subsequently incorporating Service Planning. Respondents are encouraged to draw on their experience in service review and service planning to propose an approach that will deliver a practical, scalable and sustainable Framework for use across Council.

publicQuestions.question:
We are preparing a proposal in response to City of Boroondara, Invitation to Supply -Service Review Framework, Contract No. 2026/164, issued 1 September 2026 (Parts A, B, C and D) and welcome the opportunity to do so. In accordance with clause 2.2 of Part B.2 -Council Requirements, we submit the following requests for clarification and further information through VendorPanel for the attention of the Project Manager.

Several of the matters below concern apparent discrepancies or omissions within the Invitation documents. We raise them in accordance with our obligation under clause 1.2(b) of Part B.2 to notify Council in writing of any discrepancy, ambiguity, error or inconsistency, so that Council has a fair opportunity to consider what corrective action, if any, is necessary. We understand that Council is under no obligation to respond, and that responses of general application may be issued to all suppliers as part of the Invitation.

Timetable and process

1.	Which cut-off date applies to requests for clarification? The VendorPanel Request Summary (Reference D) states 5:00pm, Tuesday 8 September 2026, while Item 8 of Part A.1 states 14 September 2026 as the end of the period for questions or requests for information.

2.	Please confirm the intended date for formal notification of the successful supplier. Item 8 of Part A.1 states 2 October 2026, while VendorPanel records a decision date of 29 September 2026.

3.	Does Council intend to hold a briefing session under clause 2.3 of Part B.2? Item 7 of Part A.1 has not been populated and no briefing has been advertised on VendorPanel. If a session is to be held, please advise the date, time and format.

Evaluation, response format and lodgement

4.	What weighting is applied to each of the evaluation criteria listed in Item 10 of Part A.1, and how is the demonstration of sustainable and social procurement impact weighted relative to price and to professional competence, capacity and experience?

5.	Is a page limit or word limit to be applied to the proposal? Clause 3.4(c) of Part B.2 refers to limits "where specified", but no limit is specified in the Invitation or in Part D. If a limit applies, please confirm whether it extends to supplementary material and curricula vitae.

6.	Should the seven questions posed by Council within VendorPanel be answered in VendorPanel, within Part D - The Proposal, or in both? We also seek Council's guidance on where the reverse brief required by Part A.2 should be presented, as Part D contains no corresponding field.

7.	Part D refers to the completion and return of the COMP 002 notification of risks and hazards form. That form was not included in the documents issued with the Invitation. Please provide the form, or confirm whether it is required for an engagement of this nature.

Mandatory requirements

8.	Is RapidGlobal registration applicable to this engagement? If so, please confirm at what stage of the process registration and accreditation are required.

9.	Please confirm the insurance limits required for this engagement. Clause 6.3 of Part C requires public liability cover of not less than $10,000,000 and professional indemnity cover of not less than $5,000,000, each with a principal's indemnity extension, while the insurance schedule in Part D retains placeholder values ("$XXML") and includes product liability and WorkCover fields that may not be applicable to a consultancy engagement.

Scope, pilot and Part 2

10.	Has Council established a budget envelope or Maximum Spend Amount for Part 1, and separately for the optional Part 2?

11.	Item 8 of Part A.1 records the indicative timeframe for Part 2 as "6-8". Please confirm whether this is expressed in weeks or in months.

12.	How and when will the small Council service for the Part 1.B pilot be nominated, and what indicative information can Council provide regarding its scale, budget, staffing and the maturity of its performance and financial data?

13.	What Council resourcing will be made available to the provider during the engagement, including a project sponsor, a working group or steering forum, service owner and staff availability, and access to service performance, financial, workforce and customer data, particularly during the six-week pilot?

14.	What is the current status and expected completion date of Council's Service Catalogue, and how firm is Council's present intention to proceed with Part 2?

15.	Are the nine draft Service Review Guardrails at Reference B settled, or does Council expect the successful provider to test and refine them as part of Part 1.A?

16.	Does Council have an existing service review methodology, template or completed review that the Framework must align with, build upon or replace? If the structure of the developing Service Catalogue is available, would Council make it available to inform the design of the Framework?

17.	Beyond the July 2026 Overview at Reference C, is the full Benefits Management Framework available to respondents, including benefit domains, headline benefits, the KPI and measure library, and any benefit register or reporting templates? Alignment with the Benefits Framework is an express requirement of Part A.2.

Proposed Contract (Part C)

18.	Clause 6.2 of Part B.2 provides that the successful supplier must enter into a contract on the basis of its proposal without negotiation, while Part D invites suppliers to state departures from Part C, which Council will risk assess and which "will be subject to negotiations". Please confirm how departures stated in the Part D compliance table will be treated during evaluation, and whether the statement of a departure affects a proposal's conformity.

19.	Clause 5.4 of Part C grants the Consultant a licence to use the Deliverables and associated Intellectual Property for non-commercial purposes only. Would Council consider granting the successful provider a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the general methodology and generic templates for commercial purposes, excluding all Council-specific, confidential and identifying content?

20.	The Framework is intended to provide the basis for establishing a panel of suitably qualified providers to undertake future service reviews. Please confirm whether the provider engaged to develop and pilot the Framework will be eligible to respond to that subsequent panel approach to market, or whether Council would regard that as a conflict of interest precluding participation.

21.	Clause 3.3 of Part C contemplates that "Contract retentions shall be made where applicable". Please confirm whether Council intends to apply any retention to payments under this contract and, if so, on what basis.

We would be grateful for Council's response in sufficient time to be reflected in our proposal ahead of the closing time of 5:00pm on 22 September 2026.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council thanks the supplier for its clarification questions in relation to City of Boroondara Invitation to Supply – Service Review Framework, Contract No. 2026/164. Council provides the following responses for the assistance of suppliers in preparing proposals. These responses should be read together with the Invitation documents and any addenda or clarifications issued through VendorPanel.

Timetable and process

1. Which cut-off date applies to requests for clarification?

Council confirms that the applicable cut-off date for requests for clarification is 14 September 2026, as stated in Item 8 of Part A.1 of the Invitation. Council will update or clarify VendorPanel records if required.

2. Please confirm the intended date for formal notification of the successful supplier.

The intended date for formal notification of the successful supplier is 2 October 2026, as stated in Item 8 of Part A.1. This date is indicative and may be varied by Council in accordance with the Invitation conditions.

3. Does Council intend to hold a briefing session under clause 2.3 of Part B.2?

Council does not currently intend to hold a briefing session. Suppliers should submit any clarification questions through VendorPanel by the applicable cut-off date.

Evaluation, response format and lodgement

4. What weighting is applied to each of the evaluation criteria listed in Item 10 of Part A.1?

Council has not published individual weightings for the evaluation criteria. Proposals will be assessed having regard to the criteria listed in Item 10 of Part A.1, including professional competence, capacity and experience, price, risk, mandatory requirements, sustainable and social procurement impact, and the overall value for money proposition.

5. Is a page limit or word limit to be applied to the proposal?

No specific page or word limit has been specified in the Invitation documents. Suppliers should ensure their proposal is complete, concise and directly responsive to the requirements. Supplementary material and curricula vitae may be included where relevant.

6. Should the seven questions posed by Council within VendorPanel be answered in VendorPanel, within Part D – The Proposal, or in both?

Suppliers should answer the VendorPanel questions in VendorPanel as required. The reverse brief required by Part A.2 should also be included in the supplier’s proposal submission as a clearly labelled section, either within Part D where most appropriate or as an attachment to the proposal.

7. Part D refers to the COMP 002 notification of risks and hazards form, which was not included.

The COMP 002 notification of risks and hazards form is not required for this engagement because RapidGlobal registration is not required.

Mandatory requirements

8. Is RapidGlobal registration applicable to this engagement?

No. Council confirms, following advice from Council’s OHS representative, that RapidGlobal registration is not required for this engagement.

9. Please confirm the insurance limits required for this engagement.

The required insurance limits are those stated in clause 6.3 of Part C: public liability insurance of not less than $10,000,000 for any single occurrence and professional indemnity insurance of not less than $5,000,000 for any single occurrence. Product liability and WorkCover requirements apply only where relevant to the supplier’s circumstances and the nature of the services.

Scope, pilot and Part 2

10. Has Council established a budget envelope or Maximum Spend Amount for Part 1, and separately for the optional Part 2?

Council has not disclosed a budget envelope for Part 1 or the optional Part 2. Suppliers should provide a value-for-money proposal with clear pricing for Part 1 and separate pricing for the optional Part 2.

11. Item 8 of Part A.1 records the indicative timeframe for Part 2 as “6–8”. Please confirm whether this is expressed in weeks or months.

The intended timeframe for Part 2 is 6–8 weeks, subject to the supplier’s proposed approach and Council’s decision whether to proceed.

12. How and when will the small Council service for the Part 1.B pilot be nominated?

The small Council service for the pilot will be nominated by Council in consultation with the successful supplier during project initiation. Council will provide relevant information about the nominated service at that time, including available performance, financial, workforce and customer data where relevant and available.

13. What Council resourcing will be made available to the provider during the engagement?

Council will make appropriate project governance and subject matter input available, including access to relevant Council stakeholders and data where available. The detailed governance structure, including sponsor, working group or steering arrangements, will be confirmed with the successful supplier during project initiation.

14. What is the current status and expected completion date of Council’s Service Catalogue, and how firm is Council’s present intention to proceed with Part 2?

Council’s Service Catalogue is currently under development and expected to be completed by December 2026. Part 2 is optional, not guaranteed, and will proceed only at Council’s discretion following completion of Part 1 and when the Service Catalogue is sufficiently developed to support the work.

15. Are the nine draft Service Review Guardrails settled?

The nine Service Review Guardrails are draft and should be treated as guiding principles. Council expects the successful provider to have regard to them and may test and refine their practical application through Part 1.A and the pilot.

16. Does Council have an existing service review methodology, template or completed review that the Framework must align with, build upon or replace?

Council is seeking the development of a practical, fit-for-purpose Service Review Framework and associated tools. Any existing relevant materials or examples will be made available to the successful supplier where appropriate. If available and suitable, the developing Service Catalogue structure may also be shared to inform the Framework design.

17. Beyond the July 2026 Overview at Reference C, is the full Benefits Management Framework available to respondents?

Attachment 2 provides Council’s Benefits Framework for the purposes of this Invitation. Further Benefits Framework materials, including benefit domains, measures, registers or reporting templates, may be provided to the successful supplier where available and relevant to the engagement.

Proposed Contract (Part C)

18. Please confirm how departures stated in the Part D compliance table will be treated during evaluation.

Suppliers must clearly state any departures from Part C in the relevant compliance table. Departures will be considered as part of Council’s evaluation and risk assessment. The inclusion of a departure does not automatically make a proposal non-conforming, but Council may take the nature and extent of any departure into account when assessing risk and value for money.

19. Would Council consider granting the successful provider a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the general methodology and generic templates for commercial purposes?

Council’s position is as set out in Part C of the Proposed Contract. Suppliers may identify any proposed departure or alternative wording in their compliance response. Council will consider any proposed departure as part of its evaluation and risk assessment.

20. Please confirm whether the provider engaged to develop and pilot the Framework will be eligible to respond to a subsequent panel approach to market.

Council does not intend to automatically preclude the provider engaged to develop and pilot the Framework from participating in any future panel procurement. Any participation would be subject to the requirements of the future procurement process and appropriate management of any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.

21. Please confirm whether Council intends to apply any retention to payments under this contract.

Council does not currently intend to apply a payment retention under this contract unless otherwise specified in the final contract or required in the circumstances.

Council trusts these responses assist suppliers in preparing proposals ahead of the closing time of 5:00pm on 22 September 2026.

The City of Boroondara is seeking a suitably experienced provider to work with Council to develop a Service Review Framework (Part 1), with the option to subsequently extend the Framework to incorporate a Service Planning Approach (Part 2).

Part 1 – Service Review Framework

1.	Part 1.A – Development of the Framework

The provider will develop a practical, fit-for-purpose Service Review Framework that establishes a consistent approach to planning and undertaking service reviews across Council, including the methodology, tools and supporting resources required to undertake future service reviews.

The Framework should complement Council’s Benefits Framework by supporting the identification, assessment and tracking of benefits from review recommendations, and enable insights and opportunities identified through reviews to inform ongoing service improvement.

The Framework, associated resources and intellectual property will be owned by Council and will provide the basis for establishing a panel of suitably qualified providers to undertake future service reviews on Council’s behalf.

2.	Part 1.B – Pilot of the Framework

As part of Part 1, the successful provider will be required to pilot the Service Review Framework with one small Council service. The pilot will provide an opportunity to test the Framework, methodology and tools in practice and refine them based on the experience of undertaking a review.

The pilot should demonstrate how the Framework can be practically applied and help ensure the final Framework is fit-for-purpose, scalable and capable of being applied consistently across Council.

Part 2 – Service Planning Approach

As an optional next phase, Council may choose to engage the successful provider to extend the Service Review Framework to incorporate a Service Planning Approach.

Part 2 is not guaranteed and would only proceed at Council’s discretion. It is dependent on the development of Council’s Service Catalogue, which is currently underway, and would therefore be undertaken after Part 1 has been completed.

Reverse Brief

Council is seeking a reverse brief from respondents that demonstrates their understanding of the opportunity across both Part 1 and the potential Part 2, recommends an appropriate approach and sequencing, and identifies any refinements, considerations or dependencies that Council should take into account. This should include how the proposed Framework would complement Council’s Benefits Framework and support ongoing service improvement.

Respondents should outline their proposed approach to developing and piloting the Service Review Framework and, where relevant, their proposed approach to subsequently incorporating Service Planning. Respondents are encouraged to draw on their experience in service review and service planning to propose an approach that will deliver a practical, scalable and sustainable Framework for use across Council.

title: Loxton House Refurbishment and Conservation Works
description:
Muswellbrook Shire Council (the Principal) invites suitably qualified Contractors to tender for the Loxton House Refurbishment and Conservation Works at 142–144 Bridge Street, Muswellbrook, New South Wales. Loxton House is a State Heritage listed building.

The project involves the comprehensive refurbishment of the existing three-level heritage building to facilitate its adaptive reuse as a mixed-use commercial facility comprising:

a restaurant within the Lower Ground Floor;

commercial office tenancies on the Ground Floor;

commercial office tenancy on Level 1; and

associated amenities and supporting building services.

The Works include structural remediation, roof refurbishment and associated modifications, heritage conservation works, accessibility upgrades, building services replacement, internal refurbishment and fit-out, together with associated external works.

At the time of Tender, the Development Consent required for the proposed Lower Ground Floor restaurant works has not been obtained. Accordingly, the Lower Ground Floor works identified in the Contract Documents as being subject to that Development Consent are to be priced separately as Optional Additional Works in the applicable Returnable Schedule and are excluded from the Base Lump Sum Tender Price.

The Principal may elect to incorporate all or part of the Optional Additional Works into the Contract, subject to the required statutory approval being obtained and in accordance with the Contract.

Given the heritage significance of the building and the specialised nature of the Works, the Principal seeks a Contractor with demonstrated experience in the conservation, restoration and adaptive reuse of heritage-listed buildings of comparable size and complexity.

The successful Contractor shall undertake the Works in accordance with the Contract Documents and all applicable statutory approvals while ensuring the protection and preservation of the building's heritage significance throughout the duration of the Contract.

The Contractor shall provide all labour, supervision, management, plant, equipment, materials, temporary works and all other resources necessary to deliver the Works in accordance with the Contract Documents.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon

We are very interested in pricing this project for Muswellbrook Council. We are pre-qualifed with NSW Govt with the speciality of heritage and have won a National Master Builders Award for excellence in Construction for Restoration of an Historical Building $10M, however, in our experience, 3 x weeks is not enough time to prepare the price for this project..

For projects like this, we would normally need around 5 x weeks, as 1) the subcontractors are specialist subcontractors, so there are fewer from which we can gain pricing, and 2) the scope is way more detailed than a new build, and therefore takes them longer to price it.

We feel with the current closing date, it wouldn't be enough time to provide complete pricing for Muswellbrook Council. Can you please advise whether a longer tender period is possible, which would enable us to price this project.

Thank you

title: Supply and Delivery of One Articulated Motor Grader
description:
Central Goldfields Shire Council invites tenders for the supply and delivery of one (1) new articulated diesel-powered Motor Grader for use in municipal road construction, renewal and maintenance throughout the Central Goldfields Shire municipality.

The Grader will primarily operate on unsealed rural roads and, to a lesser extent, urban streets. Typical activities include road formation, gravel re-sheeting, maintenance grading, table drain construction and cleaning, scarifying, ripping, roadside maintenance and emergency works, including fire containment line construction.

The Grader will be required to operate safely and reliably in a range of weather conditions, including prolonged operation in ambient temperatures up to 45°C.

The successful Tenderer shall supply, deliver, commission and register the Grader ready for operational use.

For detailed information see Request for Tender documents.

title: Operation and Management of Bay Pavilions Aquatic Centre, Moruya War Memorial Swimming Pool and Nar
description:
Eurobodalla Shire Council (‘Council’) is issuing this open Request for Tender (RFT) for the provision of the

following scope of work:

1. The management and operation of Bay Pavilions aquatic and fitness (gym) facilities.

2. The provision of food and beverage services for the Bay Pavilions, including the café, poolside canteen

and meeting room catering.

3. The management and operation of Moruya War Memorial Swimming Pool, Narooma Swimming Pool

and facilitation of access to other on-site facilities (meeting room and kiosk).

Council has identified three separable packages, as identified above, with Tenderers able to submit a Tender to

provide singular package(s) and/or bundle of packages. Further details on the bundles of packages are included

within the scope.

What’s important to us?

Council is looking for a suitably experienced contractor(s) to undertake the management and operation of its

aquatic facilities and associated services. The key objectives for Council are to ensure that it is achieving best

value for money from its aquatic facilities contract(s) and to ensure that more specialist and/or locally based

providers are able to submit viable tender offers. It is also a key requirement for the procurement process that

the Bay Pavilions Aquatic Centre attracts a provider that will ensure the facility retains its premier, five-star

status. Council has therefore elected to offer separable packages so that tenderers may submit for one or more

individual packages or bundles, aiming to balance simplicity and operational efficiency. The details on the

separable packages are included within the Scope.

Why should you bid?

This is an opportunity to partner with Eurobodalla Shire Council on a long-term contract (four years, with two

three-year extension options) to manage and operate a partial or full portfolio of high-profile aquatic facilities,

including the Bay Pavilions Aquatic Centre, Moruya War Memorial Swimming Pool and Narooma Swimming

Pool. The separable packaging approach enables Tenderers to bid for a single package or propose an efficient

bundled offer, creating a genuine pathway for specialist and locally based operators as well as larger providers.

The successful provider(s) will have the ability to drive service quality, customer experience and participation

outcomes for residents and visitors, with scope to propose innovations and improvements to enhance the

facility offering and grow revenue within a supportive Council partnership.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement officer,

We have the following questions. If you could please provide clarification on the queries below, it would be greatly appreciated, as this information will assist us in preparing and submitting our tender response.

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

Section 1.2 lists RFID driver sign-on with asset start inhibit as a minimum requirement. Is that capability currently wired and enabled across the existing fitted assets, or is it a capability of the installed system that has not been commissioned? If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it?

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access.

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so?

4. Removal of the existing hardware

Where a proposal involves migration to a new system, does Council require the existing telematics hardware to be removed and returned to Council, and where should the cost of that removal be shown in Schedule B2, which does not include a removal line item?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon and thank you for your questions

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

Section 1.2 lists RFID driver sign-on with asset start inhibit as a minimum requirement. Is that capability currently wired and enabled across the existing fitted assets, or is it a capability of the installed system that has not been commissioned? If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it? This system is fitted and operation on all existing units

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access. Our existing cards are HID Prox. Our existing Mix Telematics system and all other systems that utilise our employee RFID cards can use all 3 of these credential types

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so? New suppliers are not required to provision for the existing historical 12 months of data. New suppliers are required to maintain a minimum rolling 12 months historical tracking data from implementation date moving forward.

4. Removal of the existing hardware

Where a proposal involves migration to a new system, does Council require the existing telematics hardware to be removed and returned to Council, and where should the cost of that removal be shown in Schedule B2, which does not include a removal line item? For a migration proposal, the implantation plan should include removal of the existing system. The proposal should include a labour time per unit removal. This would then be applied using the rate “Labour - Repair and Rectification work” on schedule B2

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon

Item 1, Control and SCADA Scope

Reference: Technical Specification (Part 2, Appendix A) Sections 15.1.1 and 15.1.2; Site Meeting Minutes dated 20/08/2026, "SCADA and PLC".

The tender documents appear to conflict on responsibility for the control and SCADA scope:

•	The Technical Specification (Sections 15.1.1 and 15.1.2) requires the Contractor to perform all SCADA configuration, RTU and control programming, program the PLC and RTU, integrate the station into Council's SCADA system, produce a Functional Specification, and fully commission the telemetry system.

•	The Site Meeting Minutes (20/08/2026) state the Contractor supplies the unprogrammed MIRI and PLC, Council returns them programmed, and the Contractor will not program or integrate the switchboard.

Please confirm who is responsible for the control and SCADA scope, specifically the PLC and MIRI programming, SCADA integration, and the Functional Specification deliverable (Section 15.1.2).

If any of these remain the Contractor's responsibility, please advise Council's preferred SCADA integrator.

Item 2, Groundwater Level for Dewatering

Reference: Geotechnical Report (Part 2, Appendix E, GE_2510.1180) Sections 5 and 6.2.3; PPR Section 2.6; Site Meeting Minutes dated 20/08/2026, "Geotechnical Conditions and Dewatering".

The tender documents give conflicting groundwater levels:

•	The Geotechnical Report states groundwater was encountered at 8.0m in BH1, records this as the groundwater table in Table 5.1, and adopts 8.0m as the basis for its trench stability assessment in Section 6.2.3.

•	The Site Meeting Minutes (20/08/2026) state groundwater may be encountered approximately 1 to 2 metres below ground level.

The 1 to 2 metre figure does not appear in the Geotechnical Report or elsewhere in the tender documents. Given the deep excavations in the scope, this difference has a significant impact on dewatering design, methodology and price.

Please confirm the groundwater level tenderers are to adopt as the basis for pricing dewatering and excavation.

If the 1 to 2 metre level is to be adopted, please provide the supporting investigation data, confirm whether the Geotechnical Report's trench stability and excavation recommendations remain valid, and advise how dewatering is to be allowed for this condition.

Regards
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI Response – Control and SCADA Scope

The Contractor shall:

* Supply the unprogrammed MIRI and HMI to Council.

Council shall:

* Provide a programmed MIRI and HMI to the Contractor.

The Contractor shall:

* Install the programmed MIRI and HMI into the switchboard.

* Test and install the switchboard into position on site and connect all site equipment as per the design.

* Not be required to produce a Functional Specification

This above scope will alleviate the contractor from having to perform SCADA integration because the equipment will come pre-programmed.

RFI Response – Groundwater Level for Dewatering

The geotechnical investigation recorded free groundwater in BH1 at approximately 8.0 m below ground level at the time of investigation.

The reference in the Site Meeting Minutes to groundwater potentially being encountered at approximately 1-2 m below ground level, as the Liquid Limit of soil is around 44%-50%, indicates the moist soil may encounter water at shallow depth. The groundwater conditions may fluctuate due to seasonal and rainfall influences and may differ from those observed during the geotechnical investigation.

Tenderers shall make their own assessment of the information provided and allow for all dewatering, groundwater management, excavation support and temporary works necessary to undertake the Works. In accordance with the PPR, all associated costs and risks are the responsibility of the Contractor and shall be deemed included in the Contract Sum. No additional groundwater investigation data is available

publicQuestions.question:
The tender documents identify Donkey Steps as a significant access constraint but do not define construction vehicle limits. Please confirm:

Which access route(s) will be available for construction traffic?

What GVM, axle load, vehicle/trailer dimensions, operating hours and movement restrictions apply?

Can tenderers assume project-specific exemptions will be approved for quarry trucks, concrete agitators, low loaders, drilling/piling plant and large armour rock deliveries?

Are pilot/escort, convoy or wet-weather restrictions applicable?

Must tenderers allow for material transfer/staging and/or access-road maintenance, upgrading or reinstatement?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Please find answers to your questions below:

Which access route(s) will be available for construction traffic? - Only one route is available into the valley, via the Donkey Steps access road. The damaged section of Wolgan Road into the Wolgan Valley is closed to all vehicles.

What GVM, axle load, vehicle/trailer dimensions, operating hours and movement restrictions apply? - The current day-to-day limit for vehicles into the Wolgan Valley is 6t GVM, with a maximum length of 8m. However, Council will review and provide exemption to vehicles above this limit that are involved in the works. Tenderers are to include details regarding the plant proposed for the works in Schedule 4 of the tender schedules, and the perceived risks and treatments involved with utilising this plant in Schedule 12.

Can tenderers assume project-specific exemptions will be approved for quarry trucks, concrete agitators, low loaders, drilling/piling plant and large armour rock deliveries? - Yes, as per above.

Are pilot/escort, convoy or wet-weather restrictions applicable? - Council may consider temporary closure of the road to residents whilst heavy plant is traversing the Donkey Steps. Wet weather restrictions are generally not applicable. However, Council may, at its discretion, close the access road in extreme weather events.

Must tenderers allow for material transfer/staging and/or access-road maintenance, upgrading or reinstatement? - There is no mandated requirement for material staging. However, tenderers are to describe their methodology concerning logistics in their response to Schedule 4 of the tender schedules. Council will require tenderers to rectify any damage to the access road. However, general wear and tear is acceptable.

title: Penrith City Library Smart Device Application
description:
The contractor is required to deliver a comprehensive mobile library application (iOS and Android) with the following key capabilities:

• Core Features:

User account access, catalogue search across physical and digital collections, real-time item availability and location and item renewals synced with the Library Management System (LMS).

• Integration:

Seamless integration with LMS and RFID systems, with LMS-agnostic functionality. The app must connect to a wide range of existing digital platforms (e.g., Libby, BorrowBox, Freegal, Beamafilm, StoryBox, Humanitix) and support future integrations.

• Digital Access:

Ability to download and access eBooks and eAudiobooks directly within the app.

• User Experience:

Intuitive, user-friendly design that meets accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG), and allows in-library borrowing via mobile devices.

• Administration:

A staff-facing CMS for content management, plus flexible branding and content customisation.

• Events & Information:

Event booking/ticketing functionality and integration with Council website content.

• Reporting & Support:

Analytics and reporting tools, along with 24/7 technical support.

Overall, the solution should provide a fully integrated, accessible and user-centred mobile library experience with strong backend management and support.
