vendorPanelDetails.background:
Penrith City Council (Council) is a large general purpose Local Government Authority in New South Wales, with the seat of the City of Penrith located approximately 55 kilometres west of Sydney’s Central Business District at the foothills of the Blue Mountains, covering an area of 404.9 square kilometres with a population of over 212,000.

Council is seeking quotations from suitably qualified and experienced providers of smart device library applications to deliver and enhance online and remote library services for eligible library members. The solution must provide unlimited 24-hour, 7-day access to library services and collections, enabling members to conveniently access library resources, information and digital content anytime and anywhere, as further described in Attachment [4] of this RFQ – Scope of specifications.

Penrith City Library delivers information, education and recreation facilities, resources and services to residents and visitors across Penrith. Services are delivered through three branch locations, a Home Library Service, a Toy Library, a Pop-Up Library, an Anytime Library and a suite of online services.

In addition to offering books and information resources (print, media and digital), the Library aids with general and specialised information enquiries, including local history research. Services also include internet access, digital literacy support, promotional activities and a diverse range of programs and events.

Penrith City Library is committed to enhancing security, improving access to physical collections and encouraging greater engagement with its digital resources and services.

Spydus (CIVICA) as its Library Management System (LMS)

A smart device application provided by Solus, which allows customers to access online library services through a single interface

These systems are well established and integral to library operations.

The Library is now seeking Requests for Quotation (RFQs) for a smart device application that will maintain a seamless customer experience (replacing Solus application) while ensuring compatibility with existing LMS and RFID infrastructure.

publicQuestions.question:
Commencement versus go-live

Does the service commencement date of 21 December 2026 represent the required production go-live date for the replacement application, or the commencement of an implementation and transition period? If an implementation period is anticipated, what is Council's target production go-live date?

Catalogue data access

What interfaces does Council's Spydus environment make available to authorised third-party applications for catalogue search and data extraction, including any API, LCF service, MARC export, OAI-PMH or Z39.50/SRU endpoint and do these cover digital collections as well as physical holdings?

Digital content delivery model

For third-party digital content platforms subject to provider DRM restrictions, does Council require digital content to be rendered natively within the application, or is authenticated access with handoff to the provider's platform acceptable?

RFID and self-check integration

Can Council provide details of the FE Technologies RFID and security environment at its branches, including gate models, the RFID tag standard and data encoding in use (for example ISO 15693 / ISO 28560)?
publicQuestions.answer:
Commencement versus go-live

Yes, the service commencement date of 21 December 2026 represents the required production go-live date for the replacement application.

Catalogue data access

We have paid for access to the Spydus API and third-party APIs are also permitted. Spydus still has SIP2 connection available, though it is not a preferred option. Spydus has the ability to export MARC records, we have OAI-PMH set up to harvest records into TROVE and I think Sharon’s team use Z39.50 to import MARC records for cataloguing purposes. We certainly use eContent harvesting to import catalogue records from Libby, BorrowBox and Indyreads. Spydus pricing has increased, so it is possible that we won’t be extending our eContent harvesting to cover any of our other providers.

Digital content delivery model

Our eContent providers handle the DRM requirements. We authenticate patron logins via Spydus API or a SIP2 process and loans are then accessed via the provider’s platform.

RFID and self-check integration

We have Designer Clear 2 Column security gates at all branches. Penrith and St Marys have Return Shelves and all branches have V5 Loan Stations. We are currently running with SIP2 integration but are in the process of converting to LCF via API. Tag data encoding format is ISO 28560 (ISO 15693 also available), frequency is 13.56 MHZ and the encoded elements are the Primary identifier and Content Parameter only.

Backed by the Economic Development Act 2012, EDQ has unique planning and approval powers and a mandate to create private sector investment opportunities by de-risking and unlocking land for redevelopment. Geotechnical certification and/or any other information to determine the quality and suitability of fill to the satisfaction of EDQ’s project engineers must be provided if requested.

Suppliers must have all necessary permits and approvals for the source of the fill material and for haulage to EDQ’s site.

title: Bamaga Football Oval Lighting
description:
The Northern Peninsular Area Council is looking to upgrade the lighting at the Bamaga Football Oval to Queensland Rugby League Seniors standards (200 Lux).

There are existing lighting poles at the ground, but it would be preferable to replace these with poles that can be lowered for maintenance. NPARC will consider multiple options from suppliers to achieve the 200 Lux standard for the lowest lifecycle cost.

Automatic and remote control of the lights is desirable.

The lights must be installed prior to the start of the 2027 football season - say 1 June 2027. Remembering that the wet season makes travel and construction works difficult from December to April each year.

This is a design and construct project. NPARC would be willing to evaluate a number of proposals from each supplier.

title: ITT2558 - Eddie De Vere Building - Internal Refurbishments
description:
The Eddie De Vere Building is one of Sunshine Coast Council’s office facilities and currently accommodates approximately 200 SCC staff across the ground floor, mezzanine, Level 1, and Level 2. Level 3 has been deactivated for an extended period due to water infiltration issues.

Stage 1 of this project involves a comprehensive review and repair of the roof membrane and external glazing across the building. These works are close to being completed and are a prerequisite to enabling the safe re-occupation of Level 3.

The works will entail demolition of existing partitions, internal doors and windows and floor coverings to levels Mezzanine, First, Second and Third. The removal and retention of or demolition of existing furniture to Levels Mezzanine and One. Installation of new partitions, internal doors and windows, floor coverings to Levels One and Three. Reconfiguration of security, electrical and data, mechanical and smoke detection on levels Mezzanine, First Second and Third. A new kitchen and PWD toilet to level Three and the re alignment of the ceiling grid to Level One and Three. Co-ordination of services and the placement of principal supplied items (Loose Furniture) will be required.

These works as documented include Architectural, Mechanical and Electrical and Hydraulic works.

Note: The Principal wishes work to commence on site prior to the 2026 Christmas Break

Council is seeking to award this lump sum Contract to a single Contractor required to provide all materials, plant and labour, to perform all necessary operations to ensure the complete and proper completion of the works associated with this Contract.

title: Tender 1226248 - Design & Construction of Molong Water Security Pipeline Project
description:
Cabonne Council has been investigating options to:

- Improve water security and drought resilience;

- Ensure the availability of supply from the Molong Creek Dam to meet current and future town water demand; and

- Provide Molong, Cumnock and Yeoval with secure water supply to support the development of these centres.

The gravity main from Molong Creek Dam to the Molong Water Treatment Plant is a key component of the Molong Water Supply System. Sections of this pipeline were constructed in 1920 with various sections then added or replaced over time. This gravity pipeline is critical for the continued operation and security of the Molong WSS. Upgrades to this pipeline are proposed to improve the transfer capacity and operation including:

- Replacing a 9,300m section of the Molong Creek Dam to Molong Water Filtration Plant gravity raw water pipeline from a point known as Peter's Pit to a point known as Gabb's Pit. This section of the existing pipeline includes single and parallel pipes of various sizes and lengths; and

- Interconnections of the new pipeline to the existing pipeline/pipelines at Peter's Pit and Gabb's Pit; and

- Reconnection of existing customer services to the new pipeline; and

- Decommissioning of the existing pipeline/pipelines.

The area is home to the site of Australia's first gold rush and is famous for ballooning, food and wine, agriculture and mining.

title: TEN/3083 - Disposal of Old Show Grounds Site, 45 Burrum Street, Bundaberg West
description:
Council is inviting offers from suitably qualified Respondents to purchase and develop the balance of the property located at 45 Burrum Street, Bundaberg West, via tender.

Property

Council is the owner of the freehold parcel, described as Lot 4 on SP270831 known as 45 Burrum Street, Bundaberg West, Queensland, Australia, 4670 (‘Property’). The site is bounded by Civic Avenue, Burrum Street, Pyefinch Boulevard and Saltwater Creek, and has an area of 7.0895 hectares, in its current form.

The Property is the remains of the former Bundaberg Showgrounds, and currently has minimal physical infrastructure on the site, but does include the remaining Bailey Gate which is a Local Heritage Place in the Bundaberg Regional Council Planning Scheme 2015. The northern portion of the site is currently occupied by the Campervan and Motorhome Club of Australia (‘CMCA’) under a lease agreement to operate a caravan park for their members. This lease area roughly aligns with the area impacted by Council's adopted Flood Hazard Area and will be retained by Council. Services are available to the site, although depending on the nature of any future development, may require some extension, relocation or upgrade.

Adjoining the Property is the recently constructed Bundaberg Aquatic Centre, a major regional facility intended to host significant sporting and community events. The Property is also located adjacent to Council's Multiplex precinct and is consequently, a strategically important location to support regional events, community infrastructure and the accommodation needs generated by these adjoining facilities and activities.

Council’s objective is to facilitate the sale and timely development of the Property in a manner that delivers economic, social and community benefits, while supporting the strategic vision for the precinct and addressing identified accommodation and housing needs within the Bundaberg Region.

title: Rosny and Richmond Tennis Courts - Resurface
description:
Council invites Tenders to undertake works as specified in these Tender Documents for the following works at the Rosny and Richmond Tennis Courts sites.

Rosny Tennis Club, Courts 1&2 – 18 Bastick Street, Rosny

-	Supply of all materials and consumables for the resurfacing of courts 1 and 2

-	Supply of portable toilet and amenities for the duration of the works

-	Install new sand filled synthetic grass surface

-	Removal and appropriate disposal of all waste materials, including old court surface

Richmond Tennis Club, Courts 1&2 – 2 Victoria Street, Richmond

-	Supply of all materials and consumables for the guttering and resurfacing

-	Supply of portable toilet and amenities for the duration of the works

-	Remove of the existing Courts 1&2 synthetic grass surface

-	Install guttering as per sketch and LGAT drawing

-	Install new sand filled synthetic grass surface

-	Removal and appropriate disposal of all waste materials, including the court surface

Full details are provided in Schedule 1 of the specimen copy of the Contract appearing in Part 4 of this Invitation. Tenderers are to contact Council’s nominated contact officer named on the cover page if additional information is required to submit the Tender.

BACKGROUND

The Rosny Tennis Courts 1 and 2 were installed over 30 years ago with synthetic grass laid over an asphalt surface. The grass surface has reached end of life and is in poor condition. Council is also progressing a separate tender to repair the retaining wall adjacent to the courts as well as install new “like for like” perimeter fencing around Courts 1 and 2. These works are planned to be completed prior to any resurfacing works commencing. All site works must be completed prior to 31 Dec 2026.

The Richmond Tennis Courts were installed over 30 years ago and the existing synthetic surface is in poor condition due to its age. Additionally, stormwater ponds at the southern corner of the court. Council is undertaking works external to the court to improve the stormwater drainage, however the court requires a dish drain to be installed to better direct flow to the Council drain. The existing chain link fence and lighting will remain undisturbed during the works.

PRE-TENDER SITE MEETING

For clarification of the Works, a pre-Tender site meeting is scheduled for Rosny Tennis Club (18 Bastick Street) at 11:30am on Thursday 17 September on-site.

A further pre-Tender site meeting is then scheduled for Richmond Tennis Club (2 Victoria Street) at 12:30pm on Thursday 17 September on-site.

Attendance at this meeting is not mandatory; however, this will be the only opportunity to physically explore the site with the Superintendent in attendance.

Those intending to attend this meeting are requested to inform the contact person nominated on the front cover of this Tender Document prior to the meeting and arrange own transportation between sites.

CLOSE OF TENDER

3pm, Tuesday 06 October 2026

LATE TENDERS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

title: TEN16730 - Mount Morgan Cemetery Extension
description:
Mount Morgan Cemetery is a heritage listed cemetery located at East Street, Mount Morgan, within the Rockhampton Region, Queensland. Established in 1886, the cemetery has served the Mount Morgan community for the majority of the town’s history and was entered on the Queensland Heritage Register on 21 October 1992. The site contains numerous memorials, structures, and landscape elements of historical, cultural, social, and aesthetic significance, including the Linda Memorial and a rare Chinese ceremonial burner.

The land formerly identified as Lot 3614 has undergone a boundary realignment along East Street South and has been consolidated with Lot 184 to form a single allotment. More recently, the consolidated site has been rezoned to Community to support and facilitate the proposed extension of the Mount Morgan Cemetery. This technical specification has been prepared to support the delivery of civil works associated with the cemetery extension, which is intended to provide additional burial capacity and associated infrastructure while maintaining the historic character, heritage values, layout and cultural significance of the existing cemetery.

Mount Morgan Cemetery is a heritage listed cemetery located at East Street, Mount Morgan, within the Rockhampton Region, Queensland. Established in 1886, the cemetery has served the Mount Morgan community for the majority of the town’s history and was entered on the Queensland Heritage Register on 21 October 1992. The site contains numerous memorials, structures, and landscape elements of historical, cultural, social, and aesthetic significance, including the Linda Memorial and a rare Chinese ceremonial burner.

The land formerly identified as Lot 3614 has undergone a boundary realignment along East Street South and has been consolidated with Lot 184 to form a single allotment. More recently, the consolidated site has been rezoned to Community to support and facilitate the proposed extension of the Mount Morgan Cemetery. title: WBHHS130454 - Expression of Interest (EOI) - Rural GP Services
description:
Wide Bay Hospital and Health Service (WBHHS) currently supports rural GP services through commissioned private general practices across the North Burnett and rural Bundaberg regions. These services are delivered through a mix of third-party management arrangements and WBHHS-employed Medical Practitioners operating under Private Practice agreements.

WBHHS is seeking responses from interested parties who wish to collaborate in co-designing and delivering sustainable, integrated and community-aligned rural primary care models for the future.

This EOI invites high-level concepts that strengthen rural GP access and build resilient service pathways in thin markets.

WBHHS is particularly interested in solutions that deliver:

a) patient-centred care

b) integrated service pathways

c) sustainable and resilient rural GP models

d) strong alignment with community needs and expectations.

WBHHS welcomes innovative concepts and enhanced service offerings. WBHHS is open to exploring new care models and commercial arrangements, including a range of subsidies and supports that may incentivise market participation and enable a genuine transition toward sustainable operating models over time.

This EOI aims to:

a) explore market interest in partnering to co-design sustainable rural GP service models

b) identify innovative, integrated, patient-centred and community-aligned approaches

c) understand workforce, training, operational and high-level commercial/support requirements, including subsidy and incentive needs

d) assess how WBHHS’s current investment could be better structured to support future sustainability

e) support transition toward future-ready operating models.

** Please note an Industry briefing meeting will take place at 11:00AM on Tuesday, 08 September 2026. This briefing will be held online via Microsoft Teams. To confirm attendance please email stacey@pisa.au and the industry briefing meeting details will be shared. **

Please refer to the supplied documentation for further information.

title: MICC Water Main Works Duchess Road, Lagoon Creek and Northridge Road
description:

(2) Completion of the remaining open-trench Duchess Road Water Main Extension works along Duchess Road, Price Road, Croft Road and McIntosh Road; and

Separable Portion 2 – Duchess Road Open-Trench Water Main Extension: completion of the remaining unconstructed water main works shown on the Part 3 concept plans, excluding sections already installed by MICC.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi

Can you provide further information for the following?

1. Is design and RPEQ certification required for separable portions 1 and 3 or only required for SP 2 as per the tender price schedule?

2. Can you please provide the long section drawing for the HDD crossing at Lagoon creek to understand the depths and levels?

3. For Separable portion 2 can you please provide a drawing clarifying the length of pipe installed by the council and length of pipe to be installed by the contractor?

4. Can you please provide the cross section of the trench for the watermain indicating the type of bedding and backfill/trenchfill material required?

5. Can you please provide a cross section of the road pavement to understand the pavement restoration works required post construction of the watermain?

6. Are property service connections required? If yes, please provide details of the number of connections, type of pipe material. Please further confirm if the new connections are required from main to meter or just connect the existing property service to the new watermain?

7. For the road crossing please confirm the size and material of the enveloper pipe.
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 31/Aug/2026 11:29 AM)

PLease find the answers to your questions.

1. Design and RPEQ certification – Separable Portions 1, 2 and 3

or the HDD works and Northridge Road works, where the Contractor is required to develop the final alignment, bore profile, methodology or other design elements, those elements are to be designed and certified by an appropriately qualified RPEQ.

For conventional pipeline construction, the Contractor may adopt applicable MICC, WSAA and recognised standard drawings/details for trenching, bedding, embedment, backfill, thrust restraint and associated pipeline construction without preparing a separate project-specific RPEQ design, unless site conditions require departure from those standards.

RPEQ-certified As-Constructed documentation will be required for all Separable Portions, confirming that the completed works have been constructed in accordance with the approved design, applicable standards and any approved design changes.

Where the Contractor proposes an alternative methodology or departure from the nominated standards or drawings, the Contractor shall provide RPEQ design and certification for that alternative prior to construction.

2. Lagoon Creek HDD long section

A detailed long section has not presently been issued.

The HDD Contractor is required to develop and confirm the proposed bore alignment, entry/exit locations and bore profile as part of its methodology. The current scope nominates an approximate minimum cover of 1.5 m beneath the Lagoon Creek bed, subject to the Contractor's proposed bore profile and Council approval.

Council will review whether any additional survey/design information is available and issue this to all tenderers if applicable.

3. SP2 – Council-installed versus Contractor-installed pipework

Council will provide an annotated plan identifying:

existing/Council-installed water main;

limits of Contractor-installed pipework;

This will be issued to all tenderers as an addendum/clarification.

4. Water main trench section – bedding and backfill

Unless specifically detailed otherwise within the Contract documents, conventional water main construction shall be undertaken in accordance with the applicable SEQ Water Supply Code and associated standard drawings, including requirements for trenching, bedding, embedment, backfill, compaction, fittings, thrust restraint and other typical water main construction details.

Where site conditions or the proposed construction methodology require a departure from the applicable SEQ standard details, the Contractor shall develop the alternative detail and provide RPEQ-certified design documentation for MICC review prior to construction.

5. Road pavement restoration

As per item 4 response.

6. Property service connections

No property service connections are included within the Contractor’s scope of works.

The Contractor is required to install the new water main infrastructure only, in accordance with the issued scope, drawings and applicable standards.

All property service connections, including connections from the new water main to existing property services/meters, will be undertaken separately by Mount Isa City Council at a later stage.

Tenderers are therefore not to include any allowance for property service connections within their tendered price.

7. Road crossing carrier/enveloper pipe

The size, material and configuration of any required enveloper/casing pipe are to be determined through the Contractor’s RPEQ-certified design for the Duchess Road crossing.

Tenderers shall consider the requirements applicable to the crossing of the TMR-controlled road corridor, including applicable TMR standards, clearances, loading requirements and approval conditions.

The Contractor’s design shall nominate the proposed carrier pipe, enveloper/casing (where required), bore diameter, depth/cover, entry and exit locations and associated construction methodology.

The final design is to be RPEQ certified and submitted to MICC for review prior to construction. Any required TMR approval shall be obtained prior to commencement of the affected works.

title: DLGWV2026-0351 Design and Construction of the Mapoon New Treated Water Reservoir Project
description:
The Department of Local Government, Water and Volunteers (DLGWV) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the Design and Construction of the Mapoon New Treated Water Reservoir Project. The works includes geotechnical investigations and surveying to support the design of a new treated water reservoir and future upgrades to the Water Treatment Plant (WTP). The scope of works also includes the demolition and removal of the existing steel structure, relocation of two sheds for repurposing by Council, remediation of the existing 1.2 ML concrete reservoir, and the design, supply, delivery, construction, installation, testing, commissioning, and performance testing of a new treated water reservoir.

Tenderers are to refer to Invitation to Offer documents for further details.

A non-mandatory Industry Briefing will be held at 10:30am AEST, 16 September 2026. Tenderers are required to register their attendance by sending an email to Procurement@dlgwv.qld.gov.au to the attention of Florine Vega-Hughes, by 14 September 2026, detailing the name/s and contact details of attendees (email address and mobile number).

publicQuestions.question:
I have a few questions relating to the electrical scope for the Mackay Turf Club tender.

What size are the proposed portable heated spas? What electrical specs are available to allow for correct sizing of cabling and outlets for connection.

On the proposed Jockey facilities electrical plans there are 2 x meter panels shown on the western wall. Is this correct or will one be sufficient?

Are the existing meter panels being reused? If not are there any specs on what meter board/s is required to be installed? What size board/s?

Do the exhaust fans require ducting/venting? Are there specific exhaust fans that need to be used?

What size, brand are the ceiling fans?

What wattage flood light is required?

Are the 2 x 20A 3 phase outlets on the eastern wall remaining in place and do they need to be replaced during the upgrades? If so is a specific brand required?

Is the solar system getting upgraded during works and will a solar contractor need to be included as part of the electrical scope?

Is the comms cabinet located on the eastern wall of the jockey facilities? Does the data cabling in the jockey facility go back to that point?

Are there any specifications for sizing of sub main cabling for the proposed Horse Drug Testing Building?

Will the sub main cabling for the Horse Drug Testing Facility nee to be installed underground or overhead?
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see below answers (A) to your questions (Q):

Q1: What size are the proposed portable heated spas? What electrical specs are available to allow for correct sizing of cabling and outlets for connection.

A1: As per designs supplied min 2m x 1.5m capable of heating to 40 degrees. Cabling to be sized according to selected unit.

Q2: On the proposed Jockey facilities electrical plans there are 2 x meter panels shown on the western wall. Is this correct or will one be sufficient?

A2: As per supplied design, meter panels to be relocated from existing position to proposed positions. Vendors may choose after suitable consultation with electrical specialist to replace western wall with a singular meter board.

Q3: Are the existing meter panels being reused? If not are there any specs on what meter board/s is required to be installed? What size board/s?

A3: As above and supplied design.

Q4: Do the exhaust fans require ducting/venting? Are there specific exhaust fans that need to be used?

A4: Standard exhaust fans vented to roof cavity.

Q5: What size, brand are the ceiling fans?

A5: Standard builders range fans 122cm.

Q6: What wattage flood light is required?

A6: Min 100w (LED version).

Q7: Are the 2 x 20A 3 phase outlets on the eastern wall remaining in place and do they need to be replaced during the upgrades? If so, is a specific brand required?

A7: To remain unless unserviceable upon inspection by electrician at which point replacement only. This is power supply for SKY TV Trucks.

Q8: Is the solar system getting upgraded during works and will a solar contractor need to be included as part of the electrical scope?

A8: As per supplied design and Scope, existing solar to be removed and reinstalled in position as required for new roof. Nil upgrades unless required under electrical code.

Q9: Is the comms cabinet located on the eastern wall of the jockey facilities? Does the data cabling in the jockey facility go back to that point?

A9: Correct

Q10: Are there any specifications for sizing of sub main cabling for the proposed Horse Drug Testing Building?

A10: To be sized according to proposed load.

Q11: Will the sub main cabling for the Horse Drug Testing Facility need to be installed underground or overhead?

A11: Preferably underground.

description:
Gwydir Shire Council invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced individuals, businesses, or organisations for the management and operation of the Bingara Riverside Caravan Park and/or the Warialda Caravan Park for the next 3 years.

Applicants may submit a tender for either facility individually or for both facilities.

Please see the attached document for further information.

Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Gwydir Shire is in the centre of the ‘Fossickers Way’, a route which offers the traveller a relaxing alternative to the New England or Newell Highways. The Shire encompasses a diverse landscape that is both picturesque and productive and is approximately 560 km north of Sydney, 160 km north of Tamworth along the Fossickers Way and 85 km north-west of Inverell. The shire is 9,122 square kilometres in size and is situated north of Tamworth Regional Council and continues almost to the Queensland border.

The southern boundary of the shire is the Nandewar Range where the Gwydir and Namoi Valleys meet. The Horton Valley and Cobbadah District are home to some Australia’s most highly regarded beef cattle studs. These enterprising farmers use the latest artificial breeding and agronomic technology to produce beef of exceptional quality. Meat Sheep and merinos that grow high quality wool are also grazed in this area.

The Gwydir River enters the Gwydir Shire where it spills from the Copeton Dam and meanders in a westerly direction through the towns of Bingara and Gravesend. The Gwydir valley is well know for irrigated and dry land cropping as well as livestock production. In addition to the traditional crops of wheat, barley, oats and sorghum, there are olive groves, pecan nut plantations and freshwater fish farms in the Gravesend district.

Heading northwest from the timbered surrounds of the town of Warialda and the close-knit community of Coolatai, the countryside opens into an undulating vista of basalt farmland. This part of the Shire which include the villages of Crooble, Croppa Creek and North Star, is known as the ‘Golden Triangle’. Farmers using advanced farming techniques, such as minimum tillage and satellite guidance systems, produce a variety of high yielding crops such as wheat, barley sorghum, maize, chick peas, canola and cotton to name just a few. This area also has several cattle feed lots which supply grain fed beef to the Australian domestic market and export markets throughout the world.

Both Warialda and Bingara have Hospitals, Aged Care Hostels, Medical Centres, Caravan Parks, Swimming Pools, Pre-schools, Libraries, Tourist Information Centres, and a Mobile Pre-school based at North Star. Warialda is the centre for the Council’s Technical Services functions. Bingara is the centre for the Administrative functions. The two centres are being linked through the use of sophisticated communications equipment to ensure that the amalgamations primary objective is achieved which is to save the existing employment numbers within each of the main urban centres of Warialda and Bingara.

Request for Tender GWY_2027_T03 – Management of Bingara Riverside Caravan Park and Warialda Caravan Park

we respectfully request clarification of the following matters.

1. Warialda manager accommodation

As there is no caretaker residence at Warialda, will Council provide the appointed manager or management couple with a dedicated powered caravan site free of charge?

If so, please confirm whether the following will be included:

•	Electricity, water and sewerage services

•	Internet access

•	Permission to establish a suitable annex or temporary outdoor living area

•	An appropriate storage area for the managers’ personal and operational equipment

2. Grounds-maintenance equipment

Please provide details of the Council-owned grounds-maintenance equipment that will be available at each park, including any ride-on mowers, push mowers, brushcutters, blowers, trailers and other tools.

Please also confirm whether Council or the contractor will be responsible for:

•	Fuel and consumables

•	Routine servicing

•	Mechanical repairs

•	Replacement of unserviceable equipment

3. Definition of minor maintenance

The RFT identifies minor maintenance as a contractor responsibility, while major maintenance and capital works remain Council responsibilities.

Could Council please provide a definition or financial threshold for minor maintenance, including:

•	Any maximum cost per individual repair

•	Any maximum annual expenditure per park

•	Whether the contractor is responsible for both labour and materials

•	Whether electrical, plumbing and other licensed trade work will be arranged and paid for by Council

An agreed threshold would assist both parties in avoiding uncertainty during the contract.

4. Cleaning, linen and guest consumables

The RFT confirms that the contractor will purchase cleaning chemicals. Please clarify responsibility for:

•	Cabin linen, towels and bedding

•	Linen laundering or commercial laundry services

•	Replacement of worn or damaged linen

•	Guest toiletries and cabin supplies

•	Toilet paper, paper towels, hand soap and sanitary products

•	Rubbish bags and other cleaning consumables

5. Waste collection and pest control

Please confirm whether Council will arrange and pay for:

•	General waste and recycling collection

•	Disposal or tipping charges

•	Sanitary-bin services

•	Routine pest-control services

•	Any specialist pest treatment required for cabins, amenities or other Council buildings

6. Collection of park income

As all park income and accommodation takings will be retained by Council, please confirm responsibility for:

•	Provision of EFTPOS terminals

•	EFTPOS merchant and transaction fees

•	Online payment gateway charges

•	Refunds and chargebacks

•	Cash banking and associated bank fees

•	Losses resulting from fraudulent transactions or chargebacks, where the contractor has followed Council procedures

7. Office and information technology equipment

Although Council will provide the GuestPoint booking platform, please confirm whether Council will also provide and maintain the necessary operating equipment at each park, including:

•	Computers and monitors

•	Printers and scanners

•	EFTPOS and point-of-sale equipment

•	Internet service at the Warialda office

•	Technical support for Council-provided systems

•	Printer ink, paper and other system consumables

8. Crown-land licence

Please advise whether the licence to operate the facilities on Council-managed Crown land will involve any:

•	Licence fees

•	Security deposits or bonds

•	Additional insurance requirements

•	Inspections or compliance costs payable by the contractor

9. Management-fee payments and annual adjustment

Please confirm whether the annual management fee will be paid monthly, quarterly or under another arrangement, and whether payments will be made in advance or arrears.

The RFT allows respondents to specify an alternative to the same annual fee applying across all three years. Does Council have a preferred CPI index or other adjustment method for respondents proposing annual indexation?

10. Historical operating information

To assist with staffing and operational planning, could Council provide the following information for each park for the previous three financial years, where available:

•	Cabin occupancy and number of cabin departures or changeovers

•	Powered and unpowered site occupancy

•	Seasonal occupancy patterns

•	Number and nature of after-hours callouts

•	Annual expenditure on minor maintenance

•	Waste, laundry and pest-control arrangements

•	An inventory of Council-owned plant and equipment available for contractor use

Robert Hardy

Council provides the following clarification.

1. Warialda Manager Accommodation

As there is no caretaker residence at Warialda Caravan Park, Council will provide the successful contractor with one dedicated powered caravan site at no charge for the duration of the management agreement.

The site will include access to electricity, water and sewerage services where available to the site.

A suitable annex or temporary outdoor living area may be established, subject to compliance with normal park requirements and prior approval from Council.

Council is currently reviewing the availability of suitable storage space at the Warialda Caravan Park and will confirm any arrangements with the successful contractor.

Internet access required for the operation of the park office and Council systems will be provided by Council.

## 2. Grounds-Maintenance Equipment

Council-owned grounds-maintenance equipment currently located at each caravan park will remain available for use by the successful contractor in undertaking the required grounds-maintenance duties.

Currently there is no dedicated equipment available for the park however this will be discussed and plant equipment provided with the successful contractor.

The contractor will have access to fuel but will be responsible for ordinary consumables associated with day-to-day use of the equipment.

Council will remain responsible for routine servicing, major mechanical repairs and replacement of Council-owned equipment that becomes unserviceable through normal wear and tear.

The contractor will be responsible for damage caused through misuse, negligence or use outside the intended purpose of the equipment.

## 3. Definition of Minor Maintenance

For the purposes of the management agreement, minor maintenance generally refers to routine, low-cost maintenance and minor repairs that can reasonably be undertaken as part of normal day-to-day park operations.

Council proposes that minor maintenance will include repairs or materials up to a maximum value of $250 per individual repair or maintenance item, with an annual expenditure limit of $2,500 per park, unless otherwise approved by Council.

The contractor will be responsible for the labour and ordinary materials associated with minor maintenance within these limits.

Electrical, plumbing and other work requiring a licensed trade will generally be arranged and paid for by Council. Major repairs, replacement of significant assets and capital works will remain Council's responsibility.

Any maintenance issue exceeding the above limits should be reported to Council for assessment and approval prior to work being undertaken, except where immediate action is required to make an area safe.

## 4. Cleaning, Linen and Guest Consumables

The contractor will be responsible for the routine cleaning of cabins, amenities and other park facilities, including the purchase of cleaning chemicals and normal cleaning consumables.

The contractor will also be responsible for routine guest and facility consumables including:

* toilet paper;

* paper towel;

* hand soap;

* rubbish bags;

* guest toiletries and similar low-value cabin supplies; and

* routine laundering of cabin linen and towels.

Council will retain ownership of cabin linen, towels and bedding and will be responsible for replacement where items have reached the end of their useful life through normal wear and tear.

## 5. Waste Collection and Pest Control

Council will arrange and pay for the existing general waste and recycling collection services associated with each caravan park, including normal disposal and tipping charges.

Council will also meet the cost of existing sanitary-bin services.

The contractor will be responsible for routine cleanliness and basic pest-prevention measures associated with normal park operations.

Council will arrange and pay for specialist pest-control treatment where required for Council-owned cabins, amenities or other buildings, including significant infestations or treatment requiring a licensed contractor.

## 6. Collection of Park Income

All accommodation income and park takings will be retained by Council.

Council will provide the EFTPOS and payment-processing facilities required to operate the parks and will be responsible for associated merchant fees and online payment gateway charges.

Council will also be responsible for legitimate refunds and chargebacks processed in accordance with Council procedures.

The contractor will be responsible for the appropriate handling, reconciliation and banking of cash and other takings in accordance with Council procedures.

Where the contractor has complied with Council procedures and has not acted negligently, losses arising from fraudulent transactions or chargebacks will remain Council's responsibility.

## 7. Office and Information Technology Equipment

Council will provide the core equipment reasonably required to operate Council's booking, payment and administrative systems at each park.

This will include, where required:

* computers and monitors;

* printers/scanners;

* EFTPOS and point-of-sale equipment;

* internet access for the park office;

* access to GuestPoint; and

* technical support for Council-provided systems and equipment.

Council will also provide routine printer ink, paper and similar consumables required for Council administrative functions.

The contractor will be responsible for any additional equipment or systems they elect to use for their own business purposes.

## 8. Crown-Land Licence

Both caravan parks are located on Council-managed Crown land.

Council does not currently propose to charge the successful contractor a separate Crown-land licence fee, security deposit or bond associated with the licence required to operate the facility.

The contractor will, however, be required to comply with all conditions of the applicable Crown-land licence and maintain the insurance requirements specified in the RFT.

Any compliance costs arising directly from the contractor's activities or failure to comply with licence conditions will remain the contractor's responsibility.

## 9. Management-Fee Payments and Annual Adjustment

The agreed management fee will be paid monthly in arrears, subject to receipt of a valid tax invoice and satisfactory performance of the required services.

Respondents may propose a fixed annual management fee for the three-year term or nominate an alternative annual adjustment mechanism as part of their tender.

Council does not mandate a particular indexation method. Where indexation is proposed, respondents should clearly identify the method and index to be used. Council would consider a recognised measure such as the Consumer Price Index as an acceptable approach.

Any proposed annual adjustment will form part of the tender evaluation and, if accepted, will be incorporated into the final agreement.

## 10. Historical Operating Information

Council is unable to provide historical operating information as we have had no booking software implemented until recently.

title: Atherton Hospital Upgrades - Design and Construct Building Contractor
description:
The State of Queensland through Queensland Health, Health Infrastructure Queensland (HIQ) on behalf of Cairns and Hinterland Hospital and Health Service (CHHHS) is undertaking the procurement of a suitably qualified Design and Construct Building Contractor to deliver the Atherton Hospital Upgrades (the Project).

The Atherton Hospital Upgrade Program comprises a series of interconnected infrastructure projects designed to improve clinical service delivery, enhance patient outcomes, address infrastructure deficiencies, and support the future healthcare needs of the Atherton community and surrounding Tablelands region.

The Atherton Hospital Upgrade Program consists of the following projects:

•	25 Bed Ward Refurbishment;

•	Oncology Refurbishment;

•	New Morgue Building;

•	High Dependency Unit (HDU); and

•	Pathology Refurbishment.

The program includes the refurbishment and expansion of key clinical facilities within Atherton Hospital, together with the construction of new supporting infrastructure to improve service capability, operational efficiency, patient safety, and staff wellbeing. The projects have been developed in response to increasing service demand, ageing infrastructure, evolving healthcare models, and the need to provide contemporary, fit-for-purpose healthcare environments that support high-quality patient care.

Tenderers are invited to attend a site inspection on Wednesday 26 August 2026. Attendance at this meeting is non-mandatory but highly desirable.

publicQuestions.question: Compliance Criterion 2.7 states that the insurance requirements for this Request for Tender are stipulated in the General Conditions of Contract. publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon,

1. Please see NTT001 relating to the General Conditions of Contract.

2 & 3. The Cyber Insurance preferred limit is $20 million but the respondents are able to submit their current limit for Cyber Insurance and state the risk factors around the lower limit. Cyber Insurance is a mandatory requirement. Respondents are also able to state that they will increase the limit to the $20 million if they are successful in the contract.

4. Professional Indemnity is not required for this contract.

Kind Regards,

Isaac Regional Council

title: Tier 1 Office Accommodation Design & Construct - Expression of Interest
description:
Design & Construct

Seqwater is undertaking a two-phase procurement process to identify and engage suitably qualified Principal Contractors for the delivery of office accommodation buildings at the Mt Crosby and North Pine Water Treatment Plant sites. The successful contractor(s) will be responsible for progressing the projects from 60% design completion through to Practical Completion.

Phase 1: Expression of Interest (EOI)

Through this EOI process, Seqwater is seeking to identify and shortlist Principal Contractors for participation in the subsequent Request for Tender (RFT) phase. Proponents may submit a response for either site or both sites, as outlined in the Statement of Requirements. Respondents will not be disadvantaged based on their selection of one or both sites.

Phase 2: Request for Tender (RFT)

The RFT will be issued to the shortlisted contractors identified through the EOI process. The RFT is anticipated to commence in mid-October 2026, with contract award expected in late March to early April 2027.

publicQuestions.question:
1.	The RFQ indicates that Council intends to establish a panel of prequalified DTAS Consultants for an initial three-year term, with an option to extend for a further year. However, the proposed contract appears to be a standalone services agreement and does not expressly reference a panel arrangement or project-specific engagements. Further, Annexure Part A, which contains key commercial and contractual particulars, has not been completed.

Could Council please confirm whether the agreement is intended to establish the overarching terms and conditions for panel participation, with individual projects to be awarded under separate RFQs, work orders, or similar engagement documents? If so, will a completed Annexure Part A be provided for each project-specific engagement, setting out the applicable commercial terms, risk allocation, and project requirements?

2.	Could Council please clarify the intended number of prequalified consultants to be appointed under each workstream of the DTAS Panel Arrangement?

3.	Could Council confirm whether geotechnical investigation services are intended to be procured under the Specialist Services workstream, or whether such services are expected to be provided as subcontracted services supporting engagements within the other workstreams?

4.	Could TCC clarify how the Case Study Pricing (Response Schedule 3) and Case Study Methodology (Schedule 4) submissions will be used for the panel bid evaluation purpose?
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes. The DTAS Contract is intended to establish the overarching terms and conditions governing the panel arrangement. Appointment to the panel does not guarantee any minimum volume of work.

Individual projects and assignments will generally be procured from the panel through project-specific engagement mechanisms, which may include Requests for Quotation (RFQs), work orders, purchase orders, or other project-specific instructions issued by Council. Each engagement will define the applicable scope, deliverables, pricing, timeframes and any project-specific requirements relevant to that commission.

Council does not intend to nominate a fixed number of consultants to be appointed under each workstream. The number of appointments will be determined following evaluation of submissions and Council's assessment of capability, capacity, value for money, geographic coverage and operational requirements.

Council reserves the right to appoint multiple suppliers to any workstream and may appoint different numbers of suppliers across the various workstreams.

Geotechnical investigation services are identified within the Scope of Work as a specialist technical service that may be required to support DTAS projects. These services may be provided directly by consultants with the relevant capability or through suitably qualified specialist subconsultants, depending on the requirements of the specific engagement. Geotechnical investigations are identified as one of the technical professional services that may apply across the DTAS workstreams

Accordingly, respondents may nominate capability under the Specialist Services workstream where geotechnical services form part of their core service offering, or may propose appropriately qualified subconsultants to support delivery under other nominated workstreams.

The Case Study Methodology and Case Study Pricing submissions are included to provide Council with a consistent basis for evaluating respondents' technical capability, delivery approach, resourcing methodology and value for money.

The Case Study Methodology will be used to assess the respondent's understanding of the requirements, proposed approach, project controls, risk management processes and ability to successfully deliver representative DTAS services within the nominated workstream.

Good morning, Team,

Before submitting for the panel, we wanted to clarify whether a consultant awarded the design contract would also be eligible to tender for the subsequent construction contract if they have construction capabilities as well. Specifically, would being involved in the design phase exclude us from the construction tender process or place us at a competitive disadvantage?

If the successful design consultant is not permitted to tender for the construction package, could you please advise whether a separate design and construct or related services tender is expected to be released?

Thank you!
publicQuestions.answer:
Suppliers appointed to this panel for design services will be eligible to tender for any future works packages that may be released under separate procurement processes, subject to meeting the requirements of the relevant tender at that time.

To ensure a fair and competitive procurement process, all design services undertaken under this panel must be developed on an agnostic basis. Design documentation, specifications, reports, drawings and associated information must not be prepared in a manner that favours, advantages or disadvantages any particular supplier, contractor, product, methodology or delivery approach. All information developed during the design phase will be made available to prospective tenderers for the subsequent works package to ensure all participants have equal access to the information required to prepare their submissions.

Accordingly, involvement in the design phase will not preclude a supplier from participating in a future construction or works tender. However, suppliers must ensure that all design outputs remain impartial and suitable for an open and competitive procurement process.

At this stage, any future construction or works package is expected to be released as a separate procurement process, subject to Council approvals and project requirements. Any such opportunity will be advertised in accordance with Council's procurement requirements

Are you only wanting full design houses and we need to subbie through them? or if you are wanting specialist suppliers do you want us to price the portions of the work we can complete in the examples? please advise.
publicQuestions.answer:
Suppliers will be required to nominate the specific workstreams, service categories, or portions of work for which they can demonstrate the necessary capability, capacity, experience and resources to perform. Appointment to the panel will only apply to those workstreams or service categories identified in the supplier's submission and assessed by Council as meeting the required standards.

Suppliers are not required to offer all workstreams or service categories under the panel arrangement. Proponents are encouraged to nominate only those areas where they have the expertise, available resources and capacity to deliver the services in accordance with the contract requirements.

Council may appoint suppliers across multiple workstreams, and the composition of suppliers within each workstream may vary depending on the capabilities and capacities demonstrated through the tender process. Future work allocations or invitations to quote will generally be limited to suppliers approved for the relevant workstream or service category.

title: 2026.069 - Development of a Laratinga Trails and Boardwalks Masterplan
description:
Laratinga Wetland is a highly popular and well used community and environmental asset with over 8,000 people accessing the wetland via its trails each week. To ensure access to the wetland is safe, equitable and maximises community and environmental outcomes, a review of the trails and boardwalk infrastructure is proposed. To help with this task, the Mount Barker District Council (“Council”) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified consultant to review existing Laratinga wetland trails and boardwalk layout and infrastructure, associated access issues and opportunities and to develop a master plan to inform future development upgrades and renewals.

The existing Laratinga trail network and boardwalks was constructed when the wetlands were first developed in the late 1990’s. The boardwalks are now at end of life, with one section having been closed to public access for over 2 years. The boardwalks consist of 1 main section that crosses basin 3 and includes a viewing platform and 2 smaller sections in basins 1 and 2 (see Attachment 1 - Laratinga Wetlands Trails map).

Council has conducted a condition audit and commissioned a quote to replace the existing structures as they were originally designed but upgraded to comply with current standards. The quote to do this came in at close to $2M which prompted the need for a cost benefit analysis to ensure community funds are invested appropriately and community benefit is maximised.

In addition, the water regime in the wetland is changing to an ephemeral system, as part of a major upgrade to the Mount Barker Wastewater Treatment Plant. As well as broader management implications, this change will require lagoons to be dewatered for a period which would enable work on boardwalks and other infrastructure to occur, and before the ephemeral system is implemented. This is currently scheduled for 2028.

Therefore, before proceeding, it has been determined that a review of the layout and design of the whole Laratinga trail network and user needs should occur to ensure whatever is implemented is fit for purpose and identifies appropriate community use, access and safety as well as achieving environmental objectives, including the needs of birdlife and other fauna.

Any queries are to be submitted via VendorPanel and a response will be provided in the same manner.

Townsville City Council is currently working towards a cultural engagement process, and does not currently have an established process. Council's primary consideration will be artistic quality, audience experience, feasibility, and alignment with the event theme, rather than whether a proposed work is a premiere presentation.

title: 2026.039 - Treasury Consultant
description:
Mount Barker District Council (“Council”) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced treasury advisory consultant to provide both:

•	Strategic treasury advisory services, and

•	Ongoing monthly treasury and debt management advice in relation to Council’s treasury function.

This engagement will support Council (as the parent entity) while recognising that treasury positions are managed across:

•	The municipal operations of Council; and

•	The Council’s Wastewater Subsidiary (GMB Water), in accordance with Council’s Treasury Management Policy (Attachment 1).

Council is one of the fastest growing municipalities in South Australia and is experiencing significant infrastructure demand driven by population growth.

Council is forecasting a peak debt position of approximately $255 million by 2028/29, largely associated with the development of a wastewater network that is being delivered ahead of development demand.

Council currently operates under an approved borrowing facility from the Local Government Finance Authority (LGFA) of up to $255 million and manages its treasury activities in accordance with its Treasury Management Policy.

Council manages its treasury activities holistically, while also recognising that the treasury positions of the Municipal operations and the Wastewater Subsidiary are managed as distinct but interrelated portfolios in accordance with its Treasury Management Policy.

Given the scale, complexity, and forward profile of borrowings, Council is seeking external expert advice to:

•	Optimise its treasury management approach

•	Manage financial risks (particularly interest rate risk)

•	Ensure alignment with long-term financial sustainability objectives

•	Test current reliance on LGFA funding and explore alternative market options

•	Strengthen both strategic treasury planning and ongoing treasury decision-making

Engagement will be for a three (3) year term with the Strategy Development to be completed within six (6) weeks of Contract commencement.

All queries are to be submitted via VendorPanel and a response will be provided in the same manner.

Council manages its treasury activities holistically, while also recognising that the treasury positions of the Municipal operations and the Wastewater Subsidiary are managed as distinct but interrelated portfolios in accordance with its Treasury Management Policy.

Given the scale, complexity, and forward profile of borrowings, Council is seeking external expert advice to:

•	Optimise its treasury management approach

•	Manage financial risks (particularly interest rate risk)

•	Ensure alignment with long-term financial sustainability objectives

•	Test current reliance on LGFA funding and explore alternative market options

•	Strengthen both strategic treasury planning and ongoing treasury decision-making

Engagement will be for a three (3) year term with the Strategy Development to be completed within six (6) weeks of Contract commencement.

All queries are to be submitted via VendorPanel and a response will be provided in the same manner.

title: Construction of Extensions and Studios - Capital Housing Program 2
description:
The Scope is described in the document(s) attached to or provided with this Request for Tender and identified as:

Scope of Works (Construct Only)

The Contractor shall undertake building approvals and complete the construction of Eight (8) new residential dwellings at the following locations as follows;

Current Addresses	Lot Number	Proposed Housing Type

- 5 Major Close	Lot 350 SP270846	2 Bedroom Studio

- 48 Workshop	Lot 48 SP265165	2 Bedroom Studio

- 37 Back Beach Road	Lot 356 SP270846	2 Bedroom Studio

- 39B Back Beach Road	Lot 357 SP265165	2 Bedroom Studio

- 16 Gribble Street	Lot 12 SP265165	2 Bedroom Extension

- 6 Major Close	Lot 346 SP270846	2 Bedroom Extension

- 98 Workshop Road	Lot 197 SP265165	2 Bedroom Extension

- 41 Back Beach Road	Lot 343 SP265165	2 Bedroom Extension

The Works include, but are not limited to, all labour, materials, plant, equipment, design, approvals and activities necessary to deliver a fully operational, compliant and complete housing development fit for purpose and ready for handover and occupation.

Reference Documents

2 Bedroom Studio Designs

o Lot 350 (5) Major Cl – Preliminary Issue C

o Lot 48 (48) Workshop Rd – Preliminary Issue C

o Lot 356 (37) Back Beach Rd – Preliminary Issue C

o Lot 357 (39B) Back Beach Rd – Preliminary Issue D

2 Bedroom Extension Designs

o Lot 12 (16) Gribble St – Preliminary Issue E

o Lot 346 (6) Major Cl – Preliminary Issue E

o Lot 197 (98) Workshop Rd – Preliminary Issue A

o Lot 343 (41) Back Beach Rd – Preliminary Issue C

.

Key Requirements

• The Contractor shall ensure the Works comply with all applicable legislation, codes, standards and authority requirements.

• The Works shall be delivered as a complete and functional development, notwithstanding any omissions or discrepancies in the reference documentation.

• A mandatory Indigenous Employment and Business Participation (IEBP) Plan shall be submitted with the Tender. Failure to submit an IEBP may result in the Tender being deemed non-conforming.

Building Approval

• Contractor must obtain relevant building approvals for each property for this work.

Site Establishment & Civil Works

• Site establishment, access, temporary services and controls

• Clearing, grubbing, demolition if required and site preparation.

• Bulk earthworks, cut and fill, trimming and compaction incl. testing if applicable

• Set out of all works in accordance with approved design and issued FFLs

• Stormwater drainage, overland flow management and lawful discharge

Residential Construction

• Construction of eight dwellings in accordance with the designs provided

• All works to be in accordance with Remote Housing Standards (RHS) or as otherwise nominated

• Complete construction of each dwelling including all structural, architectural and building elements necessary to achieve a fully functional and compliant dwelling

• Supply and installation of all fixtures, fittings and appliances

• Kitchens, bathrooms and laundries including joinery

Services & Utilities

• All hydraulic services including water, sewer and drainage

• Electrical reticulation, metering, switchboards and internal installations

• Communications and data provisions as typically required

• Coordination and connection to mains

External & Ancillary Works

• Driveways, pathways, hardstand areas and access ways

• Fencing, gates and boundary treatments

• Landscaping, reinstatement and making good of all disturbed areas

• Installation of external fixtures including T-Bar clotheslines, external sink and bins

Testing, Commissioning & Handover

• Testing and commissioning of all services and systems

• Rectification of defects and completion of outstanding works

• Provision of as-constructed documentation, manuals and warranties

• Final certification and approvals for occupancy

• Handover of a complete, operational and compliant development

Contractor Obligations

• The Contractor shall verify all site conditions, dimensions, levels and service locations prior to commencing Works.

• The Contractor shall be deemed to have allowed for all conditions that may reasonably be anticipated from available information and site inspection.

• No claim will be accepted for matters arising from failure to adequately investigate site conditions or coordinate the Works.

• The Contractor is responsible for all coordination, interfaces and integration of the Works, whether expressly stated or reasonably inferred.

Project Specification

• Design and Construction Standards for Remote Housing – August 2025

• National Construction Code (NCC)

Additional Council Specifications

Minimum specs in addition to the Remote Housing requirements; - 6mm FC sheets be nominated for soffit and patio ceiling

• Hinged doors for bedroom cupboards and linen cupboards be nominated in lieu of sliding doors

• Ensure correct rates tiles for kitchen floor area, laundry floor area, toilet floor area and bathrooms

• Exhaust fans to bathrooms, toilets and 1 in kitchen NOT directly over the stove. Exhaust fans to be 250-300mm low maintenance type. Ducted to external soffits per RHG

• Fixed ridge vents to roof where possible

• Door hold back stops to be fixed to top of all doors - Adoored 75mm white cushion clip door stop or similar

• 32mm s/s grab rails to be used as towel rails fit as many towel rails to bathrooms as reasonably possible.

• Rheem Solar HL 300ltr 3.6kw for Solar Hot Water System.

The Contractor shall comply with the current edition of the National Construction Code (NCC), all applicable Australian Standards (AS/NZS), and all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.

It shall be the Contractor’s responsibility to identify and comply with all standards applicable to the Works, whether they are specifically listed in this document.

Good Morning,

Please see below queries:

Are we pricing for the gold or platinum level in the Design and Construction Standards for Remote Housing?

The houses are designed for Gold Standard minimum and will be built accordingly.

Hardieflex 6mm FC relates to Soffits

Axon cladding is to be allowed for external wall linings.

title: Design, Build and Implementation of the AFFIRMS Reporting System
description: AFAC is seeking a suitably qualified supplier to support the design and implementation of the Australasian Fire Fatality and Injury Reporting and Monitoring System (AFFIRMS). AFFIRMS is a national evidence and research utilisation initiative aimed at improving the consistency, quality and accessibility of fire fatality and injury data across Australia and New Zealand. The successful supplier will work with AFAC member agencies to review existing data sources and methodologies, develop a sustainable reporting framework, support data governance arrangements, and establish processes that enable meaningful analysis and reporting. While technology may form part of the solution, this is primarily a research, data and evidence-based project rather than a standalone software development procurement. Services may be delivered remotely, with project commencement anticipated in late 2026.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
340 Albert St
East Melbourne, Victoria 3002
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Australasian Fire and Emergency Service Authorities Council Ltd (AFAC) is the National Council for fire and emergency services in Australia and New Zealand, creating synergies across the emergency management sector.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Tuesday 08 September 2026 10:00 PM (AUS Eastern Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
AFAC is leading the development of the Australasian Fire Fatality and Injury Reporting and Monitoring System (AFFIRMS), a collaborative initiative involving fire and emergency service agencies across Australia and New Zealand.

A feasibility study has already been completed, identifying the need for a consistent, sustainable approach to collecting, analysing and reporting fire fatality and injury data. The project is intended to improve the evidence base available to support prevention, policy, research and operational decision-making across the sector. AFFIRMS is intended to establish a sustainable national approach to fire fatality and injury reporting, rather than develop a complex new technology platform.

The successful supplier will be expected to work with a range of jurisdictional stakeholders to build on existing project work, including outcomes from the feasibility study, stakeholder engagement activities and project governance arrangements. Experience in applied research, data governance, evaluation, evidence utilisation, public sector collaboration and multi-stakeholder projects will be highly regarded.

This Request is primarily seeking expertise in research, data governance, analysis and evidence utilisation. While technology may support the proposed approach, AFAC is not seeking a standalone software development or large-scale technology implementation project. Any proposed tools or platforms should be proportionate to the project objectives and capable of integrating with existing organisational processes and data sources where appropriate.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Desired Outcomes

AFAC is seeking a supplier that can help establish a sustainable, nationally consistent approach to collecting, analysing and reporting fire fatality and injury data across Australia and New Zealand.

The successful proposal should demonstrate how it will:

Improve the consistency, quality and comparability of fire fatality and injury data across participating jurisdictions.

Support the development of practical governance arrangements, data standards and reporting processes that can be maintained over time.

Enable meaningful analysis and evidence generation to inform prevention, policy, research and operational decision-making.

Deliver recommendations that are practical, achievable and suitable for implementation across multiple agencies and jurisdictions.

Build stakeholder understanding, capability and ownership of the project outcomes.

Produce clear documentation and knowledge transfer materials to support long-term sustainability.

Highly Regarded

The following capabilities will be viewed favourably:

Experience working with government, emergency management, public safety, health or research sectors.

Expertise in data governance, evidence utilisation, program evaluation, applied research or national reporting frameworks.

Demonstrated experience facilitating collaboration across multiple organisations and stakeholders.

Understanding of injury surveillance, mortality reporting or other public sector data collections.

Ability to recommend proportionate technology or data management approaches that support, rather than drive, project outcomes.

Success Measures

Proposals will be assessed on their ability to:

Deliver practical and implementable outcomes.

Demonstrate a strong understanding of the project's strategic objectives.

Engage effectively with stakeholders.

Support long-term sustainability and sector adoption.

Provide value for money.

title: Palm Island Walking Trails & Tourism Activation Project - Design & Construct
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced Design & Construct (D&C) Contractor to undertake the design and construction of the Palm Island Walking Trails & Tourism Activation Project.

The Project comprises the delivery of the walking trails, Cultural Welcome Precinct, eco accommodation / tourism accommodation base and associated tourism-supporting infrastructure described in Part B – Specification, including all investigations, surveys, assessments, design, approvals, construction, testing, commissioning, documentation and handover required to deliver the Works.

The procurement is an implementation procurement based on the Project outcomes and recommendations identified in Part B. Tenderers are required to demonstrate the capability, capacity and methodology necessary to deliver the Works within Palm Island's remote-island, cultural, environmental and logistical context and achieve Practical Completion by 31 December 2027.

Suitably qualified Tenderers with proven capability, capacity, and sound financial and technical background to deliver the Specification outlined in this Invitation to Tender are invited to participate in this Invitation to Tender process.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01 Geotechnical Investigation Report

Our review of the tender documentation has not identified a geotechnical investigation report for the site. No information has been provided regarding the depth to rock, the nature and strength of the in situ subgrade material, groundwater levels, or subgrade CBR values.

Request: Could the Council please issue the geotechnical investigation report for the site, including borehole logs, groundwater observations and laboratory results. If no such report exists, could the Council please confirm this in writing and advise the basis on which the extent of rock and unsuitable material will be assessed and valued.

RFI-02 Electronic Design Files (CAD)

The Contract Drawings have been issued in PDF format only. Accurate quantification of earthworks cut and fill volumes, pavement areas and kerb lengths requires the underlying design data.

Request: Could the Council please provide the design files in an editable electronic format, specifically the drawings in DWG or DXF format, and the existing and design surface models in an equivalent format.

RFI-03 Extension of Tender Closing Date

The scope comprises a substantial number of separately priced trade packages, including bulk earthworks, drainage, quarry supply, concrete, asphalt, public lighting civil works and traffic management. Requests for quotation have been issued to our subcontractors and suppliers, a number of whom have advised that they require additional time to complete their pricing and to arrange site inspections.

We further note that should the geotechnical report and electronic design files sought above be issued, it will require adequate time to review that information and incorporate it into the pricing.

Request: We respectfully request that the Council grant an extension of time of two weeks to the tender closing date, from 2:00pm on Wednesday 9 September 2026 to 2:00pm on Wednesday 23 September 2026, with the supplier query cut-off extended accordingly.

RFI-04 Powercor Electrical Works Interface

The electrical service civil works require a contractor endorsed under the Victorian Electricity Distribution Network, with the service pits supplied by Powercor and the lighting installation undertaken by Powercor. Powercor works are identified as an Excluded Authority under the Annexure.

Request: Could the Council please confirm the anticipated Powercor lead times and the expected sequence of Powercor attendance relative to the construction programme, the arrangements and notice period for collection of the service pits, and confirm that any delay attributable to Powercor will be dealt with as an extension of time under the Contract.

RFI-05 Traffic Management Responsibilities

The Technical Specification apportions traffic management responsibilities between the Contractor and the Council.

Request: Could the Council please confirm whether full or partial road closures and portable traffic signals will be permitted, and whether any restriction applies to lane closures or during peak periods.

RFI-06 Site Access, Compound and Stockpile Area

The documentation refers to a temporary stockpile area in the vicinity of Liberator Drive.

Request: Could the Council please confirm the location, extent, permitted duration of use and any conditions attaching to the stockpile area, and nominate the area available to the Contractor for the site compound.
publicQuestions.answer: See Addendum released

publicQuestions.question: In regard to item 4.03 of schedule 3, if there is a shortfall in the volume of material that is salvageable and reusable (from item 2.02) and class 4 material is to be imported, how will the additional material be paid for?

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-07 Ring Road South End - Current Closure and Rail Works Completion

The southern end of Ring Road is presently closed due to rail works. We have not been able to identify any reference to this closure, its anticipated duration, or any interface with the ongoing works within the tender documentation issued to date.

Certainty as to the status and duration of that closure is fundamental to the preparation of a Traffic Management Plan and a realistic construction programme.

Request: Could the Council please advise:

(a) When are the rail works due to finish, and when will the southern end of Ring Road reopen to traffic?

(b) Should tenderers assume the southern end of Ring Road is open or closed at commencement in February 2027 and for the duration of the contract?

It is noted that as per Council's Addendum 1, RFI-05 response rules out full closure and requires business access at all times. If the southern end of Ring Road remains closed, the traffic management and detour options left to satisfy that response are materially reduced, so tenderers need its status confirmed to price on a common basis.
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI-07 Ring Road South End – Current Closure and Rail Works Completion

(a)	Rail works are anticipated to be completed in late December 2026 or early January 2027. The southern end of Ring Road at the railway crossing shall remain closed to traffic and will not be reopened.

(b)	The southern end of Ring Road is permanently closed at the level crossing and shall not be available for access or use by the Contractor, the public, or adjoining businesses at any time during the Contract period.

publicQuestions.question: RFI-08 Electrical Works: Addendum 1 confirms Powercor will install the lighting and cable. Could Council confirm that Powercor also supplies the poles, luminaires and cable, or advise which Schedule 1C item is to carry their supply?
publicQuestions.answer: Powercor will supply and install the poles, luminaires and cable.

title: Expression of Interest - Mount Peter Sewer Rising Main
description:
The purpose of this EOI is to engage with industry prior to commencing the formal procurement process to better understand market capability, capacity, appetite and potential risks associated with the delivery of the Mount Peter Sewer Rising Main project.

The EOI will seek feedback on the proposed scope, delivery approach, packaging options, procurement strategy, risk allocation and social procurement requirements to ensure the project is structured in a manner that maximises competition, encourages innovation and delivers value for money. Information obtained through the EOI will be used to inform and refine the procurement strategy and tender documentation prior to release to market in FY27.
