vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Economic Development Queensland (EDQ) is the Queensland Government’s land use planning and property development agency. We embrace partnerships across government, industry and the community to deliver new residential communities, urban precincts and industrial ecosystems.

Backed by the Economic Development Act 2012, EDQ has unique planning and approval powers and a mandate to create private sector investment opportunities by de-risking and unlocking land for redevelopment. EDQ has planned and facilitated the delivery of some of the largest residential developments in Queensland, as well as some of the state’s most iconic urban renewal projects. We set benchmarks for the property industry through innovations and we’re creating jobs of the future in regional Queensland by unlocking land to promote priority industries, including clean energy and large-scale manufacturing.

We measure our success by the value we create in economic, social and environmental impacts. Over the last decade we have generated more than $3.7 billion in private sector investment and facilitated over $1 billion in trunk infrastructure for Queensland. EDQ focuses on achieving commercial outcomes for the state while delivering on government priorities.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Mount Peter Priority Development Area (PDA) was declared on 30 July 2025 and the Mount Peter PDA Interim Land Use Plan is now in effect.

The PDA covers approximately 2,650ha of land in the Southern Growth Corridor in the Cairns Regional Local Government Area. The area is bounded by the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area to the west, the Bruce Highway to the east and extends from the existing community of Edmonton in the north to Mackey Creek in the south.

The Mount Peter PDA was declared at the request of the Cairns Regional Council to provide a streamlined planning framework that accommodates the future housing needs of the Cairns region. The area is recognised as a future growth area in the Far North Queensland (FNQ) Regional Plan.

The Cairns South State Development Area (SDA) was declared in November 2018 as a special economic zone for regionally significant industrial development to support the long-term needs of the economy and create jobs in the Cairns region.

On 21 February 2020, the Cairns South SDA was varied to include an additional 303 hectares of land around the Mulgrave Mill to support the Mulgrave Mill’s future diversification plans, including industrial development opportunities that value-add to the sugar refining process.

The SDA is now a total of 1159 hectares over two separate areas at Wrights Creek and Gordonvale. The funding and building of infrastructure is key to facilitating development within PDA and SDA locations.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Diamantina consists of two main towns Birdsville and Bedourie, with a third town of Betoota.

Bedourie is located 1,600km west of Brisbane, while Birdsville is 200km south of Bedourie and 1,200km from Adelaide.

Our towns have four aircraft services per week on the Brisbane- Mount Isa Circuit. REX (Regional Express) provides this service.

Despite it's size, Birdsville is a well-known destination for many Australian and International visitors. The town hosts one horse race meeting a year, when over 6,000 people swell the town population. It is the start of the famous Birdsville Track, which originally was used as a stock route for moving cattle from Queensland to Southern markets.

Bedourie is the Shire's administration centre. The last ten years has seen its population more than double to 140 people. The town boasts many new amenities including an aquatic centre, hot artesian spa and a community hall. Visitor numbers have increased to over 120,000 per year.

The Shire's wealth lies within its cattle industry, tourism and natural environment. Located within Queensland's Channel Country, bordering South Australia and the Northern Territory, this area is renown for producing prime quality beef. The natural irrigation from the Diamantina and Georgina River Systems is also assisting with developing an organic cattle industry.

We are fortunate that National Parks comprise 25% of our shire's area. The Simpson Desert, Diamantina National Park, (just been named in the top ten National Parks in Australia) and Astrebla National Park all offer unique scenery and wildlife for visitors to experience.

Visit the Diamantina Shire for a unique outback experience.

publicQuestions.question:
We have a question regarding how FRV expects tenderers to price individual equipment items in Annexure A Part E - FRV Approved Equipment List, Items to Supply, Price Listing Response Template.

The template asks for a single unit price per item (inclusive of delivery, installation, commissioning and off-site rubbish removal) for Metro and Regional, across Years 1–5. In practice, freight cost varies significantly depending on:

Whether the item is delivered as a standalone order or as part of a larger multi-item "fitout" order to the same site (freight cost per unit drops substantially when items are consolidated); and

The specific postcode within Victoria the item is delivered to, given the size of the "Regional" category and the range of freight cost across it.

To be clear on what we're asking: should freight be priced on the assumption the item is sent individually, or on the assumption it's sent as part of a larger multi-item fitout order - and separately, how should the unit price account for the postcode it's delivered to, given "Regional" covers a wide range of freight costs across Victoria?

We want to make sure our pricing is genuinely comparable to other tenderers' and reflects realistic costs, rather than either overstating (if we price for worst-case standalone regional delivery) or understating (if we assume fitout-scale consolidation and metro-adjacent postcodes that may not always apply.
publicQuestions.answer:
Freight is to be priced on the assumption the item is sent individually.

This reflects the expectation of the ordering.

Thank you for your question.
